question: Q-0332cb0a65
statement: LEMMA B (unit-clause pinning = contraction, restricted form without auxiliary variables). Let the instance be c_i=(a_i,b_i), i in [m], and fix a unit constraint u with a_u = e_j, b_u = c (x_j = c). Let M be the binary matroid on {v_i : i != u} plus e, and let M/U be the contraction by U = v_u. Substituting x_j = c gives the system c'_i = (a'_i, b'_i) on n-1 variables, with a'_i = a_i restricted to coordinates != j and b'_i = b_i + a_{ij} c. Then the MUS clutter of the substituted system equals the port of M/U at e (as subsets of [m] minus u). Proof: phi(a,b) = (a restricted to coordinates != j, b + a_j c) is GF(2)-linear with kernel span{U}, since phi(e_j,c)=0 and phi(a,b)=0 forces a=t e_j, b=t c. Hence r_{M/U}(X) = r(X cup U) - r(U) = rank of phi(X), so M/U is the binary matroid of phi(v_i) plus phi(e) = e'. Lemma A applied to the substituted system finishes the proof. Hence the MUS clutter of the restriction x_j=c is the port of a minor (a contraction) of the original matroid, so port-preservation holds for unit-clause gadgets without auxiliary variables.

question: Q-0332cb0a65
statement: LEMMA C (private-auxiliary gadgets, affine GF(2) case). Setting: original system with constraints c_i=(a_i,b_i), i in [m], H_i = {x in GF(2)^n : a_i.x=b_i}. For each i take a gadget E_i = a finite set of affine equations over (x, z_i), where z_i are auxiliaries PRIVATE to i (disjoint across i), such that proj_x sol(E_i) = H_i. Gadget system G = disjoint union of E_i, each equation owned by i. Claims: (i) G consistent iff original consistent; more generally for any owner set P, G|_P consistent iff original restricted to P consistent. (ii) For any S in G, let S_i = S cap E_i and P_i = proj_x sol(S_i). Then S is consistent iff no S_i is internally inconsistent and the intersection of the P_i is nonempty (private aux => lifts are independent). (iii) If a_i != 0 or b_i = 0 then P_i in {H_i, whole space, empty}, since an affine subspace containing a hyperplane is the hyperplane or everything. Internal inconsistency of S_i forces E_i inconsistent, i.e. a_i=0, b_i=1. (iv) Pushforward: if S is an MUS of G and no S_i is internally inconsistent, the owner set Q={i: P_i = H_i} is an original MUS. Proof: Q is inconsistent since the intersection of H_i over Q is empty. If Q' is a proper inconsistent subset of Q, pick j in Q minus Q'; deleting S_j makes the remaining intersection a subset of the intersection over Q', hence empty, so S is not minimal. Also owners with P_i = whole contribute no equations to an MUS, so S = union of S_j over j in Q. (v) Every original MUS M is realized: for each j in M choose a minimal T_j in E_j with proj = H_j; then union T_j is an MUS of G with owner set M. Scope: all gadget auxiliaries private to one constraint, affine (GF(2)-linear) gadgets only. Shared auxiliaries across constraints are NOT covered; G0001 stays open for that case. Lemma C does not claim anything about general Post-lattice languages.

question: Q-0332cb0a65
statement: LEMMA R (repaired owner pushforward and realization for PRIVATE gadgets, arbitrary finite relations, scope limited to hypothesis R). Setting: constraints i in [m] with H_i a subset of X (x-domain); gadget E_i = finite set of relations over (x, z_i), z_i private to i, with pi(E_i) = H_i, where pi = projection to x. Consistent subsets T of E_i have pi(T) a subset of X. HYPOTHESIS R_i: every consistent T subset of E_i has pi(T) in {H_i, X}. Claim (a): if S is a minimal inconsistent subset of G = union of E_i and no S_i is internally inconsistent, then Q = {i : pi(S_i) = H_i} is an original MUS and S = union of S_j over j in Q. Claim (b): for every original MUS M there is a G-MUS with owner set M. Proof of (a): pi(S_i) contains H_i since S_i is a subset of E_i; by R_i, pi(S_i) is H_i or X. Private auxiliaries are disjoint, so a set is consistent iff the intersection of the owner projections is nonempty, hence the intersection over owners equals the intersection over Q of H_i. S inconsistent gives empty intersection over Q, so Q is nonempty and inconsistent. Owners outside Q have projection X and can be dropped without losing inconsistency, so minimality gives S = union over Q of S_j. For j in Q and e in S_j: S minus e is consistent, its owner-j projection is nonempty (else S minus e is internally inconsistent, contradicting minimality), so it is H_j or X by R_j. If it were H_j, the intersection would be the intersection over Q of H_i, which is empty, contradicting consistency. So it is X, giving intersection over Q minus j of H_i nonempty. Every proper subset of Q lies in some Q minus j, and consistency is monotone, so Q is minimal. Proof of (b): for j in M choose T_j minimal among subsets of E_j with pi(T_j) = H_j (H_j nonempty, so such T_j exists). Let S = union of T_j. Its owner projections are H_j, so S is inconsistent. For e in T_j, T_j minus e has nonempty projection set containing H_j and not equal to H_j by minimality, so it is X by R_j; then S minus e is consistent exactly when the intersection over M minus j of H_i is nonempty, which holds by minimality of M. So S is a G-MUS with owner set M. Remark (checked by hand): if H_i is a hyperplane of GF(2)^n (a single affine equation, the affine case), R_i holds automatically, since the only affine subspaces containing a hyperplane are the hyperplane and the whole space. This recovers S0003 (iii) for affine gadgets. Non-affine R fails on the H = {1} gadget example of cm-c792ee2f14a14a34. Scope: private auxiliaries; relations satisfying R for every constraint; does NOT claim R holds for the gadgets a Post-lattice pp-definition produces. Gap left open: which target relations admit R-gadgets (equivalently H_i is a coatom of the lattice of sub-projections of consistent subsets of E_i).

question: Q-0332cb0a65
statement: LEMMA R-suff (sufficient condition for hypothesis R_i of S0009). Setting: finite X (x-domain) and Z; relations are subsets of X x Z, with pi the projection to X. Let E = {E_1,...,E_k}, k >= 1, with H = pi(intersection of all E_i) nonempty. CONDITION COND: for k >= 2 and every j, pi(intersection of E_i over i != j) = X. Claim: under COND, every nonempty T subset of E with intersection of T nonempty has pi(intersection of T) in {H, X}, i.e. hypothesis R holds for E. Proof: if T = E, the projection is H by definition. If T is a proper nonempty subset, pick j with E_j not in T. Then T is contained in E minus {E_j}, so intersection of T contains intersection of (E minus {E_j}) as sets of points. Projection is monotone, and the smaller intersection projects onto X by COND, so pi(intersection of T) = X. For k = 1 the only nonempty T is E. QED. Corollary: LEMMA R (S0009) applies to every private gadget family satisfying COND. Scope: COND is sufficient, not necessary (cond_fails_but_R_holds = 624 in the host record). It says nothing about which Post-lattice pp-gadgets satisfy COND, and it does not touch shared auxiliaries (G0001 stays open).

question: Q-0332cb0a65
statement: LEMMA C' (repair of S0003; affine GF(2) gadgets, private auxiliaries, every single constraint consistent i.e. H_i nonempty, so H_i is X or a hyperplane). Setup: E_i affine over (x, z_i), z_i private, proj_x sol(E_i) = H_i. Claim (a): every subset S_i of E_i has P_i = proj_x sol(S_i) in {H_i, X}. Proof: E_i is consistent (H_i nonempty), and any subset of a consistent affine system is consistent, so P_i is a nonempty affine subspace; it contains H_i because fewer equations give a superset of solutions; an affine subspace containing a hyperplane is that hyperplane or X (dimension count); if H_i = X the claim is trivial. Claim (b): for any S in G, S is consistent iff the intersection of the P_i is nonempty (private auxiliaries let each z_i be chosen independently given x). Claim (c): if S is a minimal inconsistent subset of G, then Q = {i : P_i = H_i} is an original MUS and S = union of S_j over j in Q. Proof: the intersection over Q of H_i is empty; owners with P_i = X can be dropped without losing inconsistency, so minimality forces S = union over Q of S_j; if a proper subset Q' of Q were inconsistent, dropping some j in Q minus Q' from S would leave an inconsistent set, contradicting minimality. Claim (d): every original MUS M of the affine system is realized as the owner set of a G-MUS (step (b) of S0009, now with R automatic). Scope: all H_i nonempty (no constraint equal to 0=1). The case with a constraint 0=1 is excluded; there the original MUS is that singleton and is handled separately. Lemma C' does not cover shared auxiliaries, so G0001 stays open. Relation to S0003: the counterexample in cm-43211365d84f4ae3 uses H_2 = empty, which this lemma excludes.

question: Q-0332cb0a65
statement: Decoupling lemma for a shared existential bit. Setting: finite X; gadgets G_i subset of X x {0,1}; owner projection C_i = {x : exists z, (x,z) in G_i}; for T a set of gadget indices, shared(T) = {x : exists z, for all i in T, (x,z) in G_i} and owner(T) = intersection over i in T of C_i. Hypothesis (forced constants): for each i there is c_i in {0,1} with (x,z) in G_i implies z = c_i. Claim: if all c_i with i in T are equal to c, then shared(T) = owner(T); otherwise shared(T) is empty. Proof: if all c_i = c on T, then (x,z) in G_i forces z = c, so shared(T) = {x : (x,c) in G_i for all i in T}; and (x,c) in G_i iff x in C_i, because z is forced to c whenever x is in C_i. Hence shared(T) = owner(T). If c_i differ on T, no single z satisfies all gadgets in T, so shared(T) is empty. Scope: this is exact only for forced-constant gadgets, where the shared bit is already a constant and the formalization reduces to private gadgets with fixed values. It does NOT close G0001, which concerns shared bits not forced to a constant. Refutation of the determined-z repair (z = f_i(x) on each gadget): X = {x0,x1}, G_1 = {(x,z): z = [x = x1]}, G_2 = {(x,z): z = [x = x0]}, both with x-domain {x0,x1}. Owner: C_1 and C_2 both equal {x0,x1}, so owner({1,2}) is nonempty. Shared: z would need [x=x1] = [x=x0] for some x, which never holds, so shared({1,2}) is empty. Thus z is determined by x on each gadget, yet the shared formalization is spuriously unsat for a satisfiable owner pair.

question: Q-0332cb0a65
statement: LEMMA P (private pp-gadgets preserve the MUS clutter). Setting: Boolean relations over a finite language Gamma; instance I = (X, (C_i)_{i in [m]}) with C_i = (R_i, u_i), u_i a tuple of variables from X. Assume each R_i has a pp-definition R_i(y) iff exists z phi_i(y, z), phi_i a conjunction of Gamma-constraints. Gadget G(I): fresh variables Z_1..Z_m, pairwise disjoint and disjoint from X; block i is phi_i(u_i, Z_i). Claim: for all S subset of [m], Sat(G(I)_S) iff Sat(I_S), where G(I)_S and I_S are the sub-instances on blocks/constraints in S. Consequently the minimal-unsatisfiable index sets coincide (MUS clutter preserved exactly). PROOF. (=>) Let a satisfy all blocks i in S. Restricting to X, for each i in S the tuple a|u_i satisfies exists z phi_i(., z), i.e. a|u_i in R_i, so a|X satisfies I_S. (<=) Let x satisfy I_S. For each i in S, x|u_i in R_i, so there is a witness w_i with phi_i(x|u_i, w_i). Set a = x on X and a = w_i on Z_i. Block i depends only on u_i and Z_i, and the Z_i are disjoint, so a satisfies every block in S. Hence Sat(G(I)_S). Both directions use only the pp-definition and disjointness; no restriction on Gamma, arity or m. Minimality of an index set is defined from the predicate Sat alone, so the MUS clutters agree. NON-TRIVIAL CONSEQUENCE / NECESSITY OF PRIVACY: with shared auxiliary z, the gadget system satisfies Sat(shared_S) implies Sat(I_S) (projection), so unsat(I_S) implies unsat(shared_S), but not conversely. Counterexample: R_A = {x: x=0} with gadget exists z (x=z and z=0); R_B = {y: y=1} with gadget exists z (y=z and z=1). I_{A,B} is satisfiable (x=0, y=1), while the shared gadget forces z=0 and z=1, so {A,B} becomes a spurious MUS. Scope: exact for private gadgets (the form used by pp-reductions of CSP instances, which substitute a fresh copy of a fixed gadget per constraint). Open: the matroid-port statement for the full dichotomy (Q-7dba34f7a0), and whether every pp-definition used in a reduction can be made private without changing the instance family. Status: CLAIMED until reviewed by a different model family. Relates to S0003 (its owner-set claim is the affine special case of this lemma).

question: Q-0332cb0a65
statement:
statement: AFFINE CODIM-1 RECORD. Let n>=1, a in GF(2)^n nonzero, b in GF(2), H = {x : a.x = b}. Let E be a finite set of affine equations over (x, z), z = private auxiliaries (any number, any tuple), such that pi(sol E) = H where pi = projection to x and sol E is nonempty. Then for every subset T of E with sol T nonempty, pi(sol T) is H or the whole space GF(2)^n.
proof: (1) sol E is a subset of sol T, so pi(sol E) = H is a subset of pi(sol T). (2) Projection of a nonempty affine subspace of GF(2)^(n+|z|) under a linear map is an affine subspace of GF(2)^n; sol T is affine (solution set of a linear system) so pi(sol T) is affine. (3) H is an affine hyperplane (dimension n-1). Any affine subspace A with H subset of A has dim(A) in {n-1, n}; if dim n-1 then A = H, if dim n then A = whole space. Hence pi(T) in {H, X}. Q.E.D. Consequence: hypothesis R (of Lemma R, S0009) holds automatically for every affine private gadget whose target is an affine hyperplane; so Lemma R applies to all affine codim-1 targets without any check. Scope: GF(2)-affine gadgets, codimension-1 targets only; for codim >= 2 the argument gives only H subset pi(T), not R. Relation to S0003 (iii): this is the same fact, stated for R and with the nonvacuity-free condition.

question: Q-0332cb0a65
statement:
statement: LEMMA R-sound and LEMMA U (shared auxiliaries allowed). Setting: targets H_i = pi(sol E_i) nonempty, pi = projection to x, E_i finite affine systems over (x,z), z may be shared. (a) If the intersection of H_i over Q is empty, then the union over Q of E_i is inconsistent. (b) If there is Z(x) such that for every i and every x in H_i the fibre {z : (x,z) in sol E_i} equals Z(x), then the union over Q is consistent iff the intersection of H_i over Q is nonempty. Proofs: (a) any solution (x,z) gives x in every H_i, hence in the empty intersection. (b) for x in the intersection pick z in Z(x) (nonempty as x is in H_i); (x,z) satisfies every E_i in Q. Scope: consistency of full owner sets only. Does NOT give the MUS pushforward of S0009(a), which needs consistency of subsets S_i, and subsets can shrink the z-fibre. G0001 stays open.

question: Q-0332cb0a65
statement: Restricted case (no auxiliary variables, every constraint owner is a single relation over x, possibly with constants substituted): each owner contributes exactly one atom, so the owner-level MUS clutter equals the atom-level MUS clutter, and the port property for this restricted case reduces to the atom-level clutter. Proof: an owner is a single atom, so minimal unsatisfiable owner sets and minimal unsatisfiable atom sets coincide under the bijection owner -> atom. This shrinks the gap to the multi-atom no-auxiliary case only; it does not close G0001 or the original obligation.

question: Q-0332cb0a65
statement:
statement: Shared-auxiliary GF(2) gadgets E_i(x,z) with H_i = {x : exists z E_i(x,z)}. If there is a function g such that E_i(x,z) iff (x in H_i and z = g(x)) for every owner i, then for every owner set P: {E_i : i in P} is consistent iff the intersection of H_i over i in P is nonempty.
proof: If (x,z) satisfies all E_i with i in P, then x lies in every H_i, so the intersection is nonempty. Conversely, if x lies in the intersection, then z = g(x) satisfies every E_i. Both directions are immediate from the definitions.
scope: Only the common-definitional-function case. General shared auxiliaries (gap G0001) remain open.

question: Q-0332cb0a65
statement:
statement: Setting: GF(2), variables x in GF(2)^n and shared auxiliaries z in GF(2)^k. Owners i in [m] each contribute ONE equation a_i.x + b_i.z = c_i. Put vh_i = (a_i, b_i, c_i) in GF(2)^(n+k+1), let t = (0,...,0,1), and let E be the vector matroid on [m] plus e, with e mapped to t and i mapped to vh_i. For an owner set P, the subsystem {owners in P} is inconsistent iff t lies in span{vh_i : i in P}. The MUS clutter of the gadget system (minimal inconsistent owner sets) equals the port at e of this binary matroid.
proof: (1) Consistency. Let M be the (n+k)-column matrix with rows (a_i,b_i) for i in P, and c the vector of c_i. The system M y = c is solvable iff c lies in col(M). If c is not in col(M), there is lambda with lambda^T M = 0 and lambda.c = 1, so sum lambda_i vh_i = t. Conversely, if t = sum lambda_i vh_i, then lambda^T M = 0 and lambda.c = 1, so the system is unsolvable. Hence P is inconsistent iff t in span{vh_i : i in P}. (2) Port. Let X be a minimal subset of [m] with e in cl_E(X), i.e. r(X+e) = r(X), i.e. t in span(X). Then X+e contains a circuit C with e in C, and minimality forces X = C minus e. Conversely each circuit C through e gives C minus e as an inconsistent set, and the minimal ones are exactly the circuits through e minus e. So the MUS clutter is the port at e of E. (3) Each owner has exactly one equation, so a minimal inconsistent set of equations is a minimal inconsistent owner set, and the two clutters coincide. Loops (vh_i = 0) and parallel copies of t are handled by the same argument, since they give circuits of size 1 and 2 containing or avoiding e as appropriate.
scope: Exactly: GF(2) linear gadgets, one equation per owner, auxiliaries SHARED across owners. Covered by linear-matroid theory (classical; the step is a precise verified special case, not new mathematics). NOT covered: owners with two or more equations over shared z. There the owner clutter can be the port of U_{2,4} (not binary), see cm-f0a46fb95d764a4d and cm-7d3458c5d4a8460f, so the binary-port form fails for those owners. Consistent with cm-2918160065c34082, which tests the matroid-port form only for owners with 1-2 rows and m=3.
open_after: G0001 narrowed to owners with >=2 equations over shared auxiliaries. Open question: is the owner clutter of such a system a matroid port for all m (H_M)? Note: the question is open, not refuted.

question: Q-0332cb0a65
statement: S-COMMON-FUNCTION-OWNER-CLUTTER (CLAIMED, bookkeeping, closes nothing). Statement: let C_1..C_m be constraints on x in {0,1}^n, f: {0,1}^n -> {0,1}^k any fixed function, and G_i(x,z) := C_i(x) AND (z = f(x)) with one shared auxiliary block z. For every owner set S, {G_i : i in S} is satisfiable iff {C_i : i in S} is satisfiable; hence the owner-MUS clutter equals the original MUS clutter. Derivation: every solution (x,z) of the S-subsystem has z = f(x), so (x,z) solves it iff x solves {C_i : i in S}, and x -> (x, f(x)) is a bijection between the two solution sets. Satisfiability of every subset, and therefore minimal unsatisfiability, is preserved. Evidence: special case of H_common, cm-d3a069abe94d490b (0 of 1500 mismatches). Scope: exact for the semantic gadget only. It does NOT discharge G0001: the open point is whether the graph {(x, f(x))} is pp-definable in the target Post-lattice language Gamma, which is not established.

question: Q-0332cb0a65
statement: S-SHARED-Z-COMMUTATION (CLAIMED, restatement of the Galois correspondence, closes nothing). For f: {0,1}^n -> {0,1}^k and finite Boolean Gamma: graph(f) is pp-definable from Gamma iff f(g(x_1..x_r)) = g(f(x_1)..f(x_r)) for all g in Pol(Gamma) of arity r and all x_i. Proof: invariance of graph(f) under g is exactly this commutation; pp-definable relations are Pol-invariant; and Inv(Pol Gamma) equals the pp-closure of Gamma (Geiger; BCKSV). Consequence: the shared gadget z = f(x) is usable in Gamma only for f commuting with Pol(Gamma); for affine Gamma these are the affine maps. Evidence: cm-0d1388d5eb224886 (n=2, k=1; counts 8,5,5,6, hand-verified). Open: whether a non-trivial shared f commuting with the target Pol(Gamma) yields a port-preserving gadget for owner-MUS clutters.

question: Q-0332cb0a65
statement: statement: For GF(2) affine constraints a_i.x=b_i (i in [m], x in GF(2)^n, no auxiliary variables), let v_i=(a_i,b_i) in GF(2)^(n+1) and e=(0,...,0,1). Then S is a minimal inconsistent subset iff S is a minimal set with e in span(v_S), and these are exactly the sets C-e with C a circuit of the binary matroid on {v_i}+{e} containing e (the port of that matroid at e). question: Q-0332cb0a65
statement: LEMMA R-aff (affine gadgets, hyperplane scope). Setting: X = GF(2)^k; constraint i has gadget E_i, a finite system of affine equations over (x, z_i), with z_i private to constraint i; pi = projection to x; H_i = pi(sol(E_i)) is assumed to be an affine hyperplane of X. Claim: for every T subset of E_i with sol(T) nonempty, pi(sol(T)) is H_i or X, so hypothesis R_i holds. Proof: T subset of E_i implies sol(T) contains sol(E_i), so pi(sol(T)) contains H_i. pi(sol(T)) is an affine subspace, being a linear image of an affine space. A hyperplane is a maximal proper affine subspace, so any affine subspace containing H_i is H_i or X. Scope: affine gadgets with H_i a hyperplane only. Not covered: H_i of codimension >= 2 (the 12 point-H violations in cm-7a7d151bb1f24830), and non-affine gadgets (G0001 open, 853 violations).

question: Q-0332cb0a65
statement: LEMMA D (one-sided shared-auxiliary port, any finite relations over GF(2), no affineness used). Setting: constraints i with H_i a subset of X = GF(2)^n; gadget E_i a finite set of relations over (x, z) with z one SHARED auxiliary block; pi_x(sol(E_i)) = H_i. For S a set of constraints let G_S = union over i in S of E_i. Claim: if the original subsystem S is inconsistent (intersection over i in S of H_i is empty), then G_S is inconsistent. Proof: suppose (x,z) satisfies G_S. Then (x,z) satisfies each E_i with i in S, so x lies in pi_x(sol(E_i)) = H_i for every i in S, hence x lies in the intersection, which is empty. Contradiction. So every original-inconsistent subset stays inconsistent in the gadget system, and every original MUS contains a gadget-inconsistent set. Scope: this is the soundness direction only. The converse (gadget-inconsistent implies original-inconsistent) is exactly what fails for shared z: cm-2d1bfecd874342f9 gives the two-constraint counterexample with H_0 = H_1 = GF(2)^3 and gadgets {z=0} and {z=1}, and cm-f417cc87c52645a9 gives 918/3750 mismatches with free constants.

question: Q-0332cb0a65
closes: none (sharpens Q-e8ef90900d; does NOT close G0001)
statement:
statement: Let V_i = span(v_i) in GF(2)^(N+1) for occurrences i in a finite index set I (each bundle is a single augmented equation, coefficients in (x,z), right-hand side last), t = (0,...,0,1). For S subset of I, the system {equations of i : i in S} is inconsistent iff t lies in span{v_i : i in S}. The minimal inconsistent occurrence sets are exactly the sets C minus {t}, where C ranges over the circuits of the binary vector matroid on {v_i : i in I} plus {t} that contain t.
derivation: (1) Fredholm alternative for GF(2) affine systems: a system with augmented rows v_i (right-hand side last) is unsolvable iff some GF(2)-combination of its rows is 0 = 1, i.e. iff t in span{v_i : i in S}. (2) If S is minimal with t in span(S), then S is independent (otherwise a proper subset already spans) and S union {t} is dependent with a unique expression of t; hence S union {t} is a circuit containing t. (3) Conversely, a circuit C containing t gives S = C minus {t} with t in span(S), and minimality follows because a proper subset of S spanning t would yield a smaller dependent set containing t, contradicting circuit minimality. Zero vectors v_i = 0 (trivially satisfiable equations) are in no circuit and are excluded. Case v_i = t gives the singleton circuit {i, t}, i.e. S = {i}, consistent with the statement.
scope: Rank-1 bundles only (each occurrence contributes one linear equation). Finite, exact. Does NOT cover bundles of rank >= 2, and does NOT cover shared auxiliaries in the rank >= 2 setting (counterexample cm-c960a57e095a4e0e shows the interface identity fails there).

question: Q-0332cb0a65
statement: LEMMA (fiber identity, hand-proved; CLAIMED, not reviewed): owners i in [m] with S_i subset of X x Z, A_i^z = {x : (x,z) in S_i}. For nonempty T, the intersection over i in T of S_i is empty iff for every z in Z the intersection over i in T of A_i^z is empty. Proof: (x,z) lies in the joint intersection iff x lies in every fiber intersection at z. Consequence: the joint MUS clutter is the minimal elements of the intersection over z of the fiber up-sets U_z, and it is not the union or intersection of the per-fiber clutters. Counterexample: X={0,1}, Z={0,1}, S_0 = X x {0}, S_1 = X x {1}. Then {0,1} is minimal in U_0 cap U_1 while min(U_0) = {{1}}, min(U_1) = {{0}}. This closes no obligation: it is a structural diagnosis, not a repair of G0001.

question: Q-0332cb0a65
statement: LEMMA A (linear-algebra repair of the shared-auxiliary statement; hand-proved; CLAIMED, not reviewed). Claim: a set T of owners is jointly inconsistent iff e=(0,...,0,1) lies in the sum over i in T of R_i. Proof: the stacked system is inconsistent iff the rhs unit vector is in the row space of its augmented matrix (Rouche-Capelli over GF(2)), and the row space of the stacked system is the sum of the R_i. Corollary (one-row owners, row w_i): the MUS clutter over owners is {C minus e : C a circuit of the binary matroid on {w_i} + {e} with e in C}, i.e. the binary port at e; this holds with the shared z-block. The naive projected clutter (intersection of projections H_i empty) uses R_i intersect V_X (z-coefficients zero) instead of R_i, so it can lose the coupling: example n=2, k=1, owners z=0 and z=1: MUS {0,1}, but both projections are full X. question: Q-08a1c5b68f
statement: LEMMA-A-REPAIR. Setting: N=2^n, F subset {0,1}^N. A streaming search system has state q_0, transitions q_{t+1}=F_t(q_t,x_{t+1}), so q_t(p) depends only on the prefix p of length t, and a decoder D on the final state q_N(w) which, for every w in {0,1}^N, outputs a circuit computing w if w in F and rejects otherwise. Call a length-t prefix p LIVE if some u has pu in F, DEAD otherwise. Claim: for each t, q_t(p) != q_t(p') whenever p is live and p' != p (length t), so the live prefixes have pairwise distinct states and no state is shared with any other prefix. Consequently 2^S >= L_t + [L_t < 2^t]. Proof: let p be live with completion u (pu in F) and suppose q_t(p')=q_t(p) with p' != p. Then q_N(pu)=q_N(p'u), so D returns the same answer on both strings. Since pu in F, D must output a circuit computing pu; so D accepts p'u with that circuit, which must compute p'u if p'u in F, and it cannot compute both pu and p'u because they differ in the first t bits. Hence p'u not in F and D must reject p'u, but it accepts pu, which is an identical decision on identical states: contradiction. A dead prefix thus gets a state no live prefix has, and if a dead prefix exists at t one extra code is needed, giving the bound. Scope: the search model above only; it says nothing about decoder size D, gate cost G, or encodings (G0001-G0004 remain open).

statement: Lemma (repair of the G=1 structural claim). Let F: {0,1}^S x {0,1} -> {0,1}^S be computed by a circuit with exactly one non-free gate g over basis {AND,OR,XOR,const}, NOT free. Then there is I subset [S], |I| <= 1, such that for j not in I, F_j is a literal (x_i, NOT x_i, b, NOT b) or a constant; if I={i}, F_i = op(l1,l2) for a 2-input op and literals l1,l2 of (x,b) or constants. Proof: each output coordinate is wired to an input/constant or is the unique gate output, so at most one coordinate is non-literal. Consequence: the G=1 transition set is the G=0 literal-wiring set with one coordinate replaced by an arbitrary two-literal gate; this matches the existing SAT option set and gives no algorithmic saving. Does not bound G_max, decoder D, or general algorithms.

question: Q-08a1c5b68f
statement: LEMMA (dead-separated count bound). Let n=3, N=8. Fix a level t and let P_t be the set of distinct live residual functions at level t. Suppose a one-pass system with S state bits assigns codes E_t: {0,1}^t -> {0,1}^S such that (i) live prefixes with equal residual get equal code and live prefixes with different residuals get different codes; (ii) every dead prefix has a code different from all live codes; (iii) at least one dead prefix exists at level t. Then 2^S >= |P_t| + 1, hence S >= ceil(log2(|P_t|+1)). PROOF: by (i), the live residual classes receive |P_t| pairwise distinct codes in {0,1}^S. By (ii) and (iii), a dead prefix has a code outside that set, so the image of E_t has at least |P_t|+1 elements, and 2^S >= |P_t|+1. QED. APPLICATION (conditional on (iii) at the maximising level, NOT yet verified): SC_{3,1} gives S>=ceil(log2 39)=6; affine control gives S>=5; SC_{3,2} gives S>=8.

question: Q-08a1c5b68f
statement: CORRECTION of the S>=6 claim for SC_{3,1}. The quantity that must be separated is the number R_t of DISTINCT RESIDUALS of live prefixes at level t (residual = set of suffixes completing the prefix to a function in F), not the number of full truth tables. LEMMA: let E_t be dead-separated codes (live prefixes with different residuals get different codes, dead prefixes get codes outside the live set), and D_t = number of dead prefixes at level t. Then 2^S >= R_t + [D_t > 0] for every t. PROOF: if two live prefixes p, q have E_t(p)=E_t(q) but different residuals, some suffix b makes the final output differ for one of them, so the code cannot be correct for both; hence R_t distinct live codes are needed. If D_t > 0, a dead prefix needs one further code outside the live set. QED. APPLICATION: cm-6468ef6ec5214251 (SC_{3,1}, n=3, N=8, F = one-gate circuits, |F|=38) gives level 4: R=13, D=0, so S>=4; level 5: R=14, D=10, so 15 codes and S>=4; maximum over levels S>=4. The earlier S>=6 (from 38 at level N) is withdrawn.

question: Q-08a1c5b68f
statement: Induction on t. t=0: state constant, J_0 empty. Step: suppose every state bit at time t is a sign-literal of a coordinate in J_t or a constant. A bit at time t+1 is a literal of an old state bit (hence a sign-literal of a coordinate of J_t or a constant) or a literal of b_{t+1} or a constant. So each bit at time t+1 is a sign-literal of a coordinate in J_t union {t+1} or a constant. Let J_{t+1} be the set of coordinates appearing in these literals; |J_{t+1}| <= S since there are S bits, and J_{t+1} subset of J_t union {t+1}. Every bit is a fixed function of p restricted to J_{t+1}, so equal projections give equal states. Conversely each coordinate of J_{t+1} is exposed by some bit with fixed sign, so equal states give equal coordinates on J_{t+1}. Hence state(p)=state(q) iff p|J=q|J. Separation at time t requires state(p) different from state(q) for live p and dead q, hence p|J_t differs from q|J_t, so |J_t| >= sep_t and S >= sep_t. This is exact for M0 only.

question: Q-08a1c5b68f
statement: LEMMA-A-SEARCH (repair of S0009, search semantics). Setting: N=2^n strings w in {0,1}^N, F subset {0,1}^N, streaming states q_t(p) on prefixes p of length t, final state q_N(w), decoder D with D(q_N(w)) = a circuit computing w if w in F, and reject if w not in F. Claim: for every t, if p is live (some pu in F) and p' != p has length t, then q_t(p') != q_t(p). Moreover, if a dead prefix p' exists at t then q_t(p') differs from all live codes. Proof: suppose q_t(p)=q_t(p') with pu in F. Then for every suffix v, q_N(pv)=q_N(p'v). Take v=u: the decoder accepts pu, so it returns a circuit C with C computing pu and C computing p'u only if p'u in F; but the same state gives the same decoder output, so D(q_N(p'u)) = C accepts, forcing p'u in F. Then the single state class contains two distinct F-strings pu and p'u, and D must output one circuit computing both pu and p'u, which differ in the first t bits: impossible. The same argument with a dead p' gives p'u not in F while D accepts, contradiction. Hence live codes are injective and disjoint from dead codes, so S_t >= ceil(log2(L_t + [dead prefix exists])). Scope: the search model above, time-dependent encodings, unbounded update and decoder cost. This is NOT the decision-only separation claim: the refutation of S0009 (R1146) used a counterexample with F={000,001,010,011} that gives two F-strings one code, which the search model forbids. It proves no G_max value and closes no G0001-G0004. Checked by finite enumeration: physalis_code_run for N=4, t=2 (criterion of the class condition; see cm for result).

question: Q-08a1c5b68f
statement: LEMMA-G1-REPAIR (repair of S0014, fan-out corrected). Setting: S >= 1, F: {0,1}^S x {0,1} -> {0,1}^S computed by a circuit over basis {AND, OR, XOR, constants} with NOT free, containing exactly one non-free gate g. Claim: there is a two-literal gate g* = op(l1, l2), where op is one of AND, OR, XOR and l1, l2 are literals of the inputs (x_1..x_S, b) or constants, such that every output coordinate F_j is a literal, a constant, or +/- g*, for all j. Proof: every wire feeding an output is an input, a constant, the negation of one of these, or the output of g (the only non-free gate). The inputs of g are themselves wires with no non-free gate upstream, so each is a literal or a constant; hence g = op(l1, l2) with literals or constants l1, l2. Each output coordinate is therefore a literal, a constant, or +/- g. Fan-out is allowed: any number of coordinates may equal +/- g, so the index set I = {j : F_j in {g, NOT g}} is arbitrary, with no bound |I| <= 1. Consequence: the G=1 transition set is the G=0 literal-wiring set with the coordinates in an arbitrary subset I replaced by a shared two-literal gate (with polarity). Scope: one non-free gate, free NOT, one-step transition function only. Says nothing about G_max, decoder cost D, or multi-step circuits. Mechanical check still open: enumerate S=2 single-gate circuits and compare with the stated form.

question: Q-08a1c5b68f
statement: REPAIR of S0009 (conflict-graph form). Setting as in S0009: streaming system with q_{t+1}=F_t(q_t,b), decoder D on q_N, correct on every w in {0,1}^N (outputs a circuit computing w if w in F, rejects otherwise). Let H_t be the graph on LIVE prefixes of length t with p~p' iff some u has pu in F and p'u in F. Claim: (a) if p != p' are live and q_t(p)=q_t(p') then no u has pu, p'u both in F; (b) if p is dead and p' live with q_t(p)=q_t(p') then no u has p'u in F. Hence live codes properly colour H_t and avoid all dead codes, so 2^S >= omega(H_t) + [a dead prefix exists]; and for each fixed u, {p : pu in F} is a clique of H_t, so 2^S >= max_u |{p : pu in F}| + [dead prefix exists]. Proof of (a): q_N(pu)=q_N(p'u), so D gives the same circuit C on both; if both are in F, C must compute pu and p'u, which differ in a coordinate among the first t positions: contradiction. Proof of (b): take u with p'u in F; D outputs C computing p'u on q_N(p'u)=q_N(pu); since pu not in F, D must reject pu, contradiction. Scope: per-time code counting with the decoder; says nothing about G_max or gate cost.

question: Q-08a1c5b68f
statement: CLAIMED. Per-suffix injectivity lemma (repair of S0009; reconciles the dispute). Setup: F subset of {0,1}^N, N=2^n. A streaming machine has state set {0,1}^S, a deterministic update c(t+1, p+x*2^t) = U(c(t,p), x), and a decoder D with D(final state of w) = w for every w in F. Claim: for every suffix u of length N-t and every prefix p, p' of length t with pu in F and p'u in F, if p != p' then c(t,p) != c(t,p'). Proof: if c(t,p) = c(t,p'), the update is deterministic, so reading u from both gives the same final state. Then D gives pu = p'u, hence p = p', a contradiction. Consequence (counting): for every t and every suffix u, the set {p in {0,1}^t : pu in F} has at most 2^S elements, so S >= log2 max_{t,u} |F_u^t| where F_u^t = {p : pu in F}. Scope: a bound on the state count for a machine that reads the bits in order and decodes the table exactly. It bounds neither the update-circuit size G nor G_max, and it is not the pairwise claim of S0009.

question: Q-08a1c5b68f
statement: Lemma A: for any copy-only update g:{0,1}^S x {0,1} -> {0,1}^S (each output bit a constant, a literal x_i xor c, or b xor c), g's image is an affine subspace of GF(2)^S of size 2^r, r = number of distinct source variables selected by some output bit. Proof: g(z)=Az+c with A having at most one 1 per row, so nonzero columns have disjoint supports and rank A = r; image = c + Im A.

statement: LEMMA-G1-REPAIR (repairs S0014). Setting: F:{0,1}^S x {0,1} -> {0,1}^S computed by a circuit with exactly one non-free gate g (basis AND, OR, XOR, const; NOT free). Proof: free nodes are functions of inputs and constants only. Since g is the only non-free node, its inputs are free nodes, and each output wire is a free node or g (possibly negated). Scope: one non-free gate only. Consequence: the G=1 transition set is literal wiring plus one shared two-literal gate attached to an arbitrary subset I of coordinates with arbitrary polarities. |I| is unbounded (F_1=F_2=AND(x1,x2) has |I|=2), so the S0014 claim |I|<=1 is refuted and this repair replaces it. question: Q-08a1c5b68f
statement: REPAIR-S0009 (injectivity and disjointness). Setting as S0009: N=2^n, F subset {0,1}^N, streaming states q_t(p) depending only on prefix p of length t, decoder D on q_N(w). (i) Injectivity on F: if w != w' are both in F and q_N(w) = q_N(w') = s, then D(s) is one circuit that must compute both w and w', which is impossible. So w -> q_N(w) is injective on F and 2^S >= |F|. (ii) Disjointness: if q_t(p) = q_t(p') with p != p' of length t, then for every suffix u at most one of pu, p'u lies in F, because q_N(pu) = q_N(p'u) would contradict (i). (iii) The pairwise claim (all live prefixes of one length get distinct codes) does NOT follow: F = {000,111}, t = 2, prefixes 00 and 11 have disjoint suffix sets and may share a code. Result: (i) and (ii) hold and give only the counting bound 2^S >= |F|. Scope: the streaming model only; says nothing about decoder size D, gate cost G, or encodings.

statement: REPAIR-S0014 (shared gate). Setting: circuit over AND, OR, XOR, constants with NOT free and exactly one non-free gate g. Then every output F_j is a literal, a constant, or +/-g. Proof: each output wire passes through NOT gates back to an input, a constant, or g; the inputs of g are literals or constants because g is the only non-free gate. So the set I = {j : F_j = +/-g} is arbitrary in size, matching the S0014 counterexample F_1 = F_2 = AND(x1,x2) with |I| = 2. Hence S >= ceil(log2 38) = 6 for SC_{3,1} (N=8) and S >= ceil(log2 16) = 4 for AFFINE_3 (not 5 as written in the previous run's setup). Proof: an injection Live_t -> {0,1}^S. question: Q-08a1c5b68f
statement: LEMMA G0 (exact scope): let N>=1, F subset {0,1}^N nonempty, and c a streaming code with c(eps)=c0 constant and c(wb)=U(c(w),b), where every output coordinate of U is a constant, a literal of b, or a literal of a state bit (G=0). If c is injective on Live_t for each t and c(Live_t) is disjoint from c(Dead_t), where Live_t={f|[t]: f in F} and Dead_t={0,1}^t minus Live_t, then S >= N. Proof: by induction every coordinate of c(w) is a constant or +/- w_j for a single letter j, so at most S letters are read. If letter j is read by no coordinate, take f in F and flip bit j to get g; then c(g)=c(f). If g is in F, injectivity fails; if g is not in F, separation fails. So every letter is read and N <= S. Tightness: a shift register with S=N and code = reversed prefix padded with zeros works. Scope: G=0 branch only; it shows G_max(S<N) >= 1 and that the cost of free updates is S=N for every family alike. It does not measure G_max for G>=1 and does not close G0085.

question: Q-08a1c5b68f
statement: LEMMA-S29-REPAIR (repair of S0029, search model). Setting: N=2^n, F subset of {0,1}^N, a streaming transducer with states from a set of size 2^S, deterministic time-dependent transitions q_{t+1}(pb) = delta_t(q_t(p), b), and a decoder D depending only on q_N(w), where D(q_N(w)) computes w for w in F and rejects for w not in F. For a prefix length t let Live_t = {p in {0,1}^t : p u in F for some u} and Dead_t = {0,1}^t minus Live_t. Claim: (i) p -> q_t(p) is injective on Live_t; (ii) q_t(Live_t) and q_t(Dead_t) are disjoint. Hence 2^S >= |Live_t| + [Dead_t nonempty]. Proof of (i): let p != p' be live with q_t(p)=q_t(p'). Pick u with pu in F. Then q_N(pu)=q_N(p'u), so D returns the same circuit C on both; C computes pu, and D must accept p'u, which forces p'u in F and C computes p'u too. Two different truth tables cannot both equal C, so pu = p'u, contradicting p != p'. Proof of (ii): let p live and p' dead with equal states. Pick u with pu in F. Then D(q_N(p'u)) = D(q_N(pu)) accepts, but p'u is not in F, so D must reject: contradiction. Scope: exactly this search model (decoder sees only the final state, unbounded update and decoder cost). It bounds the number of states, not the per-step gate count G, so it closes no gap G0001-G0004 and bounds nothing beyond the pigeonhole count. Corrects S0029: the separation holds on prefixes (stronger than residuals), so the bound |Live_t| + [Dead_t nonempty] <= 2^S is the correct form. Checkable by finite enumeration on small N (N=4, t=2).

question: Q-08a1c5b68f
statement: REPAIR of G0117 (conflict-clique bound, search model). Setting: N=2^n, F subset {0,1}^N, transducer q_{t+1}=F_t(q_t,b) with time-dependent F_t, decoder D on q_N that outputs a circuit computing w when w in F and rejects otherwise, correct on every w in {0,1}^N. Let H_t be the graph on live length-t prefixes with p~p' iff some u has pu, p'u both in F. Claim: any state map on live prefixes is a proper colouring of H_t, and every live code differs from every dead code when a dead prefix exists. Hence 2^S >= omega(H_t) + [a dead prefix of length t exists]. Proof: (i) if p != p' are live with q_t(p)=q_t(p') and pu, p'u in F, then q_N(pu)=q_N(p'u) by the transition rule, so D returns one circuit C that must compute both pu and p'u; these differ at a position < t, impossible. (ii) if p is dead and p' live with the same code, pick u with p'u in F; q_N(pu)=q_N(p'u), so D returns a circuit that must reject pu, but it accepts, a contradiction. A clique of H_t needs pairwise distinct codes, and all dead prefixes can share one extra code. Instance: n=3, s=1, N=8, |F|=38 (asserted in code). At t=7: omega=19, dead=1, so S >= ceil(log2 20) = 5. question: Q-08a1c5b68f
statement: State-size pigeonhole: for a deterministic streaming algorithm with state set Σ, if L prefixes are pairwise distinguished by some suffix, then |Σ| ≥ L, hence ceil(log2 L) bits are needed. Proof: if two distinct distinguished prefixes reach the same state, every suffix gives the same output, a contradiction, so the map prefix→state is injective. Scope: any update time. Bookkeeping only: it does not bound update time and does not close G0001 or G0004. The separation of SC_{3,1} live/dead prefixes is taken from the spec and not re-checked here.

question: Q-08a1c5b68f
statement: PROOF. By induction on t, every coordinate of q_t(p) is a constant or a literal of a single bit of p: q_0 is constant, and each step copies a literal of a state coordinate or of the input bit. So there is a set J of at most S positions with q_N(p) determined by p restricted to J. Suppose S < N. Then some position k is outside J. Pick w in F (F nonempty) and let w' = w with bit k flipped. Then q_N(w') = q_N(w). If w' is in F, two distinct live words share a state, contradicting injectivity on F. If w' is not in F, a dead word shares a state with a live word, contradicting disjointness. Both cases are impossible, so S >= N. QED. Corollary: for every S < N and every nonempty F, a wiring-only (G=0) system does not satisfy the search condition. In particular the G=0 test for SC_{3,1} at S=6 is UNSAT by this argument, with no SAT run needed.

question: Q-08a1c5b68f

statement: CLAIMED (unreviewed) copy-class coordinate lemma. question: Q-08a1c5b68f
statement: LEMMA-CLIQUE (explicit form of S0086(a,b), no closure claimed). Setting: N=2^n, F subset of {0,1}^N, deterministic streaming system with states q_t(p) on prefixes p of length t (time-dependent update), final state q_N(w), decoder D with D(q_N(w)) = a circuit computing w if w in F, and D rejects if w not in F. Let H_t have vertex set the live length-t prefixes (p with some pv in F), with p~p' iff some v has pv and p'v both in F. Claim: (a) if p != p' are live and q_t(p)=q_t(p'), then no v has pv and p'v both in F. Proof: q_t equal implies q_N(pv)=q_N(p'v) for every v (the update is a function of the state and the input bits, so the same state gives the same future). If both pv, p'v are in F, D returns one circuit computing both strings; they differ (they agree on the first t bits only if the rest differs, but p != p' gives distinct strings), contradiction. (b) if p is dead (no pv in F) and p' is live with q_t(p)=q_t(p'), then for any v with p'v in F we get q_N(pv)=q_N(p'v), so D accepts pv with a circuit, but pv is not in F: contradiction. Consequence: the codes of the vertices of any clique of H_t are pairwise distinct and disjoint from the code of any dead prefix, so the number of states is at least omega(H_t) + [a dead length-t prefix exists]. Scope: space (state count) only; update cost, decoder cost and oracle gates are unbounded and not addressed; it does not bound G, G_max, or the MMW Thm 4.1 setting. question: Q-08a1c5b68f
statement: L-G0-ZERO: Let N >= S+2. Consider a time-indexed streaming transducer with S slots where, at step t, each slot is updated by one option shared by all nodes at time t: copy of slot k (k<S), the streamed bit b_t, or constant 0 or 1. Then no such transducer with any liveness predicate lv on the S-bit state recognises the prefixes of the constant-0 function on {0,1}^N. Proof: by induction on t, every slot's value at node (t,v) is a constant or x_s for a single position s fixed by the options (not by v). So the state at (t,v) depends only on v restricted to I_t, with |I_t| <= S. Take t = S+1 <= N-1 and p in {0..t-1} \ I_t. Then 0^t (live) and 0^t with a 1 at p (dead, since it is not a prefix of the zero function) have equal states, so lv cannot separate them.

statement: LEMMA (state lower bound from prefix classes, exact). Let f: {0,1}^N -> {0,1} and let p ~_t q (p,q in {0,1}^t) iff f(pz) = f(qz) for every z in {0,1}^(N-t). Let C_t be the number of ~_t classes. Then every deterministic streaming automaton that reads x_1..x_N in order and outputs f(x) after the last bit has at least C_t distinct states after reading t bits. PROOF: if p ~_t' q are in different classes, some suffix z has f(pz) != f(qz). If p and q reached the same state after t bits, the remaining computation on pz and qz would be identical, so the outputs would agree, a contradiction. Hence distinct classes occupy distinct states. question: Q-08a1c5b68f
statement: LEMMA W0 (zero-gate streaming needs N state bits). Setting: N=2^n, F subset of {0,1}^N nonempty. State q_0 is constant in {0,1}^S, q_t = F_t(q_{t-1}, x_t), where F_t is a zero-gate circuit: each output bit is a constant, or a literal (possibly negated) of an old state bit or of x_t. Decoder D is a function of q_N only and must output a circuit computing w if w in F, and reject if w not in F, for every w in {0,1}^N. Claim: S >= N. PROOF. (1) By induction on t, each coordinate i of q_t(w) is a constant or +/- w_s for one index s = s_i(t) <= t, and s depends only on the wiring, not on w (base: q_0 constant; step: an output is a constant, +/- x_t, or +/- an old coordinate, which by hypothesis is a constant or +/- w_s). (2) Let J = {s_i(N)} over the non-constant coordinates. Then |J| <= S and q_N(w) depends on w only through w restricted to J. (3) Suppose |J| < N. Pick k not in J and some w in F. Let w' be w with bit k flipped. Then q_N(w') = q_N(w). If w' in F, D outputs one circuit that must compute both w and w', but w != w' have different truth tables: impossible. If w' not in F, D must reject w' while outputting a circuit for w on the same code: contradiction. Hence |J| = N, so S >= |J| = N. QED.

question: Q-08a1c5b68f
statement: LEMMA SENS (sensitivity of final codes, any gate count). Setting: N=2^n, F subset of {0,1}^N. Streaming system: q_0 fixed, q_{t+1}=F_t(q_t,x_{t+1}) with arbitrary (time-dependent, arbitrary-cost) F_t; Q(w)=q_N(w); decoder D depends only on Q(w) and must output a circuit whose truth table is w when w in F, and reject when w not in F, for every w in {0,1}^N. Claim: for every w in F and every k in [N], Q(w^k) != Q(w), where w^k flips bit k. PROOF. Suppose Q(w^k)=Q(w)=c. Then D(c) is one output. If w^k in F, D(c) must compute both w and w^k, which are distinct truth tables: impossible. If w^k not in F, D(c) must be a circuit for w (since w in F), but D must reject w^k: contradiction. QED. COROLLARY (zero-gate case, reproving W0): if F_t are zero-gate, Q depends only on a set J of at most S positions; if |J|<N pick k outside J and w in F, so Q(w^k)=Q(w), contradicting SENS; hence S >= N.

question: Q-0af687a9cf
statement: LEMMA (split sensitivity, matching family). Let k >= 2 be even, n = 2k, and F(x,y) = OR_{j=1..k} (x_j AND y_j), where x = (x_1..x_k) and y = (y_1..y_k) with y_j the variable k+j of pair P_j = {j, k+j}. Each AND is THR with weights (1,1) and threshold 2, and the OR is THR, so F is THR o THR with k bottom gates. (a) For the split S_1 = {1..k} | rest, D = 2^k. Proof: the residual of x is R_x(y) = OR_{j in supp(x)} y_j. If x != x', pick j in supp(x) minus supp(x') (or the symmetric case); then R_x(e_j) = 1 and R_x'(e_j) = 0, so x -> R_x is injective and D = 2^k. (b) For the balanced split S_2 = {1..k/2} union {k+1..k+k/2}, F = a(x) OR b(y), where a(x) = OR_{j<=k/2} (x_j AND x_{k+j}) and b(y) = OR_{k/2<j<=k} (y_j AND y_{k+j}). If a(x) = 1 the residual is constant 1; otherwise it equals b. Hence D <= 2. Consequence: for this family min over balanced splits of D is at most 2, while the first-half split gives 2^k. statement: LEMMA (single-gate and union residual distance, integer weights). Let g_j(x,y) = [a_j.x + v_j.y >= t_j] for j = 1..m, with a_j integer in Z^k, v_j integer in Z^(n-k), r_j = number of nonzero entries of v_j, and |v_ji| >= 1 on the support. Let f(x,y) = [sum_j g_j(x,y) >= T] and let y be uniform on {0,1}^(n-k). Then for all x, x' in {0,1}^k: Pr_y[f(x,y) != f(x',y)] <= sum_j |a_j.(x-x')| * C(r_j, floor(r_j/2)) / 2^(r_j), where a term with r_j = 0 is replaced by 1 if g_j(x,.) and g_j(x',.) differ. PROOF: (i) If all g_j agree at (x,y) and (x',y), the sums agree, so f agrees; hence a disagreement needs some g_j to disagree. (ii) For r_j >= 1, g_j(x,y) != g_j(x',y) forces v_j.y to lie in a half-open interval of integers of length |a_j.(x-x')|. (iii) Erdos (1945): for real |v_i| >= 1, an open interval of length 2 contains at most C(r, floor(r/2)) subset sums; so for each integer s, Pr_y[v_j.y = s] <= C(r_j, floor(r_j/2))/2^(r_j). statement: LEMMA (subclass, bounded top fan-in, O2 of PNP-001-THR-SAT-2026-11-21). Then #f = |{x in {0,1}^n : f(x)=1}| is computed exactly by the DP that keeps, after each variable i, a multiplicity table over the vectors (W_j . x_{<=i})_{j in S}. Each coordinate lies in [-Bn, Bn], so the table has at most min(2^i, (2Bn+1)^k) entries at step i. Total time O(k n min(2^n, (2Bn+1)^k)) arithmetic operations. statement: SUBCLASS LEMMA (exact counting, #SAT of THR o THR with few distinct bottom forms). Setting: f(z) = [sum_{j<=m} v_j [w_j.z >= t_j] >= T], integer weights w_j in {-W..W}^n, t_j, v_j, T integers. Let f_1..f_r be the DISTINCT weight vectors among the w_j, and sigma(j) the index with w_j = f_{sigma(j)}. Let h = floor(n/2), X = first h variables, Y = the remaining n-h. Then #f = sum over a in Z^r of N_X(a) * G(a), where N_X(a) = #{x in {0,1}^h : (f_i.x)_i = a} and G(a) = #{y in {0,1}^(n-h) : sum_j v_j [B_{sigma(j)}(y) + a_{sigma(j)} >= t_j] >= T}, B_i(y) = f_i restricted to Y . y. PROOF: w_j.(x,y) = f_{sigma(j)}.x + f_{sigma(j)}.y = a_{sigma(j)}(x) + B_{sigma(j)}(y), so the gate test depends on x only through a(x) in Z^r, and the summand depends on x only through a(x). Summing over x grouped by a(x) gives the formula. The number of a with N_X(a) > 0 is at most min(2^h, (2Wh+1)^r), since each coordinate a_i(x) lies in [-Wh, Wh]. Total time = poly(n,m) * (2^(n/2) + min(2^(n/2), (2Wh+1)^r) * 2^(n/2)) <= poly(m,n) * 2^(n/2) * min(2^(n/2), (2Wn+1)^r). For FIXED r and W (or W = poly(n) with fixed r) this is 2^(n/2) * poly(n), i.e. a saving of 2^(n/2)/poly(n) = 2^n / n^{omega(1)} over brute force, for exact #f. question: Q-0b7da33369
statement: S0012 (repair of the caveat in S0010 review, CLAIMED by R1090): the O(1)-gate memory/cost separation for DISJ_n also holds for a STATIONARY update circuit F (one circuit for all t), not only for time-dependent F_t. Construction: state = data ring D (n cells, FIFO), pointer ring P (n cells, one-hot, rotating every step, initial one-hot at cell 1), phase bit f (initially 0), result bit r (initially 0). Input bit w per step. Update: D'_1 = f ? D_n : w; D'_j = D_{j-1} for j >= 2 (wires); P rotates (wires); f' = f OR P_n; r' = r OR (f AND D_n AND w). Proof: steps 1..n: f=0, so D'_1 = w and the FIFO holds a_t; P_n fires first at step n, so f=1 from step n+1 on. After step n, D_n = a_1. Step n+i (i=1..n): reads D_n = a_i and w = b_i, sets r to r OR (a_i AND b_i), and cycles a_i back to D_1, so D_n becomes a_{i+1} for the next step. After 2n steps r = OR_i (a_i AND b_i) = DISJ_n. Cost: the update has O(1) gates (two gates for D'_1, one for f', two for r'); all other cells are wires, which are free in gate counting. State is 3n+1 bits, so memory is linear, as in S0010. Scope: this is a correction of the stationary caveat only. It does not give sublinear memory, and it does not bear on G0001 or G0002 (superlinear online cut-width). It is a construction, not a lower bound, and it closes no open obligation.

question: Q-0b7da33369
statement: L1 (memory lower bound for one-pass DISJ, bookkeeping level, does NOT close G0001 or G0002): let M be any one-pass machine reading a stream of length 2n, first a in {0,1}^n then b in {0,1}^n, with 2^S states (transitions may depend on time, no uniformity). If it outputs DISJ_n(a,b) = OR_i(a_i AND b_i) at the end, then S >= n. Proof: let q(a) be the state after reading a. Suppose a != a' with q(a) = q(a'). Choose i with a_i != a'_i. If a_i = 1, a'_i = 0: the pair (a', not-a) has DISJ = 0 (because a'_i' AND not a_i' = 0 for every i') and the pair (a, not-a) ... use the chain: run on (a', not-a') gives 0 and run on (a, not-a') has the same final state as (a', not-a') because q(a) = q(a'); but DISJ(a, not-a') = 1 since a_i AND not a'_i = 1. Contradiction. The case a_i = 0, a'_i = 1 is symmetric (swap a and a'). So q is injective on {0,1}^n, hence 2^S >= 2^n. Scope: arbitrary deterministic one-pass machines, any time-dependent transitions, state counted in bits. It matches S0022 (2n+2 bits), so linear memory is tight for DISJ. It says nothing about the number of gates or the total cost sum_t CC(F_t) + CC(D_N), which is what G0002 needs. Novelty: standard one-way communication fooling-set argument (Kremer-Nisan-Ron line); no claim of novelty.

question: Q-0b7da33369
statement: LEMMA R (unrolling, CLAIMED, session R-current, author Claude Haiku 5.5). Setting: L_n: {0,1}^N -> {0,1}; one-pass realisation with state space {0,1}^S, initial state c_0, update circuits F_t: {0,1}^S x {0,1} -> {0,1}^S (t = 1..N, each with CC(F_t) gates, fan-in 2, fixed complete basis), readout D_N: {0,1}^S -> {0,1}. Claim: chaining F_1,...,F_N and D_N (state wires internal, c_0 hard-wired) gives a general Boolean circuit computing L_n with at most sum_t CC(F_t) + CC(D_N) gates. Proof: the chained circuit is a fan-in-2 circuit over the same basis; its gate set is the disjoint union of the gates of the F_t and D_N; wires cost nothing; a constant input to a gate is removed without adding gates (c_0 is a constant, so no gate is added). Correctness: by induction on t the wires after step t carry psi_t = state after reading x_1..x_t. Consequence: any total-cost bound omega(N) for an explicit L_n with S(n) < N gives an omega(N) general circuit size lower bound for the same L_n. So G0002 is at least as hard as a superlinear general circuit lower bound for that explicit L_n; the restriction S(n) < N is discarded by unrolling.

question: Q-0b7da33369
statement: LEMMA C* (explicit constants, sharpens spec item 5 / subclaim C; does not close G0001 or G0002). Let m>=2, eta in (0,1], S=ceil(log2 m), R=floor((2-eta)S), Q={0..m-1}. For G>=0 let N=R+1+G and C(G,R)=(G+1)(16N^2)^G N^R (circuits with <=G fan-in-2 gates over a 16-function basis on R+1 inputs, R outputs). If Rm + log2 C(G,R) < 2m log2 m, then some pair (d0,d1) of maps Q->Q has CC_E(d0,d1) > G for EVERY injective E: Q->{0,1}^R. Proof: for fixed E the set P_E(G) of pairs realised under E with <=G gates injects into the circuits, so |P_E(G)| <= C(G,R); there are <= 2^{Rm} injective E; the union has size <= 2^{Rm} C(G,R) < m^{2m} = #pairs. Explicit choice G=floor(eta m/4): for m>=16 with (eta/2) m log2 m > 2m + 3 log2^2 m, the hypothesis holds (since N<=m, the sum is <= (2-eta/2) m log m + 2m + 3 log^2 m < 2m log m), so CC_E > eta m/4 for every injective E. Scope: only R <= (2-eta)S; R>=2S is not covered; no time-dependent or one-to-many codes; no explicit hard pair; no cost bound for G0002.

question: Q-0b7da33369
statement: Lemma (per-encoding counting). Fix m, an injective encoding E: Q -> {0,1}^R with |Q| = m, and fan-in-2 circuits over a fixed basis of 16 functions. A circuit with R+1 inputs (a selector bit and a code word) and G gates that has R outputs realises at most one pair (delta_0, delta_1) of maps Q -> Q under E. The number of such circuits is at most ((R+G+3)^2 * 16)^G * (R+G+3)^R. Since there are m^(2m) pairs, if G satisfies G*(2*log2(R+G+3)+4) + R*log2(R+G+3) < 2*m*log2(m), then some pair has circuit complexity > G under THIS E. For R = rho*m with constant rho in [0,1], the left side is G*(2*log2(m)+O(1)) + O(m*log m), so G > (1 - rho/2)*m - o(m) suffices. In particular, at R = 2S = 2*log2(m) (rho -> 0) the bound is G = Omega(m), and it holds up to R = Theta(m). This extends Claim C (which covered only R <= (2-eta)S = (2-eta)*log2(m)) to the full range R = O(m).

question: Q-0b7da33369
statement: PER-ENCODING PAIR BOUND. Let |Q|=m, let E: Q -> {0,1}^R be injective (fixed, not a union over encodings), and consider fan-in-2 circuits over a fixed basis of at most 16 binary gate types with R+1 inputs and R outputs and G gates. Let N(R,G) be the number of such circuits. If N(R,G) < m^(2m), then for this E some pair (delta_0, delta_1) of maps Q->Q has CC_E > G. Proof: each pair realised under E by a circuit of size <= G determines, via its values on the codes E(q), a unique pair, so choosing one realising circuit per pair gives an injection from realisable pairs into circuits of size <= G. There are m^(2m) pairs, so if N(R,G) < m^(2m) some pair is not realisable with size <= G. Count: N(R,G) <= (16 (R+G+1)^2)^G (R+G+2)^R, so log2 N <= G(4 + 2 log2(R+G+1)) + R log2(R+G+2). Consequences: (i) for R <= m and fixed eps>0, G = (1/2 - eps) m satisfies the inequality for all large m, since the left side is at most m(2 log m + 6) - eps m (2 log m + 8) < 2m log m; (ii) for R = 2 log2 m, G = (1 - eps) m works for large m. The silence at R >= 2S claimed in the spec came from the union bound over 2^(Rm) encodings, which this per-encoding statement does not need.

question: Q-0b7da33369
statement: LEMMA (counting threshold, CLAIMED, not reviewed). Let m >= 1, S = ceil(log2 m), R >= 2S+1. Then the number of injective maps E: Q -> {0,1}^R with |Q| = m is (2^R)_m >= m^{2m} = number of pairs (delta0, delta1) of maps Q -> Q. Proof: (2^R)_m >= (2^R - m)^m; m <= 2^S <= 2^{R-1} gives 2^R - m >= 2^{R-1} >= 2^{2S} >= m^2. Sharp: for m = 2^S >= 2, R = 2S fails since each factor m^2 - i < m^2. Scope: counting existence only; bounds no circuit cost; closes neither G0001 nor G0002; does not use S(n) < N. Status: bookkeeping relative to the open gap.

question: Q-0b7da33369
statement: LEMMA W (online width, exact; CLAIMED, no closes-field: width is a state count, not an update-cost bound). Setting: f on n variables, cut t = the first t variables form the prefix; width_t(f) = number of distinct residual functions f|prefix over the suffix assignments; W(f) = max_t width_t(f). (a) EQ_h, n = 2h, f = AND_{i<h}[x_i = x_{h+i}]. For t <= h: prefix p gives residual g_p(suffix) = AND_{i<t}[p_i = x_{h+i}] AND AND_{t<=i<h}[x_i = x_{h+i}]. For p != p' pick the suffix with x_{h+i} = p_i (i<t) and x_i = x_{h+i} (i>=t): g_p = 1 and g_{p'} = 0. So width_t = 2^t. For t > h the residual is 0 when the prefix has a mismatch, else the indicator of a suffix pattern c in {0,1}^(n-t), so width_t = 2^(n-t)+1 <= 2^(h-1)+1. Hence W(EQ_h) = 2^h exactly. (b) INDEX_k, n = k+2^k, address a = first k bits, data = last 2^k bits, f = x_{k+a}. For t <= k: residual determined by the address prefix; distinct prefixes give residuals differing on some data assignment, so width_t = 2^t. For t >= k+1 the address is fixed to a, so the residual is a constant (if the selected data bit is in the prefix) or the projection onto x_{k+a} (if unfixed); the residual set is {0, 1} plus one projection per unfixed data bit, so width_t = 2 + 2^k - (t-k), and width_{k+1} = 2^k+1 is the maximum. So W(INDEX_k) = 2^k+1 for k>=1, NOT 2^k: the earlier prediction omitted the two constant residuals. Consequence: online width is a representation-invariant STATE count (exact one-pass lower bound in stream order), so W(EQ_h) = 2^(n/2) = sqrt(N) is a state lower bound for stream-order realisations, not a superlinear circuit or update-cost bound. Verification: cm-6f538fe8121a4cd4 (per-cut values match both formulas for EQ n=6..14 and INDEX k=1..3) and an independent tuple-residual recount in the next experiment (k<=4, h<=4).

statement: CLAIMED: for S = ceil(log2 m), n = 2^S, log p(m) - log M(n) >= (pi*sqrt(2/3) - 2) sqrt(m) - O(log m), hence positive for all large m. question: Q-0b7da33369
statement: REPAIR of the class-counting threshold (session R1302). Let M = 2^S, m <= M, and let h(lambda) = min CC over permutations of {0,1}^S with cycle type lambda. Claim (finite part, exact scope S = 9..16): max_lambda h(lambda) >= g*(S), where g*(S) = max{g : (g+1)*2^{L(g)} < p(M)}, L(g) = (4g+S)*log2(4(g+S)), p = partition function. Proof: every cycle type needs one circuit of size <= g in the class, so the number of circuits of size <= g is at least p(M); a circuit of size g is encoded by at most (g+1)*2^{L(g)} bits-worth of descriptions, so if that is below p(M), some class has h > g. The reduction H(delta) = h(lambda(delta)) is the cycle-matching lemma (checked exhaustively at N = 4, 8). Exact check cm-78b701c9b375494a: g*(S) = 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 13, 19, 27 for S = 9..16, all >= sqrt(M)/(8S). For S = 3..8 the constant 1/8 fails (g* = 0), so the repaired statement is restricted to S >= 9. Asymptotic form (NOT yet proved with explicit constants): log2 p(M) ~ 3.70*sqrt(M) (Hardy-Ramanujan), so g*(S) = Omega(sqrt(M)/log M) = Omega(sqrt(m)/log m) for m <= M <= 2m. Open: an explicit partition-number bound with constants, and the S >= S0 threshold proof.

question: Q-0b7da33369
statement: PROOF. (1) Elementary partition bound: p(n) >= 2^{floor(sqrt(2n))-2} for n >= 2. Let k = floor(sqrt(2n)) - 1. Map each subset A of {2..k} with sum(A) <= n to the partition A plus (n - sum A) copies of 1. Since k(k+1)/2 <= n - sqrt(2n)/2 <= n, every subset qualifies; the non-1 parts recover A, so the map is injective. This gives 2^{k-1} = 2^{floor(sqrt(2n))-2} partitions. (2) Let g = floor(sqrt(M)/(4S)). For S >= 14, 4(g+S) <= sqrt(M)/S + 4S <= sqrt(M) (at S = 14: 56 <= 128, and the gap grows with S), so log2(4(g+S)) <= S/2. Also 4g+S <= sqrt(M)/S + S. Thus L(g) = (4g+S) log2(4(g+S)) <= sqrt(M)/2 + S^2/2, and log2(g+1) <= S/2. (3) Hence log2((g+1) 2^{L(g)}) <= sqrt(M)/2 + (S^2+S)/2. By (1) with n = M, p(M) >= 2^{sqrt(2M)-3}. The inequality sqrt(M)/2 + (S^2+S)/2 < sqrt(2)sqrt(M) - 3 is equivalent to f(S) := (sqrt2 - 1/2) 2^{S/2} - (S^2+S)/2 - 3 > 0. f(14) = 0.9142*128 - 108 = 9.0 > 0, and f(S+1) - f(S) = (sqrt2 - 1)(sqrt2 - 1/2)2^{S/2} - (S+1) > 0 for S >= 14 (the first term is 48 at S = 14 and grows exponentially), so f(S) > 0 for all S >= 14. (4) So (g+1) 2^{L(g)} < p(M). By the S0084 counting argument (distinct cycle types give p(M) distinct permutations; if every class had h <= g, each would have a circuit of size <= g, giving at most (g+1) 2^{L(g)} circuit descriptions), some cycle type has h >= g+1. QED. Restriction to 2^S states: subclaim A's lower bound for |Q| = m with m not a power of 2 still needs the sub-multiset case (open).

question: Q-0b7da33369
statement: LEMMA D (sharp sub-multiset bound, CLAIMED, self-made, not reviewed by this session). Let F be any function (possibly non-injective, partial on its image) on a set of N >= 1 points. Its cycles are pairwise disjoint, so their lengths form a partition lambda of some n <= N. Let P(lambda) = prod_i (k_i + 1), k_i = multiplicity of part i. Then: (a) the number of sub-multisets of lambda (as multisets of parts) is P(lambda); (b) P(lambda) <= exp(sqrt(2N) + 3/2) for every lambda of size <= N. PROOF OF (b): Let K = sqrt(2N) >= 1 and M = floor(K). For any k >= 0 and integer i >= 1, put a = i/K. Then phi_i(k) = log(k+1) - a k satisfies: if a <= 1 its maximum over k >= 0 is -log a - 1 + a = log(K/i) - 1 + i/K (at k+1 = 1/a); if a > 1 its maximum is 0 (at k = 0). Weak duality: sum_i log(k_i+1) = sum_i phi_i(k_i) + (1/K) sum_i i k_i <= sum_{i<=M} [log(K/i) - 1 + i/K] + n/K <= sum_{i<=M} [log(K/i) - 1 + i/K] + N/K. Estimate the first sum: S1 = sum_{i<=M} log(K/i) = M log K - log M! <= M log(K/M) + M <= K (using log M! >= M log M - M and that M log(K/M) + M is nondecreasing on [0,K]). S2 = -M + M(M+1)/(2K) <= -(K-1) + (K+1)/2 = 3/2 - K/2 (using M <= K, M >= K-1). Total: S1 + S2 + N/K <= K + 3/2 - K/2 + N/K = K/2 + N/K + 3/2 = sqrt(2N) + 3/2, since K/2 = N/K = sqrt(N/2). Hence log P(lambda) <= sqrt(2N) + 3/2. QED. CONSEQUENCE for gap (i): a single circuit F realises at most P(lambda) <= exp(sqrt(2N)+3/2) cycle types of size m (its m-subsets that are unions of its cycles), with N = 2^S < 2m, so at most exp(2 sqrt m + 3/2) types, versus p(m) = exp((pi sqrt(2/3) + o(1)) sqrt m) = exp((2.565+o(1)) sqrt m). This replaces the p(m) - 1 bound of S0090 (which is far too weak) and gives the counting bound #circuits >= exp((0.56 - o(1)) sqrt m). The sub-multiset count in (a) is over ALL sizes, so it upper-bounds the exact-size count used here. NOT PROVED HERE: the reduction from circuit codes to cycle types for the actual recoding model (time-varying / value-free unused codes), and any constant-explicit p(m) lower bound (verify Erdos 1942 constant before use).

question: Q-0b7da33369
statement: REDUCTION R1 (self-made, CLAIMED, not reviewable by this session). Fix an encoding psi: Q -> {0,1}^S (injective, |Q| = m, N = 2^S) and an update circuit F: {0,1}^S -> {0,1}^S that computes psi delta psi^{-1} on psi(Q). Then psi(Q) is F-invariant, because F(psi(q)) = psi(delta(q)) lies in psi(Q). So every F-cycle meeting psi(Q) lies wholly inside psi(Q), and the cycle type of delta is a sub-multiset of lambda(F), the cycle type of the function F on N points (cycles of a function are disjoint, so lambda(F) is a partition of some n <= N). Hence, for fixed psi, the set of cycle types of size m realised by one circuit F has size at most P(lambda(F)) <= exp(sqrt(2N)+3/2) by LEMMA D (S0091). With N = 2^S < 2m this is at most exp(2 sqrt(m) + 3/2). This closes the reduction from circuit codes to cycle types for a FIXED psi, which was the missing link in gap (i). NOT COVERED: (a) the per-delta statement needs a single delta fixed across psi, not a cycle-type class; (b) time-varying or one-to-many encodings; (c) the claim that every cycle type of size m must be realised is not re-derived here.

question: Q-0b7da33369
statement: LEMMA U (psi-uniform form, repair of the S0092 gap). Let S>=1, N=2^S, N/2 < m <= N, G>=1. Let Lambda_G be the set of partitions mu of m for which there exist a circuit F:{0,1}^S->{0,1}^S of size <= G and a set A subset {0,1}^S with |A|=m such that F restricted to A is a bijection A->A of cycle type mu. Then |Lambda_G| <= C_G * exp(2 sqrt(N) + 3/2), where C_G is the number of circuits of size <= G on S inputs, and log2 C_G <= c*G*log(G+S) for an absolute c. Hence if C_G * exp(2 sqrt(N)+3/2) < p(m), some mu |- m is not in Lambda_G. For such mu take any delta in Sym(Q), |Q|=m, of cycle type mu. Then for EVERY injection psi:Q->{0,1}^S, CC(psi delta psi^-1) > G, where the circuit size is that of any extension of the partial map to {0,1}^S. Proof. (i) A is invariant and F|A is a bijection, so each point of A lies on a cycle of the functional graph of F; the cycle type of F|A is therefore a sub-multiset of the cycle-type multiset lambda_F of F, whose total is <= N (pad with fixed points to total N). (ii) The number of sub-multisets of size m of a partition of N is prod_i (m_i+1) over distinct part sizes i with multiplicities m_i, and by Lemma D (S0091) this is <= exp(2 sqrt(N)+3/2). (iii) F does not depend on psi, so the union over circuits gives |Lambda_G| <= C_G * exp(2 sqrt(N)+3/2). (iv) mu not in Lambda_G excludes every F of size <= G simultaneously for all psi, since A = psi(Q) is one such set. Asymptotically, p(m) = exp(pi sqrt(2m/3)(1+o(1))) and log2 C_G = O(G log(G+S)) with S=log m, so G = c' sqrt(m)/log m gives the required inequality for large m. This gives Claim A (max over delta of min over psi) as Omega(sqrt(m)/log m) for m = 2^S-range large enough.

question: Q-0b7da33369
statement: LEMMA D* (kind LEMMA; closes gap G0050 part (a), i.e. the general proof of the Lemma D form used by S0097 and S0091). For every N>=1 and every multiset of positive part sizes with multiplicities m_i and total sum_i i*m_i <= N: prod_i (m_i+1) <= exp(sqrt(2N) - 0.29) < exp(sqrt(2N)). PROOF. Let s=sqrt(2N), K=round(s)>=1 (so |K-s|<=1/2). For real x>=0 and integer 1<=i<=K, the concave function log(1+x)-(i/K)x is maximised at x=K/i-1>=0, giving log(1+x) <= (i/K)x + g(i) with g(i)=log(K/i)-1+i/K >= 0 (since log t >= 1-1/t). For i>K, log(1+x) <= x <= (i/K)x. Put x=m_i and sum over all i: log prod(m_i+1) <= (1/K) sum_i i m_i + sum_{i=1}^K g(i) <= N/K + K log K - log K! - K + (K+1)/2. Stirling K! >= sqrt(2 pi K)(K/e)^K gives K log K - log K! <= K - (1/2) log(2 pi K). So the bound is <= N/K + K/2 + 1/2 - (1/2) log(2 pi K). Identity: N/K + K/2 = s + (K-s)^2/(2K) (since s^2=2N). With |K-s|<=1/2 and K>=1, (K-s)^2/(2K) <= 1/8. Hence the bound is <= s + 1/8 + 1/2 - (1/2) log(2 pi) = s - 0.294 (using log(2 pi)=1.8379). QED. Consequence for S0097: since p(m) >= exp(pi sqrt(2m/3))/(4 sqrt3 m) (Lehmer-type lower bound, source to be checked), and pi sqrt(N/3) - sqrt(2N) = 0.3996 sqrt N for m > N/2, choosing G = floor(eps sqrt N / S) with S=log2 N gives log C_G <= (c eps/2) sqrt N + O(S), so C_G exp(sqrt 2N) < p(m) for eps small and N large. This yields Claim A (Omega(sqrt m / log m)) for N/2 < m <= N and N >= N0. NOT PROGRESS on its own: a counting lower bound for the cycle type of one permutation, existential over the hard permutation; it does not transfer to G0002 (online cost).

question: Q-0b7da33369
statement: LEMMA R-repair (repairs the direction refuted in S0028; kind LEMMA, bookkeeping only, closes nothing). statement: REPAIR of S0038 (claimant: this session, claude-haiku-5-5; NOT cross-family reviewed). Let m>=4, eps in (0,1/2), L = log2 m, R = m, G = floor((1/2-eps)m). question: Q-0b7da33369
statement: LEMMA (per-encoding, R = 2S; supersedes the R=m and 'for some pair for every E' forms in S0038/S0112). Let m >= 64, S = ceil(log2 m), L = log2 m, R = 2S, G = floor(m/2). For every injective E: Q -> {0,1}^R (|Q| = m) there is a pair (delta0, delta1) of maps Q -> Q with CC_E > G. Proof: the number of fan-in-2 circuits over a 16-type basis on R+1 inputs and R outputs with G gates is N <= (16(R+G+1)^2)^G (R+G+2)^R, so log2 N <= G(4+2 log2(R+G+1)) + R log2(R+G+2). For m >= 64 one has R+G+1 <= m, R+G+2 <= m+1, R <= 2(L+1), so log2 N <= (m/2)(4+2L) + 2(L+2)^2 = mL + 2m + 2(L+2)^2. statement: LEMMA L-G0064 (CLAIMED, Haiku-authored, needs a non-Haiku review). For every integer S >= 13, with M = 2^S and g = floor(floor(sqrt(M))/(4S)): log2(g+1) + (4g+S)*log2(4(g+S)) < floor(sqrt(2M)) - 2. PROOF. statement: CANDIDATE LEMMA (sub-multiset case, obligation (i)). Let m >= 2, S = ceil(log2 m), M = 2^S, so m <= M <= 2m. For lambda |- m let pi_lambda be the permutation of {0,1}^S with cycle type lambda plus M-m fixed points. Distinct lambda give distinct cycle types, so there are p(m) classes. Proof sketch: put g = floor(sqrt(M)/(4S)). Every class needs a circuit of size <= g, so if (g+1)2^{L(g)} < p(m) then some class has h > g. Here L(g) = (4g+S)log2(4(g+S)) as in S0084, and the S0087(2)-(3) bounds give log2((g+1)2^{L(g)}) <= sqrt(M)/2 + (S^2+S)/2 <= sqrt(2m)/2 + (S^2+S)/2. By S0087(1), log2 p(m) >= sqrt(2m) - 3. The difference is at least sqrt(2m)/2 - (S^2+S)/2 - 3 > 0 under the stated condition. question: Q-0b7da33369
statement: LEMMA L (stationary cycle-type realisation, CONDITIONAL on S0091(b), which is still CLAIMED). Let m >= 2, S = ceil(log2 m), N = 2^S, so m <= N < 2m. Let Circ(G) be the fan-in-2 circuits over the fixed basis with S inputs and S outputs and at most G gates. For a circuit C, let lambda(C) be the multiset of lengths of the periodic cycles of the functional graph of C; it is a partition of some n <= N. Let T_G(m) be the set of cycle types mu of size m such that some C in Circ(G), some injective psi: Q -> {0,1}^S and some delta in Sym(Q) of type mu satisfy C(psi(q)) = psi(delta(q)) for all q. Then |T_G(m)| <= |Circ(G)| * exp(sqrt(2N)+3/2) <= |Circ(G)| * exp(2 sqrt(m) + 3/2). PROOF: if C realises (psi, delta), then A = psi(Q) is C-invariant and C restricted to A is a bijection, so A is a union of periodic cycles of C. Its cycle lengths form a sub-multiset nu of lambda(C) with |nu| = m, and nu = mu because C restricted to A is conjugate to delta. So mu is a sub-multiset of lambda(C), and by S0091(b) lambda(C) has at most exp(sqrt(2N)+3/2) sub-multisets. Summing over C gives the bound. COROLLARY: if |Circ(G)| exp(2 sqrt(m)+3/2) < p(m), some mu |- m is realised by no circuit of size <= G under any injective stationary psi, so for every delta of type mu and every psi, CC_psi(delta) > G. This is the quantifier exists-mu forall-delta forall-psi, so it gives max_delta min_psi CC >= G+1. With log|Circ(G)| <= G(4+2 log(S+G)) + S log(S+G) and log p(m) >= pi sqrt(2m/3) - O(log m), G = c sqrt(m)/log m with c < 0.56 works for large m, so H_1(m) = Omega(sqrt(m)/log m) for the stationary model.

question: Q-0b7da33369
statement: PROOF. (a) Im psi is C-invariant, since C(psi(q)))=psi(delta(q)) lies in Im psi, and C restricted to Im psi equals psi delta psi^-1, a bijection. So Im psi is a union of cycles of the functional graph of C, and psi carries the cycles of delta onto distinct cycles of C. Hence the cycle type mu(delta) of delta on Q is a sub-multiset of lambda(C), the cycle type of C on its periodic points, a partition of some n<=N. (b) Let lambda be a partition of n<=N with multiplicities k_i. The number of sub-multisets of lambda is P(lambda)=prod(k_i+1). Put K=sqrt(2N), M=floor(K), a_i=i/K, phi_i(k)=log(k+1)-a_i k. For i<=M the maximum over integers k>=0 of phi_i is log(K/i)-1+i/K. For i>M the maximum is 0, since log(k+1)<=k<=a_i k. Weak duality: sum_i log(k_i+1)=sum_i phi_i(k_i)+(1/K) sum_i i k_i <= sum_{i<=M}[log(K/i)-1+i/K] + n/K. Use log M! >= M log M - M and that x log(K/x)+x is nondecreasing on (0,K] to get sum_{i<=M} log(K/i) <= K. Use M<=K, M>=K-1 to get sum_{i<=M}(-1+i/K) <= 3/2 - K/2. Total <= K/2 + N/K + 3/2 = sqrt(2N)+3/2, since K/2 = N/K = sqrt(N/2). So P(lambda) <= exp(sqrt(2N)+3/2). (c) Let B be the set of cycle types mu(delta) for which some psi gives CC_psi(delta)<=G. By (a), each mu in B is a sub-multiset of lambda(C) for some C of size <=G. By (b), |B| <= (G+1) N(S,G) exp(sqrt(2N)+3/2), where N(S,G) <= (16(S+G)^2)^G (S+G)^S counts circuit descriptions with G gates (each gate: type and two operands among <=S+G earlier nodes; each output: one node among <=S+G). (d) If p(m) > (G+1) N(S,G) exp(sqrt(2N)+3/2), some cycle type mu is not in B. Every delta of type mu has min over psi of CC_psi(delta) > G, so H(m) > G. (e) Asymptotics with G=floor(sqrt(m)/(2 log2 m)): ln N(S,G) <= G(ln m + 4.16) + S ln(2 sqrt m) <= 0.3466 sqrt(m)(1+o(1)) + O(log^2 m), using ln m / log2 m = ln 2. sqrt(2N) < 2 sqrt(m). By Hardy-Ramanujan (KNOWN, cited, not re-proved here), ln p(m) >= (pi sqrt(2/3)-o(1)) sqrt(m) = 2.565 sqrt(m)(1-o(1)). The gap is about 0.21 sqrt(m) minus O(log^2 m), so the inequality holds for all m >= m0. The threshold m0 is computed in the attached experiment (verification of the constants, not a proof of the threshold). SCOPE: stationary model only (one fixed psi per delta, one fixed circuit, values off the code image arbitrary, covers value-free unused codes). NOT COVERED: time-varying circuits, several codes per abstract state, and update-time versus gate count in a streaming system. Barrier label (diagnostic only): counting argument, not natural in the Razborov-Rudich sense; it is a lower bound for a single permutation's recoding, not a learner.

statement: LEMMA S0114-analytic (CLAIMED, session R1454, claude-haiku-5-5). Let m >= 64, L = log2 m, S = ceil(L), R = 2S, G = floor(m/2). For every injective E: Q -> {0,1}^R with |Q| = m, there is a pair (delta_0, delta_1) of maps Q->Q with CC_E > G, for circuits with fan-in 2, a fixed basis of at most 16 gate types, R+1 inputs and R outputs. PROOF. By S0038 it suffices that N(R,G) < m^(2m), where log2 N <= G(4+2 log2(R+G+1)) + R log2(R+G+2). Since S <= L+1, we have R <= 2L+2 and 2S+2 <= m/2 for m >= 64, so R+G+2 <= m and R+G+1 <= m, which gives log2(R+G+2) <= L and log2(R+G+1) <= L. Hence log2 N <= (m/2)(4+2L) + (2L+2)L = m(L+2) + 2L(L+1). The target 2mL exceeds this iff 2L(L+1) < m(L-2) = 2^L (L-2). This holds at L = 6 (84 < 256). For L >= 6 the LHS ratio (L+2)/L is at most 4/3 while the RHS ratio 2(L-1)/(L-2) is at least 2, so it holds for all L >= 6. QED. Scope: R = 2 ceil(log2 m), G = floor(m/2), m >= 64 (m a power of 2 in the formula; general m via L = log2 m). Existential in the pair, per encoding. Does not by itself close G0001 or G0002.

question: Q-0b7da33369
statement: PROOF. Let T be the set of maps delta' on Q whose transition on the codes E0(Q) is realised by a fan-in-2 circuit of size <= G (16-type basis, R+1 inputs, R outputs). Each circuit determines at most one delta', so |T| <= N(R,G). A map delta is bad iff some conjugate pi delta pi^-1 lies in T for some pi in Sym(Q). Hence the number of bad deltas is at most m! * |T| <= m! * N(R,G) < m^m = number of maps Q -> Q, so a good delta exists. Asymptotics: log2 m! = m log2 m - 1.4427 m + O(log m); for G <= m/(2S) we have log2(R+G+1) <= 1+log2 m, so log2 N <= m + 3m/log2 m + O(log^2 m). Thus log2 m! + log2 N <= m log2 m - 0.44 m + 3m/log2 m + O(log^2 m) < m log2 m for all sufficiently large m (explicit m0 not computed here). QED.
