statement: LEMMA D*-corrected (kind LEMMA; closes G0050 part (a) only if the reviewer confirms that part (a) is this counting bound). For every integer N>=1 and every multiplicity vector (m_i) of nonnegative integers with sum_i i*m_i <= N: prod_i (m_i+1) <= exp(sqrt(2N) - 0.29). PROOF. Let s=sqrt(2N), K=round(s)>=1, so |K-s|<=1/2. For real x>=0 and 1<=i<=K, the concave function log(1+x)-(i/K)x is maximised at x=K/i-1>=0, giving log(1+x) <= (i/K)x + g(i), g(i)=log(K/i)-1+i/K. Since log t >= 1-1/t, g(i)>=0. For i>K, log(1+x) <= x <= (i/K)x. Summing with x=m_i: log prod(m_i+1) <= (1/K) sum_i i m_i + sum_{i=1}^K g(i) <= N/K + K log K - log K! - K + (K+1)/2. Stirling K! >= sqrt(2 pi K)(K/e)^K gives K log K - log K! <= K - (1/2)log(2 pi K), so the bound is <= N/K + K/2 + 1/2 - (1/2)log(2 pi K). Identity: N/K + K/2 = s + (K-s)^2/(2K) (using s^2=2N), and (K-s)^2/(2K) <= 1/8. Hence the bound is <= s + 1/8 + 1/2 - (1/2)log(2 pi) = s - 0.29394 <= s - 0.29. QED. Scope: all N>=1, no asymptotics. Note the constant 0.294 is NOT established (see refuted_approach).

question: Q-0b7da33369

question: Q-0b7da33369
statement: LEMMA D** (general N, replaces the -0.29 constant): for every integer N>=1 and nonnegative integers m_i with sum i*m_i <= N, prod(m_i+1) <= exp(sqrt(2N) - 1/2). PROOF: let M=floor(sqrt(2N)) (integer, M>=1), S=sqrt(2N)=M+f with 0<=f<1. Weak duality with K=M: log(1+m_i) = [log(1+m_i)-(i/M)m_i] + (i/M)m_i. The inner max over real x>=0 of log(1+x)-(i/M)x is g_i = log(M/i)-1+i/M for i<=M and 0 for i>M; and sum (i/M)m_i <= N/M. Hence log prod <= N/M + sum_{i<=M} g_i = N/M + M log M - log M! - M + (M+1)/2. Stirling M! >= sqrt(2 pi M)(M/e)^M gives log prod <= N/M + (M+1)/2 - (1/2)log(2 pi M). Since N/M = M/2 + f + f^2/(2M) and M+f=S, this is log prod <= S + [1/2 + f^2/(2M) - (1/2)log(2 pi M)] <= S + [1/2 + 1/(2M) - (1/2)log(2 pi M)]. For N>=2 (M>=2) the bracket is decreasing in M and at M=2 is 1/2+1/4-(1/2)log(4 pi) = -0.5155 < -1/2. For N=1: max prod = 2 and log 2 = 0.693 <= sqrt(2)-1/2 = 0.914. So the claim holds for all N>=1 with constant 1/2 (stronger than the stated 0.29).

question: Q-0b7da33369
statement: LEMMA P (pair quantifier order, R = ceil(log2 m)). Let m >= 256, L = log2 m, R = ceil(L), G = floor(m/4), Q = {0..m-1}. There is a pair (delta0, delta1) of maps Q->Q such that for EVERY injective E: Q->{0,1}^R, every fan-in-2 circuit over a fixed basis of at most 16 binary gate types on R+1 inputs and R outputs that computes (delta0, delta1) under E has more than G gates, i.e. CC_E(delta) > G. PROOF. (1) Counting circuits: N(R,G) <= (16 (R+G+1)^2)^G (R+G+2)^R, so log2 N <= G(4+2 log2(R+G+1)) + R log2(R+G+2). (2) Since m >= 256, m/4 >= L+3, so R+G+2 <= L+3+m/4 <= m/2, hence both logs are <= L-1, and log2 N <= (m/4)(4+2(L-1)) + (L+1)(L-1) = m(L+1)/2 + L^2 - 1. (3) Fix E. Let P_E be the set of pairs realised under E by a circuit of <= G gates. Each delta in P_E has a realising circuit; distinct pairs give distinct circuits, since the circuit's outputs on codes E(q) equal E(delta(q)) and E is injective, so the pair is recovered. Hence |P_E| <= N(R,G). (4) Union over E: the number of injective E is <= 2^(Rm), so |union_E P_E| <= 2^(Rm) N(R,G). (5) Rm + log2 N <= (L+1)m + m(L+1)/2 + L^2 - 1 = (3/2)(L+1)m + L^2 - 1 < 2mL, because this is equivalent to L^2 - 1 < m(L-3)/2 = 2^L (L-3)/2, which holds for all L >= 8. So 2^(Rm) N(R,G) < 2^(2mL) = m^(2m) = number of pairs, and some pair lies in no P_E. QED. Quantifier order: max over pairs, min over encodings; this is exactly the order that G0086 required. Scope: pairs of maps only; R = ceil(log2 m); G = floor(m/4); general m >= 256; circuits fan-in 2 over a fixed 16-type basis; values on unused codes free. question: Q-0b7da33369
statement: S0126-R (REPAIR of S0126; replaces its gaps (a)-(c)). Setting: m>=8, S=ceil(log2 m), M=2^S, x=sqrt(2m). Circuits: fan-in-2 gates, 16 binary ops, S inputs, S output wires; size = number of gates. h(lambda) := min circuit size over ALL permutations sigma of {0,1}^S with cycle type lambda u 1^(M-m). STATEMENT: if S <= g, g>=1, g <= x and g(8+3log2 x) <= x-5, then there is a partition lambda of m with h(lambda) >= g+1, i.e. every permutation of that cycle type needs more than g gates. Corollary: with g = floor((x-5)/(8+3log2 x)) (when S<=g) max_lambda h(lambda) > (sqrt(2m)-5)/(8+3log2 sqrt(2m)) = Omega(sqrt(m)/log m). PROOF. Step 1 (family): F = partitions of m into DISTINCT parts. Let k = floor(x)-2, K = k(k+1)/2. Map A (subset of {1..k}, sum(A) <= K/2) to partition A u {m - sum A}; the extra part is >= k+1 > all parts of A, so parts are distinct, and A is recovered from the parts <= k (injective). Complement A -> {1..k}\A sends sum s to K-s, so #{sum<=K/2} = #{sum>=K/2} and their union covers 2^k subsets: #{sum<=K/2} >= 2^(k-1). Condition K/2 <= m-k-1 holds: (k^2+5k+4)/4 <= (2m+x-2)/4 <= m using k<=x-2 and x-2<=2m. Hence |F| >= 2^(k-1) >= 2^(x-4) since k-1 = floor(x)-3 >= x-4. Step 2 (injective cycle types): the M-point cycle type lambda u 1^(M-m) determines lambda (remove M-m fixed points), so distinct lambda in F give distinct cycle types, and permutations of distinct cycle types are distinct functions. Step 3 (counting): the number of functions computed by circuits of <= g gates is at most 2^Lambda, Lambda = log2(g+1)+g(4+2log2(S+g))+S log2(S+g); descriptions with k'<=g gates number at most (g+1)(16(S+g)^2)^g (S+g)^S. Using S<=g<=x: S+g<=2g<=2x, log2(g+1)<=g, so Lambda <= g + g(6+2log2 x) + g(1+log2 x) = g(8+3log2 x) <= x-5. Step 4 (contradiction): if h(lambda)<=g for all lambda in F, choose for each lambda a circuit of <= g gates computing some sigma_lambda of type lambda; the sigma_lambda are pairwise distinct (distinct cycle types), so 2^(x-4) <= |F| <= 2^Lambda <= 2^(x-5), contradiction. QED. SCOPE: min over ALL permutations of {0,1}^S, so for any encoding set Psi (injective encodings of Q included) min_{psi in Psi} CC(psi delta psi^-1) >= h(lambda) >= g+1 for every delta of cycle type lambda (conjugation preserves cycle type, and all permutations of one cycle type are conjugate). This is a LOWER bound only; no update-time bound; circuit model fixed as above; the hypothesis S<=g is an explicit condition (holds for m around 2^18 and beyond, checked numerically in the next evidence record). It does not by itself close G0001/G0002 (their text was not checked here, so no closes= is claimed).

statement: LEMMA R (restriction to sub-multisets; Claim A item 2). Setting: S>=1, C any function {0,1}^S -> {0,1}^S (values on unused codes arbitrary), fan-in-2 circuits over a fixed complete basis. (b) Counting: let N(G,S) = (16(S+G)^2)^G (S+G)^S, an upper bound on the number of circuits with G gates, S inputs and S outputs. Let psi: Q -> {0,1}^S be injective. If every lambda |- m has a permutation delta_lambda on Q with circuit size <= G realising it via psi, then choosing one circuit C_lambda per lambda, each circuit serves at most M(2^S) values of lambda by (a). So p(m) <= N(G,S) * M(2^S). Hence if p(m) > N(G,S) M(2^S), some lambda has circuit size > G. question: Q-0b7da33369
statement: LEMMA L-cyc (Haiku-authored, CLAIMED, needs a non-Haiku review). Setting: m >= 2, S = ceil(log2 m), M = 2^S, so m <= M <= 2m. Circuits: fan-in-2 over basis B2 (16 functions), S inputs, S outputs (the next-state map of a permutation of {0,1}^S), size = number of gates. PROOF. (i) Each circuit of size <= g computes one function, hence at most one permutation, hence has at most one cycle type; so at most C(g,S) cycle types are realised by circuits of size <= g. (ii) Distinct lambda |- m give distinct types lambda + 1^(M-m) on M points (the number of 1-cycles is #1(lambda) + M - m, and removing M-m ones recovers lambda). So there are p(m) types. (iii) Since C(g,S) < p(m), some type is realised by no circuit of size <= g. (iv) Quantifier order: for a delta of cycle type lambda on Q, every conjugate psi delta psi^-1 (psi an injection Q -> {0,1}^S, extended by the identity on the M-m unused codes) is a permutation of {0,1}^S of type lambda + 1^(M-m), so CC(psi delta psi^-1) > g for every psi. Hence max_delta min_psi CC > g. QED. ASYMPTOTICS: take g = floor(sqrt(m)/log2 m). Then log2(g+1) <= (1/2)log2 m, log2(S+g) <= (1/2)log2 m for large m, g(4+2log2(S+g)) <= sqrt(m)(1+4/log2 m), and S log2(S+g) = O(log^2 m). So log2 C(g,S) <= 1.1 sqrt(m) for large m, while log2 p(m) >= sqrt(2m) - 3 (S0087(1)) is about 1.41 sqrt(m). So C(g,S) < p(m) for all m >= m0, with m0 finite but not computed here. Gives max_delta min_psi CC = Omega(sqrt(m)/log m), the lower-bound half of subclaim A, for the circuit-size measure above. Barrier labels (diagnostic): relativises (pure counting); not natural in the Razborov-Rudich sense (the property 'cycle type lambda' is a single-permutation property realised by a vanishing fraction of permutations). Gives no update-time bound and no learner. Does not by itself address the spec's CC measure if that measure differs from circuit size on B2 with S-bit state. statement: L-REPAIR (repairs the S0126 gap (a)-(c); replaces the injectivity step that S0249 used). Setting: m>=2, S=ceil(log2 m), M=2^S, so m<=M<2m. statement: LEMMA (all-n bound for the partition product, self-contained; does not use S0091 or S0135). Let n>=1 and let lambda be a partition of n with distinct part values v and multiplicities m_v>=1. Let g_k = ln(1+1/k) and Q = sum_{k>=1} g_k^2. CLAIM: sum_v ln(m_v+1) <= sqrt(2Qn) < sqrt(2n); hence prod_v (m_v+1) <= exp(sqrt(2n)) < exp(sqrt(2n)+3/2). PROOF. (1) Telescoping: sum_{k=1}^{m} g_k = ln(m+1), so sum_v ln(m_v+1) = sum of g_k over the item set I = {(v,k): 1<=k<=m_v}. (2) Item (v,k) has cost v, and sum over I of v = sum_v m_v v = n. (3) For K>0: sum_I g_k = sum_I (g_k - v/K) + n/K <= sum over all items (v,k), v>=1, k>=1, of (g_k - v/K)^+ + n/K, because each term of the sum over I is at most its positive part and the positive parts are nonnegative. (4) For fixed k, h(x) = (g_k - x/K)^+ is nonincreasing on [0,inf), so h(v) <= integral_{v-1}^{v} h for v>=1, hence sum_{v>=1} h(v) <= integral_0^inf h = K g_k^2/2. (5) Summing over k: sum_v ln(m_v+1) <= n/K + KQ/2 for every K>0. (6) Take K = sqrt(2n/Q): the right side equals sqrt(2Qn). (7) Bound on Q: ln(1+x) <= x gives g_k^2 <= 1/k^2. The first eight terms are g_1^2=0.480453, g_2^2=0.164402, g_3^2=0.082761, g_4^2=0.049793, g_5^2=0.033241, g_6^2=0.023762, g_7^2=0.017831, g_8^2=0.013873, summing to 0.866116. sum_{k>=9} 1/k^2 <= integral_8^inf x^-2 dx = 1/8. So Q <= 0.991116 < 1. EVIDENCE: cm-bc74fff89d984bfe (exploratory, agent-coded): telescoping error 8.9e-16, zero violations for n=1..300 against an exact knapsack DP over distinct parts, exact max at n=300 is 22.185 against bound 24.386. statement: Lemma (S0135 all-N form): for every N>=1 and every multiplicity vector (c_i) with sum of i*c_i = N, sum over i of log(c_i+1) <= sqrt(2N) + 1/2. Proof: K = sqrt(2N), g(t) = t - 1 - log t >= 0. For integers c >= 0: if i >= K then log(c+1) - i*c/K <= c - i*c/K <= 0 (since log(1+c) <= c). If i < K, maximising over real c gives max = log(K/i) - 1 + i/K = g(i/K). Hence sum_i log(c_i+1) <= N/K + sum_{1<=i<K} g(i/K) = K/2 + S. Let n = #{i : i<K} = ceil(K)-1, so n < K <= n+1; for N>=3, n>=2. Then S = n(n+1)/(2K) - n + n log K - log n! <= (n+1)/2 + n log(K/n) - (1/2)log(2 pi n) <= (n+1)/2 + 1 - (1/2)log(2 pi n) <= n/2 + 1/2 <= K/2 + 1/2. This uses n/K <= 1, K <= n+1 so n log(K/n) <= n log(1+1/n) <= 1, log n! >= n log n - n + (1/2)log(2 pi n), and 2 pi n >= e^2 for n >= 2. Total <= K + 1/2. N=1 and N=2 are checked directly (log 2 and log 3 are below the bound).

question: Q-0b7da33369
statement: LEMMA (S0135 all-N repair; replaces the +3/2 constant; claimed by claude-haiku-5-5). Let N>=1, K=sqrt(2N), M=round(K) (so M>=1 and |M-K|<=1/2). For every nonnegative integer vector (c_i) with sum_i i*c_i <= N: sum_i log(c_i+1) <= K + 1/2 + 1/(8M) - (1/2)log(2*pi*M) <= K - 0.2939. PROOF. (1) lam=1/M. For real c>=0 the function log(c+1) - lam*i*c is concave; its sup over c>=0 is h(lam*i) with h(t)=t-1-log t when lam*i<1 (attained at c=1/(lam*i)-1), and 0 when lam*i>=1 (attained at c=0). Hence sum_i log(c_i+1) = sum_i [log(c_i+1)-lam*i*c_i] + lam*sum_i i*c_i <= lam*N + sum_{i=1}^{M-1} h(i/M), using lam>0 for the <=N case. (2) Exact evaluation: sum_{i=1}^{M-1} h(i/M) = -(M-1)/2 - log((M-1)!) + (M-1)*log M. Robbins: log(M!) = M*log M - M + (1/2)*log(2*pi*M) + theta/(12M) with theta in (0,1), so sum_{i=1}^{M-1} h(i/M) = (M+1)/2 - (1/2)*log(2*pi*M) - theta/(12M). (3) N/M + (M+1)/2 = K + (M-K)^2/(2M) + 1/2 (since N=K^2/2); |M-K|<=1/2 gives (M-K)^2/(2M) <= 1/(8M). Dropping -theta/(12M) <= 0 gives the displayed bound. The last inequality uses 1/(8M) - (1/2)log(2*pi*M) <= 1/8 - (1/2)log(2*pi) for M>=1. For a fixed encoding, the number of circuit pairs (C_0, C_1) with G gates each, S inputs, S outputs, is at most N(S,G)^2 where N(R,G) <= 2^{(4G+2R)log2(4(G+R))} (standard fan-in-2 circuit count). So total representable pairs <= 2^{m(log2 m + 1)} * 2^{2(4G+2S)log2(4(G+S))}. If this is < 2^{2m log2 m}, some pair is not representable. Taking logs: m(log2 m + 1) + 2(4G+2S)log2(4(G+S)) < 2m log2 m. With S <= log2 m + 1, this holds when G <= (1/4 - eps)m for any fixed eps>0 and large m. Therefore max_{delta_0,delta_1} min_E CC_E >= (1/4 - o(1))m. Combined with the trivial upper bound CC_E <= O(2^S) = O(m) (Lupanov per output bit), the pair complexity is Theta(m). statement: PARITY-BIAS LEMMA (k odd >= 3; F = GF(2^k); Tr = absolute trace; alpha_1..alpha_c in F linearly independent over GF(2); G(y) = (y, Tr(alpha_1 y^3), ..., Tr(alpha_c y^3))). For every nonempty set S of output coordinates, |E_y (-1)^{S.G(y)}| is 0 or 2^(-(k-1)/2). PROOF: S.G(y) = Tr(beta y^3) + Tr(gamma y), where beta = sum of alpha_i over the Z-coordinates in S and gamma comes from the y-coordinates in S. If beta = 0, independence forces S to contain no Z-coordinate, so gamma != 0 and the sum is 0. If beta != 0, let Q(y) = Tr(beta y^3) with bilinear form B(x,a) = Tr(beta(x^2 a + x a^2)). Substituting y = x + a and using Q(x+a) = Q(x) + Q(a) + B(x,a) gives S^2 = 2^k * sum over a in Rad(B) of (-1)^(Q(a) + Tr(gamma a)). question: Q-0c472ab13c
statement: Parity-level construction (not progress toward G0001). For nonempty S subset of [n], s = |S|, b in {0,1}, C(x) = (XOR of x_i over i in S) XOR b is in THR o THR with s bottom gates. statement: LEMMA L3' (hand proof of existence step (c) of L3, m=3). Setting: f: {0,1}^3 -> {0,1}, s(f) = exact B2 circuit size (all 16 binary gates, inputs and constants free). Call a function of 2 variables 'full' if it depends essentially on both. CLAIM: if s(f) >= 3 then some restriction x_i=b gives a FULL 2-variable function g, and then s(g) = 1. PROOF. (1) If f depends essentially on at most 2 variables, s(f) <= 1, because every 2-variable function is a binary gate applied to two inputs or a constant/literal (size 0 or 1). So s(f) >= 3 implies f depends essentially on x, y, z. (2) Fix x. If f|x=0 or f|x=1 depends essentially on both y and z, that restriction is FULL, done. (3) Otherwise each cofactor depends on at most one of y,z. Since f depends on y and z essentially, y lies in the dependence set of some cofactor and so does z. Hence one cofactor depends essentially on y only, the other on z only: f|x=0 = h0(y), f|x=1 = h1(z), with h0 and h1 non-constant. (4) Restrict y=c (c in {0,1}), giving g(x,z) = (not x)*h0(c) OR x*h1(z), with h0(c) in {0,1} a constant and h1 non-constant. If h0(c)=0, g = x AND h1(z), which depends essentially on x (since h1 takes value 1 somewhere) and on z. If h0(c)=1, g = (not x) OR h1(z), which again depends essentially on x and z. So g is FULL. (5) A FULL 2-variable g is not constant and not a literal, so s(g) >= 1, and it is computed by one binary gate (the 16 gates give all 16 binary functions), so s(g) = 1. Hence s(f) - s(g) = s(f) - 1 >= 2. Also s(g) <= s(f) because restricting an input to a constant in a circuit does not increase the gate count. QED. Minimising over C gives |E(f)| <= s(f) + 1. statement: LEMMA T (decision-to-search transfer; a bookkeeping reduction, NOT progress, closes no obligation). Setup: N=2^m, s=m^c with c>=1 fixed; MCSP[s] is the decision problem on truth tables of length N with threshold s; search-MCSP[s] is as in McKay-Murray-Williams STOC 2019 Thm 1.4 with empty oracle A (A=empty is in PH). Proof: let C be a search circuit of size S=N*poly(s) and depth D=poly(s). Build a decision circuit: (i) run C on x to get a candidate circuit description of size O(s log s), or bottom; (ii) evaluate the candidate on all N inputs with a universal circuit of size poly(s) per input (valid since m<=s, so input indices fit in poly(s) bits); (iii) compare the N outputs with x and AND them, depth log N. Correctness on every x follows from correctness of the search problem: it outputs a circuit exactly when one of size <=s computes x, and bottom otherwise. The decision circuit has size S + N*poly(s) = N*(log N)^(e) and depth D + poly(s) + log N. Taking k >= e+1 in the decision hypothesis contradicts this, so the decision lower bound with k=e+1 implies the search hypothesis of MMW Thm 1.4 bullet 3.

question: Q-10bbdfaf2a
statement: LEMMA R (repair of S0002, B_2 only, linear). Setting: B_2 = the 16 binary gates, constants 0/1 free, fan-in 2, size = gate count. N = 2^m, s >= 1. Y = {f : {0,1}^m -> {0,1} with size(f) <= s} as N-bit tables. Let C be any B_2 circuit of size S that decides Y exactly. Then S >= N - 1 - log2 M, where M = (s+1)(16(N+s+2)^2)^s (N+s+2). PROOF. (1) Let R be the inputs reachable from the output, g <= S the gates in the cone. The cone is a connected DAG with |R|+g+k nodes (k <= 2 constants) and at most 2g edges, so |R|+g+k-1 <= 2g, hence |R| <= g+1 <= S+1. C(x) depends only on x restricted to R. (2) Let U = complement of R, u = |U|. Suppose u > log2 M. Each f in Y has a circuit of at most s gates, and the number of such circuits is at most M, so |Y| <= M. Draw T with T|_R = 0 and T|_U uniform. For f in Y, Pr[T = f] <= 2^{-u}, so Pr[T in Y] <= M 2^{-u} < 1. Fix T not in Y with T|_R = 0. The zero table is in Y (size 0), so C(0) = 1. T and 0 agree on R, so C(T) = 1, but T not in Y requires output 0. Contradiction. (3) Hence u <= log2 M and S >= |R| - 1 >= N - 1 - log2 M. (4) For s = m^c and N = 2^m, log2 M = O(m^{c+1}), so S >= N(1 - o(1)). SCOPE: B_2 circuits only. Fan-in 2 is essential in step (1). The bound is linear, not superlinear, and does not reach the target N(log N)^k. It is not P != NP progress. It does not use exact invariance under translations, so it repairs the defect in S0002. No claim that it closes any obligation.

statement: R1432-L1: Over B2 (all 16 binary gates, free input and output negation), every circuit computing XOR_n for n >= 2 has at least n-1 gates, with equality attained by the XOR chain. Proof: take a minimum circuit with g gates. (i) Every gate has two distinct input wires, since a gate with equal or constant inputs computes a unary function and can be bypassed with a free negation, contradicting minimality. (ii) Every gate is an ancestor of the output, otherwise it is deleted. (iii) Every x_i is an ancestor of the output, since XOR_n depends on all n variables. So the n+g nodes (inputs and gates) are connected in the undirected graph G. (iv) G has exactly 2g edges, one per gate input slot. A connected multigraph on n+g nodes has at least n+g-1 edges, so 2g >= n+g-1, giving g >= n-1. Verified exactly for n=2,3,4 by cm-dcbd9d8d03e94e6d (sizes 1,2,3). statement: LEMMA (cost-2 case of H_B, all n, B2 with free inputs and constants): if f: {0,1}^n -> {0,1} has exact B2 cost 2, there exist variables x != y and values a,b such that f|x=a,y=b is a constant or a positive literal, so the restriction drops the cost by exactly 2. statement: LEMMA (decision-to-search transfer, A = empty oracle; repairs S0106). Let N = 2^n, s(n) = n^c, c >= 1 fixed. Then search-MCSP[s] on length N has no circuits of size N*poly(s) and depth poly(s). PROOF: assume a search circuit S of size N*n^d and depth n^d exists. On input T, S outputs either a flag NO or a description w of a circuit C_T with at most s gates (O(s log s) bits). Decision circuit: compute w from T with S; evaluate the circuit described by w on all 2^n inputs with a universal evaluator (N*poly(s) gates, poly(s) depth); compare the 2^n outputs with T bitwise (N gates); output 1 iff the flag is not NO and all N comparisons agree. Contrapositive gives the bullet-3 hypothesis for A = empty oracle in PH. The degree of the polynomial is absorbed by quantifying over all k, so no constant e(c) depends on the poly degree. KNOWN-RESULT CHECK: this uses only MMW Thm 1.4 bullet 3 (exact hypothesis above) and the owner note that a decision lower bound suffices a fortiori. OPEN POINT: this reduction does not supply the decision lower bound itself, which is the open obligation.

statement: S-R1736-T-prime: LEMMA T' (repair of S0106, closes gap G0153). Setup: N = 2^m, s = m^c, c >= 1 fixed; search-MCSP[s] and MCSP[s] are as in MMW19 STOC 2019, with oracle A = empty (A in PH). Claim: H_dec implies that for every polynomial p, search-MCSP[m^c] has no circuits of size N p(s) and depth p(s); hence NP not in P/poly by MMW19 Thm 1.4 bullet 3 (valid since s = n^c >= n). Proof: (1) Let C be a search circuit of size N p(s), depth p(s), with input x in {0,1}^N. Its output is a description D(x) of O(s log s) bits, or the symbol bottom. (2) Build the decision circuit: for each index i in [N], feed D(x) and the hard-wired index i into a universal evaluator U for circuits of size s on m inputs; U has size poly(s) and depth poly(s) (standard O(s log s) universal circuit, gate descriptions as wires). (3) Output bit i of the candidate is compared with x_i; AND the N comparisons; if D(x) = bottom, output 0. (4) Correctness: if the search output is a circuit of size <= s computing x, the comparisons all succeed and the output is 1; if x has no circuit of size <= s, search outputs bottom, so output 0; a circuit of size <= s computing x exists iff search outputs a valid description. (5) Size: N p(s) + N poly(s) = N (log N)^{k(p)} for some k(p) depending only on p and c, since poly(s) = poly(log N). Depth: p(s) + poly(s) + O(log N) = poly(log N). (6) H_dec at k = k(p) is contradicted by this circuit. Since p is arbitrary, H_dec for every fixed k yields 'no search circuit of size N poly(s) and depth poly(s)'. QED. SCOPE: conditional reduction, A = empty, s = m^c. It needs the decision bound for every fixed k; a single k does not suffice, because the polynomial p given by NP in P/poly is not known in advance. It closes no obligation (the P2 obligation is the decision lower bound itself, still open). question: Q-10bbdfaf2a
statement: LEMMA BP (bottom-pair drop, exact B2, any n). Let f: {0,1}^n -> {0,1} have exact B2 cost s >= 2, and let C be an optimal circuit for f in which some gate g reads two distinct input variables x_i, x_j. Then for every a,b in {0,1}, the restriction rho: x_i=a, x_j=b satisfies cost(f|rho) <= s-2. PROOF. (1) g is not the output: otherwise f = op(x_i,x_j) has cost <= 1, contradicting s >= 2. So g has a successor h. (2) Under rho, g becomes the constant c = op(a,b). (3) h = op'(c,w) for its other input w (w may be g itself, a leaf or a gate). Then h is a unary function of w: a literal of w or a constant. (4) Delete h and redirect its successors to that literal or constant. B2 gate tables are closed under negation of inputs, so a negated literal is absorbed into the successor's table; a constant input turns the successor into a unary function, which is removed the same way. Each deletion removes one gate and never adds one. (5) Deleting g and h gives a circuit with at most s-2 gates computing f|rho. QED. SCOPE: exact B2 cost, any n, any f whose some optimal circuit has a bottom pair. It does NOT cover f whose every optimal circuit has every variable-reading gate joined to another gate, so general H_B remains OPEN. CONSEQUENCE: H_B holds for every f with a bottom-pair optimal circuit, including the cost-3 functions on 4 variables whose optimal circuits have a bottom pair. Gate elimination with a drop of 2 per two-variable restriction gives only a linear lower bound (size >= about n), so this is not progress toward the superpolylog target. Barrier label (diagnostic only): not relativizing or algebrizing in any meaningful sense; not natural, since it is a structural property of a circuit, not a constructive property of the truth table; localizing: no. Next: test on n=4 whether every size>=3 function has an optimal circuit with a bottom pair (exhaustive), since that decides whether LEMMA BP covers the cost-3 case without the BFS argument.

question: Q-156fa9c912
statement: LINEAR-UPDATE DIMENSION LEMMA (restricted update class; closes nothing by itself, shrinks the linear case of G0004). Setting: F any field; N = 2^m; x in {0,1}^N; Im = Im_s = { truth tables of circuits of size <= s }; f = indicator of Im, valued in {0,1} inside F. A linear-update one-pass algorithm of dimension k over F: state s_0 in F^k fixed; s_t = A_{t,x_t} s_{t-1} for time-dependent matrices A_{t,b} in F^{k x k}; output c . s_N in F, required to equal f(x) for every x. (Affine updates are covered by adding one constant coordinate: dimension k+1.) Cut t: write x = p q with |p| = t, |q| = N - t. TRIANGULAR FOOLING SET at cut t: pairs (p_i, q_i), i = 1..r, with p_i q_i in Im for all i, and p_i q_j not in Im for all i > j (the cross entries with i < j are unconstrained). THEOREM: every such algorithm has k >= r. PROOF: for a prefix p let v_p = A_{t,p} s_0 in F^k, where A_{t,p} is the product of the prefix transitions (depends only on p). For a suffix q let w_q = B_{t,q}^T c in F^k, where B_{t,q} is the product of the suffix transitions (depends only on q). Then f(pq) = c . B_{t,q} A_{t,p} s_0 = <w_q, v_p>. So the r x r matrix M[i,j] = f(p_i q_j) equals V^T W with V = [v_{p_1} ... v_{p_r}] and W = [w_{q_1} ... w_{q_r}] in F^{k x r}, hence rank_F M <= k. By the fooling conditions M[i,i] = 1 and M[i,j] = 0 for i > j, so M is upper unitriangular with det 1 and rank_F M = r. Hence k >= r. QED. SCOPE: linear updates over a field, any time-dependent matrices, any N, any cut, any field; it says nothing about general or nonlinear updates and nothing about update time beyond the dimension. Note: the trivial bound rank_F M_t(f) <= |Im| does NOT give a lower bound; only a triangular fooling set (or any rank lower bound) does. CONSEQUENCE: the linear-update case of G0004 (poly(s) dimension cannot decide or search MCSP[s]) reduces to exhibiting, for some cut, a triangular fooling set of size superpolynomial in s inside Im_s. OPEN (not claimed): whether such a set exists. A max-degree greedy argument does not give it, because the prefix degree of Im can be comparable to |Im| (e.g. all circuits whose first cofactor is 0). GAP: G0004 (restricted class only; general update time open); no claim about P vs NP.

statement: CAP LEMMA (cut-rank cap). Let S be any set of N-bit truth tables, N=2^m. (a) For every 1<=t<N and every field F, rank_F M_t(S) <= |S|, where M_t[p][q]=1[(q<<t)|p in S]. Proof: each f in S sets exactly one entry of M_t, so M_t has at most |S| nonzero entries, hence at most |S| nonzero rows, and rank <= number of nonzero rows. (b) For S=Im_s, |Im_s| <= (16(m+s)^2)^s, since a size-<=s circuit is a sequence of at most s gates, each choosing an op (16) and two earlier nodes (at most (m+i)^2 choices for gate i). (c) For the prefix Myhill-Nerode classes of S at level t: the residual of prefix p is zero unless p is a prefix of some element of S, and distinct nonzero residuals need distinct prefixes, so the number of classes is at most |S|+1. Hence the minimal exact prefix automaton of Im_s has at most |Im_s|+1 states per level, i.e. O(s log(m+s)) bits, which is inside the budget O(log N + s log(n+s)). Consequence: a cut-rank lower bound on the STATE count of this automaton cannot exceed O(s log(m+s)) bits. The S0098 route (k >= rank_F) therefore bounds only LINEAR-dimension models; it cannot establish a streaming lower bound beyond the budget, consistent with the protocol's statement that only an update-time lower bound can.

question: Q-156fa9c912
statement: REPAIR LEMMA (residual-function automaton for EXT prefix language). Let N = 2^m, s <= poly(m). For a prefix p of length t <= N, define the residual language R_p = { q in {0,1}^{N-t} : p q in Im_s } where Im_s is the set of truth tables of fan-in-2 circuits of size <= s over m inputs. (a) The number of distinct residual languages is at most |Im_s| + 1 <= (16(m+s)^2)^s + 1. Proof: distinct nonempty residuals correspond to distinct nonempty subsets of Im_s sharing the same prefix p, so there are at most |Im_s| of them; the empty residual (p not a prefix of any element of Im_s) adds at most one. (b) The minimal exact prefix automaton of the language Im_s therefore has at most |Im_s| + 1 states per level t, and total states at most (N+1)(|Im_s|+1). State bits per level: log2(|Im_s|+1) <= s log2(16(m+s)^2) + 1 = O(s log(m+s)). (c) The state transition function (update) given a new bit b: from state representing residual R, go to the state representing R.b = { q' : b q' in R }. Computing this update may require time exponential in s (unbounded update time), because testing whether a string q' is in R.b means checking whether p b q' in Im_s, i.e., whether a given truth table prefix extends to a circuit of size <= s. No poly(s) time update is claimed. (d) This automaton is exactly the Myhill-Nerode DFA of the language Im_s, and its state count at level t equals the number of Myhill-Nerode equivalence classes of prefixes of length t. The earlier claim r_t = |P_t| + [P_t != {0,1}^t] is corrected to r_t <= |P_t| + 1 where P_t is the set of length-t prefixes of Im_s, and the inequality can be strict because distinct prefixes may yield the same residual. (e) Consequence: any streaming algorithm that decides membership in Im_s must use at least log2(|Im_s|+1) bits of state, but this lower bound is only O(s log(m+s)) bits, which is inside the O(log N + s log(n+s)) budget of the MMW19 Thm 1.2 algorithm. Hence a state-count lower bound alone cannot separate the EXT automaton from the budget. To obtain a separation, an UPDATE-TIME lower bound is needed, consistent with G0004.

statement: LEMMA (exponential-time update, not poly(s)). Setting: n>=1, s>=1, N=2^n, Im = {tt(C): C circuit on n inputs, size <= s}. For any prefix p of length t, EXT_{n,s}(p)=1 iff some C in Im has prefix p. PROOF: Every circuit of size <= s over binary fan-in gates is specified by at most s gates; gate k has an op from a set of 16 binary Boolean functions and two inputs among the n+k-1 earlier nodes, plus a choice of output node. The update for bit b on state p is one such query, so the update time is 2^{O(s log(n+s))} * poly(2^n). SCOPE: a general upper bound, exponential in s. It does NOT bound update time by poly(s), so it does not close G0003 (which needs poly(s) update) and does not touch G0004 (a lower bound).

PROOF: the transitions A_{i,b} are fixed per position i, so for a prefix p of length t the state after reading p is v_p = A_{t,p} s_0 in F^k, where A_{t,p} is the ordered product of the prefix transitions. For a suffix q of length N-t, the remaining transitions give s_N = B_q v_p with B_q in F^{k x k} depending only on q. The output is c . s_N, so f(pq) = u_q . v_p with u_q = c B_q in F^(1 x k). Hence M_t = U V where U has rows u_q (2^(N-t) x k) and V has columns v_p (k x 2^t), so rank_F M_t <= k. COROLLARY: k >= max_t rank_F M_t, which is at least the size of any triangular fooling set (the upper-triangular principal submatrix with unit diagonal has det 1). SCOPE: exact for linear-update algorithms over the field F; the bound is field-dependent in general: rank_Q and rank_{F_p} of an integer matrix can differ (rank_{F_p} <= rank_Q), so the bound for an F_p-algorithm must use rank over F_p. Does not give a poly-time or update-time bound, does not close G0004. Upper limit: rank_F M_t <= min(2^t, 2^(N-t), |Im_s|) with |Im_s| = 2^(O(s log(m+s))), so the rank bound cannot exceed the circuit-count bound of S0091 in magnitude.

question: Q-156fa9c912
statement: LEMMA L1 (fixed-s streaming for membership in Im_s; bookkeeping, not progress). Setting: m, s >= 1; Circ_s = straight-line programs of length k, 1 <= k <= s, where step j (j = 1..k) applies one of the 4 ops {AND, OR, XOR, a&~b} to a pair a < b of the m+j-1 earlier nodes. Im_s = truth tables of Circ_s. (i) COUNT: a program of length k is determined by its sequence of choices (op_j, a_j, b_j), and there are at most 4*C(m+j-1,2) <= 2(m+s)^2 choices at step j, so the number of programs of length k is at most (2(m+s)^2)^k, and |Circ_s| <= sum_{k=1..s} (2(m+s)^2)^k <= 2(2(m+s)^2)^s, since the ratio r = 2(m+s)^2 >= 2 makes the geometric sum at most 2 r^s. (ii) ALGORITHM: read x_1..x_N in order and keep the alive set A_t = {C in Circ_s : C(y) = x_y for all y <= t}, stored as a bit vector of length |Circ_s|. Start with A_0 = Circ_s. At step t, for each alive C, compute C(y_t) for the input y_t with binary expansion t in O(s+m) time, and drop C if it differs from x_t. Then A_N = {C : Eval(C) = x}, and the output is 1 iff A_N is nonempty. (iii) CORRECTNESS: by induction on t, A_t is exactly the consistent set, so the output decides x in Im_s exactly. (iv) COST: state |Circ_s| bits, per-bit time O(|Circ_s|(s+m)), so for fixed s both are poly(m) with degree O(s). For s = m^c the bound is 2^{Theta(s log m)}, superpolynomial. PROOF COMPLETE for (i)-(iv). SCOPE: membership in Im_s for fixed s only. Does NOT bound the update cost for s = poly(m), and does NOT close G0004 or G0071-G0074. Its state bound is the trivial one; the O(s log(m+s)) bit bound would need S0091, which is still unreviewed. question: Q-156fa9c912
statement: LEMMA (state count of the EXT prefix automaton, restricted class B, |B|=b). Let B be a finite binary basis (here AND, OR, XOR, so b=3; no negation or constants), let N=2^m, let C_{m,s} be the circuits of size <= s over inputs x_1..x_m with fan-in-2 gates from B, and let Im_{m,s} subset {0,1}^N be their truth tables. Then (a) |Im_{m,s}| <= prod_{k=0}^{s-1} b(m+k)(m+k+1)/2 <= (b(m+s)^2)^s. (b) For every t in 0..N and every prefix p in {0,1}^t, let R_t(p) = {w in {0,1}^{N-t} : pw in Im}. The number of distinct nonempty R_t(p) is at most |Im_{m,s}|. Hence the minimal (Myhill-Nerode) automaton reading the truth table has at most |Im_{m,s}| states at each level, i.e. log(#states) = O(s log(m+s)) bits, plus log N bits for the position counter. PROOF (a): a circuit of size s is determined by the sequence of gates; gate k picks an unordered pair {i<=j} from the m+k available nodes and one of b operations, giving at most b(m+k)(m+k+1)/2 choices; the map from sequences to truth tables is onto Im, so |Im| is at most the product. PROOF (b): restriction to the first t bits maps Im onto the set of realised prefixes, so #realised prefixes <= |Im|; R_t(p) depends only on p, so the number of distinct residuals is at most the number of realised prefixes. Both steps are elementary counting.

statement: PROOF. (1) rank_F M <= |S|: rank is at most the number of nonzero rows; each nonzero row holds at least one 1; the map x -> (x>>(N-t), x mod 2^(N-t)) is injective and each x in S sets exactly one entry, so the number of 1-entries is |S|. Hence rank_F M_t(S) <= |S| for every field F. (2) |Im_s| bound: every function in Im_s is the value of some gate of a program with j <= s gates (or a base node). A program of j gates is a sequence where gate k (1<=k<=j) is op_c(a,b) with c in [16] and a,b among the m+2+(k-1) = m+1+k earlier nodes. So the number of programs with j gates is at most prod_{k=1}^{j} 16(m+1+k)^2 <= (16(m+s+1)^2)^j, because m+1+k <= m+s+1 for k <= s. The base nodes contribute at most m+2 <= 16(m+s+1)^2 values. Summing over j=0..s: |Im_s| <= sum_{j=0}^{s} (16(m+s+1)^2)^j <= (s+1)(16(m+s+1)^2)^s. Combining (1) and (2) gives the lemma. question: Q-156fa9c912
statement: LEMMA (F_2 affine images: streaming membership). Let r, L >= 1, M_1..M_L in F_2^r (row vectors), c in F_2^L, and phi(z)_t = <M_t, z> + c_t for z in F_2^r. Let Im = phi(F_2^r). For a prefix p of length t, p is a prefix of some element of Im iff the linear system {<M_s, z> = p_s + c_s : s <= t} is consistent over F_2. Maintain the reduced row-echelon basis of the augmented system (rows (M_s | p_s + c_s)), with at most r pivots. Appending bit b to p is one insertion: reduce the new augmented row by the existing pivot rows (at most r XORs of (r+1)-bit words), declare p dead iff the reduced row is 0 with rhs 1, otherwise add it as a new pivot and clear its pivot column from the other rows. Correctness: the system is consistent iff no F_2-combination of its rows gives 0 = 1; the reduced echelon basis spans exactly the row space of the augmented system, so it detects inconsistency. Consequences: (i) x in {0,1}^L lies in Im iff the full system with rhs x_s + c_s is consistent, decidable in one pass with state O(r^2) bits and update time O(r^2) word operations per bit, with no exponential branching needed; (ii) the trie of Im restricted to affine images is poly-state per prefix. SCOPE: F_2 affine images only, z over all of F_2^r (no circuit, no size bound s). It does NOT address G0004, which concerns Im(Eval) of circuits of size <= s, where the extension question is an existential over Circ_s. This is standard Gaussian elimination, recorded as a restricted-class special case; it is bookkeeping and does not count as progress toward P vs NP. statement: SIZE-1 STREAMING LEMMA (special case s=1; does NOT close G0004 or G0009). statement: REPAIR of S0057 (state-count form). Setting: p=3, t,k>=1, A in F_3^{k x t}, c in F_3^k, phi(x)=Ax+c, B={0,1}^t, K(A):=|ker A ∩ {-1,0,1}^t|. For x in F_v, A(x-x0)=phi(x)-phi(x0)=0 and every coordinate of x-x0 lies in {-1,0,1}, so x -> x-x0 maps F_v injectively into ker A ∩ {-1,0,1}^t, giving |F_v| <= K(A). The fibres F_v partition B, so 2^t = sum_v |F_v| <= |phi(B)| K(A). PROOF of (ii): if phi(x)=phi(y) with x,y in B, then x-y in ker A with coordinates in {-1,0,1}, so x-y in ker A ∩ {-1,0,1}^t = {0} (K(A)=1 and 0 is always in the set), hence x=y. QED. question: Q-156fa9c912
statement: LEMMA K-BOUND (kind LEMMA). Let F = F_p, p prime, A a k x t matrix over F, K(A) = |ker A cap {-1,0,1}^t| with -1 read in F, r = rank A. Then K(A) <= 3^(t-r). PROOF: ker A is a subspace of dimension d = t - r. Choose a set S of d coordinates such that the projection pi_S: ker A -> F^S is injective (exists: a basis of ker A, as a d x t matrix, has d linearly independent columns S, and then pi_S is an isomorphism onto F^d). For y in ker A cap {-1,0,1}^t, y is determined by pi_S(y), and pi_S(y) lies in {-1,0,1}^S, which has 3^d elements. Hence K(A) <= 3^d. Consequence: |phi(B)| >= 2^t / K(A) >= (2/3)^t * 3^r ... more precisely |phi(B)| >= 2^t / 3^(t-r). Tightness: equality K(A)=3^(t-r) is attained on the tested instances (max ratio 1.0, cm-4a7a793493bf40c0). SCOPE: a state-count bound for a linear map on the Boolean cube; no update-time bound; does not close G0004 or G0009. Refutes nothing new. Hypothesis H_gap (K(A) <= 3^(t-r) fails for p >= 5) is refuted by the same argument, not only by the sample.

question: Q-156fa9c912
statement: PROCEDURE UPD (exact bit-streaming update of the EXT prefix automaton, claimed by R1460). Setting: N = 2^m, Circ_s = all straight-line circuits of size 1..s on m inputs (gate lists, output = last gate), totally ordered by list index ord. Truth tables Eval(C) in {0,1}^N. The state after reading prefix p of length t is w(p) = ord-least C with Eval(C) starting with p, if one exists. STATE: the single circuit w (encoding O(s log(m+s)) bits) plus the counter t (log N bits). CLAIM: UPD(w, b) := ord-least C in Circ_s with Eval(C)[0..t] = Eval(w)[0..t-1] . b computes w(pb) exactly. PROOF: (i) Eval(w)[0..t-1] = p, since w(p) starts with p by definition, so p is recoverable from the state. (ii) {C : Eval(C) starts with pb} = {C : Eval(C) starts with p and Eval(C)_t = b} is exactly the set the scan tests, so the scan returns min S(pb) = w(pb). (iii) If no C matches, S(pb) is empty and the stream is dead. RUNNING TIME: scanning costs at most |Circ_s| candidates; each prefix test evaluates a candidate on assignments 0..t, which is O((t+1) s) word operations. With |Circ_s| <= 2(16(m+s)^2)^s (each gate: 16 ops and at most (m+s)^2 operand pairs), one bit costs O((16(m+s)^2)^s (t+1) s) operations and N bits cost O((16(m+s)^2)^s N^2 s). SCOPE: exact for every m, s; the time is polynomial in N for fixed s but exponential in s, so it does NOT give poly(s) per-bit update and does NOT close G0004 or G0003. It shows that the update function is computable from the O(s log(m+s))-bit state plus t, with an explicit bound. OPEN: whether the scan over Circ_s can be replaced by a search of size poly(s) (this is the content of G0004).

statement: PROC-U (space-bounded exact update, no stored witness). CLAIM 2 (space): the enumerator is a mixed-radix counter over gate sequences of length at most s, using O(s log(m+s)) bits of workspace plus O(log N) for the index t. question: Q-156fa9c912
statement: LEMMA (corrected circuit-count bound, repair of S0115 step iv). Setting: n>=1, s>=1, Circ_{n,s} = circuits on n inputs with at most s binary gates and a designated output node, Im = {tt(C) : C in Circ_{n,s}}, L = |Im|. CLAIM: L <= (16(n+s)^2)^s (n+s), hence log2 L <= s*log2(16(n+s)^2) + log2(n+s) = O(s log(n+s)), and the number of distinct residual functions R_p (over all prefixes p of any fixed length t) is at most L+1. PROOF: a circuit is a sequence of s gates followed by an output choice. Gate k (k=1..s) takes an ordered pair of nodes among the n+k-1 <= n+s-1 nodes already present (at most (n+s)^2 choices) and one of 16 binary Boolean operations, giving at most 16(n+s)^2 choices per gate. question: Q-156fa9c912
statement: LEMMA S (exact residual streaming for EXT). Let S subseteq {0,1}^N be any finite set (in particular S = Im_s, the truth tables of circuits of size <= s on m inputs, N = 2^m). For a prefix p of length t define the residual R_t(p) = {q in {0,1}^{N-t} : p q in S}. There is a deterministic streaming algorithm that reads p bit by bit and maintains R_t(p) explicitly as a list of bitstrings: initial state R_0(epsilon) = S; on reading bit b at level t, compute R_{t+1}(pb) = {q' in {0,1}^{N-t-1} : b q' in R_t(p)} by scanning R_t(p), keeping entries whose first bit is b and deleting that first bit; after N bits accept iff R_N(p) is nonempty (equivalently contains epsilon). PROOF OF CORRECTNESS by induction on t. Base t=0: R_0(epsilon) = S = {q : epsilon q in S}. Inductive step: assume R_t(p) = {q : p q in S}. Then {q' : b q' in R_t(p)} = {q' : p b q' in S} = {q' : (pb) q' in S} = R_{t+1}(pb), so the transition preserves the invariant. At t = N, R_N(p) = {q in {0,1}^0 : p q in S} = {epsilon} if p in S and emptyset otherwise, so accepting iff R_N(p) nonempty decides membership p in S exactly. RUNNING TIME: materialising S costs O(|S| * N) bit operations if not already given; one transition scans R_t(p) and costs O(|R_t(p)| * (N-t)) <= O(|S| * N) bit operations; reading all N bits costs O(|S| * N^2) bit operations total; space is O(|S| * N) bits to store the explicit list. CONSEQUENCE: this is a correct decision procedure for EXT_{n,s} (membership in Im_s) in time O(|Im_s| * N^2) = O((s+1)(16(m+s+1)^2)^s * N^2) = 2^{O(s log(s+m))} * poly(N) using the circuit-enumeration bound (conditional on S0152/S0320, unreviewed). It does NOT give poly(s) update time: per-step update is O(|S| * N), exponential in s when |S| is exponential in s log m. Thus G0003 (poly(s) update) is not closed by this lemma; closing it requires either (a) a compact representation of residual sets of size poly(s) * poly(m) with a poly(s)-time transition, or (b) an algorithm that avoids explicit residuals. The state-count bound (at most |S| nonempty residuals per level) is necessary but not sufficient for poly(s) update.

statement: LEMMA (K = 1 repair of the SURVIVOR COMPRESSION step; does NOT close G0001). statement:
LEMMA (Exact undecided probability under random restriction with uniform threshold). Let g(x) = [∑_{i=1}^n w_i x_i ≥ t] be a threshold gate with integer weights w_i, S = ∑ |w_i|. Let R_p be the random restriction: each variable is free independently with probability p, otherwise fixed to 0 or 1 with probability (1-p)/2 each. Let the threshold t be chosen uniformly from {t_min, ..., t_max} where the interval length L = t_max - t_min + 1 satisfies L ≥ S (in particular, t uniform on [-S, S] works). Then P_{R_p, t}[g|R_p is non-constant] ≤ p, with equality when L = S and the threshold range matches the possible sums exactly.

PROOF. For a fixed restriction ρ, let F be the set of free variables. The restricted gate is g_ρ(y) = [∑_{i∈F} w_i y_i ≥ t - ∑_{i∉F} w_i ρ(i)]. This is non-constant iff the threshold t falls in the interval I_ρ = (L_ρ, U_ρ] where L_ρ = ∑_{i∈F: w_i<0} w_i, U_ρ = ∑_{i∈F: w_i>0} w_i. The length of I_ρ is U_ρ - L_ρ = ∑_{i∈F} |w_i| =: W_F. Since t is uniform over an interval of length L ≥ S ≥ W_F, P_t[g_ρ non-constant] = W_F / L ≤ W_F / S. Now take expectation over R_p: E[W_F] = ∑_i |w_i| · P(i free) = p S. Thus P_{R_p,t}[undecided] = E[W_F/L] ≤ E[W_F/S] = p. Equality holds when L = S and the threshold distribution is uniform over exactly S+1 consecutive integers covering the full range of possible sums. ∎

statement: LEMMA (gcd-refined window bound, one THR gate, per fixed free set). Let g(x) = [sum_j w_j x_j >= t] with integer weights, F a set of variables, and out = complement of F. (i) Non-constancy: let lo = sum_{j in F} min(w_j,0), hi = sum_{j in F} max(w_j,0). The F-part of the sum takes its minimum lo and maximum hi, so the restriction is non-constant iff t - hi <= c < t - lo, where c = sum_{j in out} w_j x_j. (ii) Sperner: write y_j = x_j if w_j > 0 and y_j = 1 - x_j if w_j < 0. Then c = const + sum_{j in out, w_j != 0} |w_j| y_j with positive integer coefficients a_j = |w_j|. The window [t-hi, t-lo) contains W_F consecutive integers, hence at most ceil(W_F/g_F) <= floor(W_F/g_F)+1 values of the correct residue. Summing (ii) over these values gives P[nonconst | F] <= (floor(W_F/g_F)+1)/sqrt(r_F). QED. statement: Formalization of S-54f648a904 (inclusion-exclusion for #F). Let F = C_1 and ... and C_m be a CNF over x_1..x_n. For S subset of [m] put L(S) = union of C_i over i in S, and N(S) = #{a in {0,1}^n : every literal of L(S) is false under a}. Then #F = sum over S of (-1)^|S| N(S). Moreover N(S) = 2^(n - |V(S)|) if L(S) contains no complementary pair {x, not-x}, and N(S) = 0 otherwise, where V(S) is the set of variables occurring in L(S). Proof: with f_i(a) = 1 iff C_i is falsified by a, [a satisfies F] = product over i of (1 - f_i(a)). Expanding gives sum over S of (-1)^|S| times product over i in S of f_i(a), and that product is 1 exactly when all literals of L(S) are false under a. Summing over a gives the identity. A consistent L(S) forces the values of V(S) and leaves n - |V(S)| variables free; an inconsistent L(S) has no satisfying-falsifying assignment.

statement:
LEMMA (De Morgan leaf size, general). Setting: formulas are trees with fan-in-2 gates from {AND, OR} and leaves labelled by literals x_i or NOT x_i; L(f) = minimum number of leaves over formulas computing f. Parity_d(x) = x_1 XOR ... XOR x_d.
(A) L(NOT f) = L(f). Proof: for a formula F, let F^d be obtained by swapping AND and OR at every gate and negating every leaf literal. By induction on F, F^d computes NOT of F's function (De Morgan), and F^d has the same number of leaves. Hence L(NOT f) <= L(f), and the reverse follows by applying the same argument to NOT f.
(B) L(f XOR g) <= 2(L(f) + L(g)). Proof: take formulas F, G with leaves L(f), L(g). By (A), F^d and G^d compute NOT f and NOT g with the same leaf counts. The formula H = (F AND G^d) OR (F^d AND G) computes (f AND NOT g) OR (NOT f AND g) = f XOR g and has 2L(f) + 2L(g) leaves (F, F^d, G, G^d are each a copy of a subtree).
(C) For every j >= 0, L(parity_{2^j}) <= 4^j. Proof by induction. j = 0: parity_1 = x_1, one leaf, 1 = 4^0. Step: parity_{2^{j+1}}(x) = parity_{2^j}(x_left) XOR parity_{2^j}(x_right) on disjoint variable sets. By (B), L <= 2(4^j + 4^j) = 4^{j+1}. Since parity_{2^j} is computed by a formula on 2^j variables with 4^j = (2^j)^2 leaves, this gives the exact pattern d^2 at d = 2^j.
NOTE (not a claim): the same recursion for general d gives L(parity_6) <= 2(L(3)+L(3)) = 40 > 36 = 6^2 with L(3)=10, so the bound d^2 is NOT derived for general d by this construction; only the powers of two are proved.

statement: PROOF. Each cross wire carries one bit from its source side to its target side. Evaluate C in topological order: a gate on side S_A needs only values from S_A or from cross wires; the value of a cross wire is a function of its source side's inputs and bits already received, so it is sent once, by its source party, as one bit. Each cross wire contributes at most one bit, so the transcript has at most kappa bits. Once all cross wires are transmitted, both parties know the output bit for their input pair; the party holding the output gate sends one more bit, so the total is at most kappa+1 bits. A deterministic protocol with c bits has at most 2^c leaves; each leaf is a combinatorial rectangle on which the output is constant, so M is a sum of at most 2^c rank-one 0/1 matrices, rank_R(M) <= 2^c. Hence log2 rank <= kappa+1. The argument uses only the wire count, not any gate structure, and it holds for any partition of gates. statement: L-K1-PREFIX (closes G0005(a) for the prefix-cut family). Setting: f:{0,1}^N->{0,1} computed by a fan-in<=2 circuit C with gates G, inputs x_1..x_N in a fixed order. Let W = number of wires (gate-input edges), Lambda(C)=sum over wires u->g of (P(g)-P(u)). For i in [1,N-1], M_i = communication matrix of f for A={x_1..x_i}, B=rest. Let L_i={v: P(v)<=i}. Input x_j is in L_i iff j<=i, so L_i restricted to inputs is exactly A. If g in L_i and u->g is a wire, P(u)<=P(g)<=i so u in L_i: no wire goes from the right side to the left side. statement: REPAIR of S0001 (single-split cut lemma, input wires counted). Statement: Let C be a fan-in<=2 Boolean circuit on inputs X disjoint-union Y computing f, with communication matrix M_f (rows indexed by assignments to X, columns by assignments to Y). Fix any side assignment of all nodes (inputs included) to {A,B} with every x in X on A and every y in Y on B; gates may be placed freely. Let kappa = number of EDGES (u,g) of C with side(u) != side(g), input nodes included. Then rank_Q(M_f) <= 2^(kappa+1). PROOF: fix a topological order v_1..v_T (inputs first). Process v_1..v_T in order: the owner of v (the party of side(v)) computes val(v) from its own input bits and from values already received; every in-neighbour u of v on the other side has a cross edge (u,v), so u has a cross out-edge and was transmitted when processed, hence the owner of v has it. The owner transmits val(v) as one bit exactly when v has at least one cross out-edge. After all nodes, if the output node o was not transmitted, its owner sends val(o) as one final bit. Both parties then know f(a,b). MESSAGE COUNT: each transmitted node has >=1 cross out-edge and out-edge sets of distinct nodes are disjoint, so at most kappa nodes are transmitted; total <= kappa+1 bits. The schedule (order, sender rule) is fixed in advance, so the transcript determines whose turn it is. RECTANGLE: a deterministic protocol with c bits has at most 2^c leaves; the inputs reaching a leaf form a rectangle A_l x B_l (standard, since each message depends only on the sender's input and the transcript); f is constant on each leaf because val(o) is in the transcript (either transmitted or the final bit). So M_f = sum over leaves with f=1 of 1_{A_l} 1_{B_l}^T, a sum of at most 2^(kappa+1) rank-one matrices, hence rank_Q(M_f) <= 2^(kappa+1). QED. SCOPE: one fixed split X|Y, any gate placement, any side assignment (the best bound is min over assignments of kappa). statement: MINLA LEMMA (limit of the single-order prefix route; does not close G0001/G0002). Let G be a graph on n vertices with edge expansion h = min over S with 1<=|S|<=n/2 of |boundary(S)|/|S|. statement: PROOF. (1) By induction over a topological order, every node in P has a value that depends only on a, since P is closed under predecessors. (2) Let W be the set of wires leaving P; |W| = w(P). For any node outside P, its value is a function of its own inputs, which are either suffix inputs, outside gates, or wires in W. So for each suffix assignment b there is a function G_b with f(a,b) = G_b(z(a)), where z(a) in {0,1}^W lists the values carried by the wires in W. (3) Therefore f(a,.) = G_(.)(z(a)) is determined by z(a), which takes at most 2^(w(P)) values, so at most 2^(w(P)) distinct subfunctions occur. QED. Consequence: if every level l admits a closed prefix set with w_l <= W, then the OBDD has size at most n 2^W and #SAT of C takes time about n 2^W poly(s). For W = O(log s) this is polynomial.

statement: PROOF OF L1. (i) By induction on topological order, every A-node is a function of x alone: x-inputs trivially; an A-gate's inputs are A-nodes because no B-node feeds an A-gate. (ii) Let S(x) in {0,1}^kappa be the values of the kappa cross nodes (A-nodes with a B-consumer), which are functions of x by (i). By induction every B-node is a function of (y, S(x)): its inputs are y-inputs, B-nodes, or A-nodes, and any A-node feeding a B-node is a cross node, hence a coordinate of S(x). (iii) For s in {0,1}^kappa let u_s be the indicator vector of {x : S(x) = s} and w_s(y) = G(s,y). statement: PROOF OF L2. Fix a topological order v_1,...,v_N of the circuit. Let c_1,...,c_kappa be the nodes of K in that order; each c_i is owned by Alice (A) or Bob (B). Protocol: for i = 1..kappa the owner of c_i sends the bit value(c_i), then the output owner sends f's bit if f is not in K, i.e. at most kappa+1 bits. Well-defined and deterministic: the speaker sequence depends only on the circuit and the side assignment, not on the inputs. Correctness: when the owner of c_i speaks, it knows its own input and all bits sent so far, and it can compute c_i. Induction on the topological order: any input of c_i is either an input node (owned by the speaker, since inputs lie on their own side), a node on the speaker's side (computed by the speaker by induction), or a node on the other side with a consumer on the speaker's side, hence in K, hence earlier in the order and already sent. So value(c_i) is a function of the speaker's input and the transcript so far. Thus the transcript determines all of K and f. Rectangles: for a fixed transcript tau, the set of x with tau consistent is a set X_tau, and similarly Y_tau for y; by the standard induction over rounds the set {(x,y): transcript = tau} equals X_tau x Y_tau. On a leaf f is constant (it is determined by tau). Hence M_f = sum over leaves with f=1 of u_tau w_tau^T with u, w 0/1 vectors, so rank_Q M_f <= number of leaves <= 2^(kappa+1). QED. Note: L2 does not use the one-way hypothesis; L1 (one-way, bound 2^kappa without +1) remains a separate sharper statement.

question: Q-2f96f7e0f1
statement: PROOF. (a) Restricted gate = [R_j(x_A) + S_j >= t_j], R_j = sum_{i in A} w_ji x_i. If A has p positive and q negative weights, R_j takes every integer value in [-q, p] (choose a positive-weight and b negative-weight variables; value a-b covers the whole interval), so the value set is exactly [L_j, U_j] with U_j-L_j = p+q = k. The gate is non-constant iff U_j+S_j >= t_j and L_j+S_j < t_j, i.e. t_j-U_j <= S_j < t_j-L_j; this window contains k integers. (b) Erdos-Littlewood-Offord (Erdos 1945): for reals a_1..a_f with |a_i|>=1 and any real x, #{eps in {0,1}^f : |sum a_i eps_i - x| < 1} <= binom(f, floor(f/2)). Apply with a_i = w_ji (i in F) and x = s an integer: Pr_z[S_j=s] <= binom(f,floor(f/2))/2^f <= 1/sqrt(f), using binom(2r,r)/4^r <= 1/sqrt(3r+1) and binom(2r+1,r)/2^(2r+1) = binom(2r+2,r+1)/2^(2r+2) <= 1/sqrt(3r+4). Gate j is non-constant only if S_j lies in one of k integers, so Pr_z[j non-constant] <= k/sqrt(f). Summing over j by linearity gives E_z[N] <= m k/sqrt(n-k). QED. CONSEQUENCE: with k = round(n^delta), delta < 1/2, the expected surviving fraction is <= n^(delta-1/2)(1+o(1)) -> 0 polynomially; at delta = 1/2 it is O(1). Consistency check (not a sharpness test): k/sqrt(n-k) = 1.155 (n=16,k=4), 1.118 (n=25,k=5), 1.080 (n=49,k=7), above the observed fractions 0.74, 0.72, 0.70 in cm-9e6b480beb584cee. SCOPE AND LIMITS: +-1 weights only (the MAJ∘MAJ bottom layer). For general THR weights the window has sum_A|w_ji| integer points and the bound becomes sum_A|w_ji|/sqrt(#(F ∩ supp)), which is useless for large weights, so Chen-Tal-Wang's general THR∘THR count is NOT covered. KNOWLEDGE gain: exact characterisation (a) and an expectation bound (b) for the ±1 case. ALGORITHMIC gain: none yet - the polynomial-approximation step of a CAPP algorithm is still open, and the bound does not yet yield a running time. Erdos-Littlewood-Offord is classical; the new content is the exact characterisation and the application to the restricted MAJ∘MAJ bottom layer.

question: Q-2f96f7e0f1
statement: GENERAL-WEIGHT ALIVE-SURVIVAL LEMMA (integer weights, S0007). Setting: w_ji, t_j integers; A subset [n], |A|=k, F=[n]\A, f=n-k; z uniform on {0,1}^F; L_j = sum_{i in A} min(0,w_ji), U_j = sum_{i in A} max(0,w_ji), S_j(z) = sum_{i in F} w_ji z_i, f_j = #{i in F : w_ji != 0}, N(A,z) = #{j : T_j restricted to x_F=z is non-constant on {0,1}^A}. Then (a) INCLUSION: if gate j is non-constant then t_j - U_j <= S_j(z) < t_j - L_j; the window holds exactly U_j - L_j integers. (b) For f_j >= 1: Pr_z[j non-constant] <= (U_j - L_j)/sqrt(f_j). (c) E_z[N(A,z)] <= sum_{j: f_j>=1} (U_j-L_j)/sqrt(f_j) + #{j : f_j = 0 and t_j - U_j <= 0 < t_j - L_j}. PROOF. (a) The restricted gate is [R_j(x_A) >= t_j - S_j(z)] with R_j = sum_{i in A} w_ji x_i, whose values lie in [L_j, U_j]. Non-constancy gives some x_A with R_j >= t_j - S_j, so U_j >= t_j - S_j; and some x_A' with R_j < t_j - S_j, so L_j < t_j - S_j. These are the two inequalities. Integrality gives the count U_j-L_j. (b) S_j depends only on the f_j coordinates with nonzero weight, which are uniform bits. Each nonzero weight has |w| >= 1, so Erdos (1945) gives Pr[S_j in an open interval of length 2] <= binom(f_j, floor(f_j/2))/2^{f_j} <= 1/sqrt(f_j). Summing over the U_j-L_j integers in the window gives (b). (c) For f_j = 0, S_j = 0 and the gate is non-constant iff the window contains 0; for f_j >= 1 use (b); then linearity. QED. CHECK: for +-1 weights with all F-weights nonzero, f_j = f and U_j - L_j = k, so (c) reduces to S0006. SCOPE AND CAVEAT: the exploratory check cm-9284392501944f05 summed only over gates with f_j >= 1, so it did not test the f_j = 0 term in (c); the term is needed for general weights and is covered by this proof, not by that run. Progress: bookkeeping. The bound is in expectation, costs 2^k per surviving gate, and closes no obligation (G0001, G0002, G0007 stay OPEN).

question: Q-2f96f7e0f1
statement: REPAIR of S0012(b), general nonzero integer weights (CLAIMED, for review). Setting as in S0012, with f_j = #{i in F : w_ji != 0}. Claim: E_z[N(A,z)] <= sum_j (U_j - L_j) * a_j, where a_j = C(f_j, floor(f_j/2))/2^{f_j} <= 1/sqrt(f_j) whenever f_j >= 1. Proof: (1) Window identity from S0012(a): gate j is non-constant iff S_j(z) lies in a set of U_j - L_j consecutive integers. (2) Union bound: Pr_z[S_j in window] <= (U_j-L_j) * max_c Pr_z[S_j(z)=c]. (3) Erdos Littlewood-Offord: S_j is a sum of f_j terms of integer absolute value >= 1, and the number of subsets with sum in any open interval of length 2 is at most C(f_j, floor(f_j/2)); so each point atom is at most a_j. (4) C(f,floor(f/2))/2^f <= 1/sqrt(f) for f >= 1. Hence E_z[N] <= sum_j (U_j-L_j)/sqrt(f_j). Scope: this is an expectation bound with the sum over gates; for f_j = 0 the gate is deterministic and the bound must be replaced by an indicator term, so the statement needs f_j >= 1 or a separate count of such gates. question: Q-2f96f7e0f1
statement: PROCEDURE R2 (deterministic restriction by conditional expectations; repair of the refuted every-z form). Setting as in S0006: w_ji in {-1,+1}, |A|=k, f=n-k>=1, S_j(z)=sum_{i in F} w_ji z_i. Since the non-constancy of gate j on {0,1}^A depends only on the offset S_j(z) (A-weights and t_j are fixed), N(A,z) = #{j : S_j(z) in W_j}, where W_j is a set of at most k integers (S0006 step 1). Let F_r(p) = sum_j P[S_j in W_j | first r bits of z equal p], for a prefix p of length r. Then (i) F_r(p) = (F_{r+1}(p0)+F_{r+1}(p1))/2; (ii) each F_r(p) is an exact finite sum: given p, S_j = a_j(p) + (signed Bin(f-r,1/2)), so P[S_j in W_j | p] = sum over s in W_j of the binomial pmf at the shifted index. Algorithm: start with the empty prefix; at each of the f steps append the bit b minimising F_{r+1}(pb). By (i), F is non-increasing along the path, so the output z* satisfies N(A,z*) = F_f(z*) <= F_0 = sum_j P[S_j in W_j] <= m k / sqrt(f) (S0006). Running time: f steps, each O(m k f) exact arithmetic (rational with denominator 2^f, or exact integers), so poly(n, m). Scope: +-1 weights; the output is ONE restriction z*, not a CAPP algorithm.

question: Q-2f96f7e0f1
statement: LEMMA D (derandomised window bound, scope: +-1 weights on A and F, A fixed). Setting: disjoint A, F with |A|=k>=1, |F|=f>=1; gates g_j(x,z) = [sum_{i in A} w_ji x_i + sum_{i in F} w_ji z_i >= t_j], w_ji in {-1,+1}, t_j integer, j=1..m. For z in {0,1}^F let N(z) = number of j with g_j(.,z) non-constant on {0,1}^A. CLAIM: a deterministic procedure computes z* in {0,1}^F with N(z*) <= m k / sqrt(f) using O(m f^3) arithmetic operations on integers of O(f) bits. PROOF. (a) Let L_j = sum_{i in A} min(0,w_ji), U_j = sum_{i in A} max(0,w_ji); U_j - L_j = k. g_j is non-constant given z iff L_j + S_j < t_j <= U_j + S_j, S_j = sum_{i in F} w_ji z_i, i.e. S_j lies in an integer window of exactly k integers. (b) By S0006(b) (sign flip y_i = z_i or 1-z_i, Y ~ Bin(f,1/2), central binomial bound), for uniform z: Pr[g_j non-constant] <= k C(f,floor(f/2))/2^f <= k/sqrt(f). (c) For a prefix b in {0,1}^p of z, let E(b) = sum_j Pr_{z''}[g_j non-constant | z_{1..p} = b], z'' uniform on {0,1}^{f-p}. Then E(b) = (E(b0)+E(b1))/2, so min(E(b0),E(b1)) <= E(b). The procedure sets b_{p+1} to the minimiser; E is non-increasing along the run; at p=f, E equals N(z*) because each term is then 0/1. E(empty) = sum_j Pr[...] <= m k/sqrt(f) by (b). Hence N(z*) <= m k/sqrt(f). (d) Cost: for a fixed prefix, Pr[g_j non-constant | prefix] = Pr[t_j - U_j - c_j <= S'_j < t_j - L_j - c_j] with c_j the fixed-prefix contribution and S' the free-part sum. S' has a distribution over [-f,f] computed by a DP in O(f^2) operations (exact, with weights 2^{-(f-p)}). Each step evaluates 2 candidates over m gates: O(m f^2) per step, O(m f^3) in total. QED. SCOPE AND LIMITS: (i) +-1 weights only; (ii) A fixed in advance (the adaptive choice of A, G0016, is still open); (iii) the bound m k/sqrt(f) is below m only when k < sqrt(f), so it gives no saving at k = sqrt(n) and m = n^1.5; (iv) no CAPP algorithm follows: the later cost is still 2^k times the surviving count. WHAT IT CLOSES: the deterministic-bound part of G0007(ii) and G0008(i) in the form 'a poly-time computable z with a deterministic surviving-gate bound', for fixed A and +-1 weights. It does not close the adaptive-A question, general integer weights (G0009(b)), or Chen-Williams 2019 (Q-05bce643f5). DEPENDENCY: relies on the S0006(b) window step (CLAIMED, not reviewed by this session). Hand check of steps (a)-(c) passed; exact enumeration cm-5cb23cf8bfcd43c4 (43680 cases, 0 violations) and derandomisation check cm-e0aa5fa35d4a4793 (400 instances; N(z*) = E_last <= E_root <= bound, E monotone, 0 violations) are exploratory computations and are not part of the proof.

question: Q-2f96f7e0f1
statement: LEMMA D2 (self-contained replacement of S0031 LEMMA D; supersedes it, no CLAIMED premise). Scope: disjoint A, F, |A|=k>=1, |F|=f>=1; w_ji in {-1,+1} for i in A and i in F; t_j integers, j=1..m; g_j(x,z)=[sum_A w_ji x_i + sum_F w_ji z_i >= t_j]; N(z)=#{j: g_j(.,z) non-constant on {0,1}^A}. CLAIM: a deterministic poly-time procedure outputs z* in {0,1}^F with N(z*) <= m k / sqrt(f). PROOF. Step 1 (value set): V_j = {sum_A w_ji x_i} = all integers in [L_j,U_j], L_j=sum_A min(0,w_ji), U_j=sum_A max(0,w_ji), U_j-L_j=k (positive-weight subset sums cover 0..p, negative cover -q..0, union covers -q..p). So g_j non-constant given z iff L_j+S_j < t_j <= U_j+S_j with S_j=sum_F w_ji z_i, i.e. S_j in W_j = {t_j-U_j,...,t_j-L_j-1}, exactly k integers. Step 2 (sign flip): y_i=z_i if w_ji=+1, y_i=1-z_i if w_ji=-1. Then S_j = Y - r_j, Y=sum_F y_i ~ Bin(f,1/2), r_j=#{i in F: w_ji=-1}. So Pr_z[S_j in W_j] = sum over s in W_j of Pr[Y=s+r_j] <= k C(f,floor(f/2))/2^f <= k/sqrt(f), using C(f,floor(f/2))/2^f <= 1/sqrt(f) for all f>=1 (from C(2n,n)/4^n <= 1/sqrt(3n+1), n>=1, and checked at f=1). Step 3 (derandomisation): for a prefix b of z of length p, E(b)=sum_j Pr over the free suffix of [S_j in W_j]. E(b)=(E(b0)+E(b1))/2, so choosing the next bit minimising E never increases E; at p=f, E = N(z*) since each term is 0/1; E(empty) <= mk/sqrt(f) by Step 2. Hence N(z*) <= mk/sqrt(f). Cost: exact distribution of each suffix sum by DP, O(f^2) per gate per candidate, O(m f^3) total, integers of O(f) bits. SCOPE AND LIMITS: fixed A; +-1 weights only; bound is below m only when k < sqrt(f), so no saving at k=sqrt(n), m=n^1.5; no CAPP algorithm (cost still 2^k times survivors). CLOSES: the deterministic fixed-A part of G0007(ii) and G0008(i) for +-1 weights. OPEN: adaptive choice of A (G0016), integer weights (G0009(b)), survivor approximation (G0007(iii)), Chen-Williams 2019 (Q-05bce643f5). Exploratory checks cm-5cb23cf8bfcd43c4 and cm-e0aa5fa35d4a4793 are not part of the proof. Status: CLAIMED, not reviewed; this session cannot review it.

question: Q-2f96f7e0f1
statement: INTEGER-WEIGHT SURVIVOR LEMMA (G0009(b)). Setting: A, F partition [n], |A| = k >= 1, f = |F| >= 1, integer weights w_ji with |w_ji| >= 1 for i in F (zero weights on A allowed), thresholds T_j in Z, gates g_j(x,z) = [sum_A w_ji x_i + sum_F w_ji z_i >= T_j] on x in {0,1}^A, z in {0,1}^F. Let M_j = sum_{i in A} |w_ji| and N(z) = #{j : g_j(., z) non-constant}. CLAIM: (i) for each j, #{z : g_j(., z) non-constant} <= M_j * C(f, floor(f/2)); hence P_z[non-constant] <= M_j / sqrt(f). (ii) E_z N(z) <= (sum_j M_j)/sqrt(f) <= m k B / sqrt(f) if |w| <= B on A. (iii) The conditional-expectation fixing of Lemma S-DERAND gives z* with N(z*) <= E_z N. PROOF. (1) Window: g_j is non-constant iff min_x (A-sum) + S < T_j <= max_x (A-sum) + S, where S = sum_F w_ji z_i. This holds for any integer weights, with no gap condition. With L = sum_A min(0,w_ji) and U = sum_A max(0,w_ji), non-constancy is equivalent to T_j - U <= S <= T_j - L - 1. This is an integer window with exactly U - L = M_j integers. (2) Point masses: put eps_i = 2 z_i - 1 in {-1,+1}. Then S = s iff sum_F w_ji eps_i = 2s - sum_F w_ji. Since |w_ji| >= 1, Erdos's Littlewood-Offord theorem (1945: for reals |b_i| >= 1, an open interval of length 2 contains at most C(f, floor(f/2)) of the 2^f sums sum eps_i b_i) gives #{z : S = s} <= C(f, floor(f/2)) for every integer s. (3) Union: #{z : S in window} <= sum over the M_j window integers of #{z : S = s} <= M_j C(f, floor(f/2)). Dividing by 2^f and using C(f, floor(f/2))/2^f <= 1/sqrt(f) (f >= 1) gives (i). Summing over j gives (ii). (4) Step (iii) uses only that N is an integer-valued function whose expectation is known; the DP for E_p has integer sums in [-fB, fB], so it costs O(m f^2 B) per evaluation and O(m f^3 B) in total. SCOPE: non-zero integer weights on F, arbitrary integers on A, fixed A. Zero weights on F reduce f to f' = #nonzero F-weights, giving 1/sqrt(f'). The ±1 lemma S0006 is the case M_j = k. The lemma says nothing about all z simultaneously, adaptive A, or Chen-Williams 2019.

statement: PROCEDURE (CLAIMED, not reviewed). Algorithm: keep a table indexed by S = (S_1..S_k), S_c = sum over processed variables q of w_{c,q} x_q. Start with {(0,..,0): 1}. For variable i = 1..n and each b in {0,1}, add w_{c,i} b to every coordinate S_c and accumulate counts. Output the sum of table counts over final S with sum_j v_j [S_{c(j)} >= t_j] >= T. Correctness: [w_c . x >= t] = [S_c(x) >= t], so F(x) = G(S(x)) for a fixed function G. By induction, after i variables the table maps each S to the number of length-i prefixes with partial sums S. Summing over final S gives sum_x [G(S(x)) >= T] = #F. Bound: after i steps each S_c lies in [-Wi, Wi], so the table has at most (2Wi+1)^k entries and the total time is O(n (2Wn+1)^k (k+m)) arithmetic operations. Scope of consequence: for k <= eps n / log2(2Wn+1), the time is 2^{eps n} poly(n, m, W), so #SAT of THR o THR with at most k distinct bottom weight vectors is computed in 2^{eps n} poly time.
