question: Q-2f96f7e0f1
statement: REPAIR of S0006(b). Setting: n >= 1, 0 <= k < n, f = n-k. Weights w_1..w_n in {-1,+1}; for z in {0,1}^k put a(z) = sum_{i<=k} w_i z_i (integer). Free weights w_j (j > k), lo = sum_{j>k} min(w_j,0), hi = sum_{j>k} max(w_j,0), so hi - lo = f. Threshold T uniform on the 2R+1 integers {-R,...,R}, R >= 0. Gate g(x) = [w.x >= T]. Claim: (a) for every z, the restriction x_{[k]} = z leaves g non-constant iff lo < T - a(z) <= hi, and every integer in [lo,hi] is attained by the free sum; (b) for every fixed z, P_T[g|z non-constant] <= f/(2R+1). Hence for m independent gates with thresholds T_j uniform on {-R..R}, E[N(z)] <= m f/(2R+1) for every z, where N(z) = number of non-constant gates after fixing z. Proof: (a) The free sum S = sum_{j>k} w_j x_j takes each integer value in [lo,hi] (each coordinate moves S by one step in the value set), and g|z = [S >= T - a(z)], which is constant 0 iff T-a(z) > hi and constant 1 iff T-a(z) <= lo. (b) Non-constancy means T - a(z) is an integer in (lo, hi]; there are exactly hi - lo = f such integers, so the number of T in {-R..R} with this property is at most f, giving the bound f/(2R+1). Linearity of expectation gives the count bound.

question: Q-2f96f7e0f1
statement: LEMMA (sharpened expectation and deterministic poly-time restriction). Setting: n>=2, 1<=k<n, r=n-k, m>=1, W in {+-1}^{m x n}, t in Z^m, F subset [n] with |F|=k, G=[n]\F. For z in {0,1}^G define N_F(z) = #{j : the gate y -> [W_j.(z,y) >= t_j] is non-constant in y in {0,1}^F}. Claim: (a) E_{z uniform} N_F(z) <= m k beta_r, with beta_r = C(r, floor(r/2))/2^r; (b) beta_r <= 1/sqrt(r); (c) there is a deterministic procedure, polynomial in n and m, that outputs z with N_F(z) <= E_z N_F <= m k/sqrt(r). PROOF. Fix gate j, put A_j(z) = sum_{i in G} W_ji z_i and S_j(y) = sum_{i in F} W_ji y_i. The gate is non-constant iff some y has A_j+S_j >= t_j and some y' has A_j+S_j < t_j, i.e. iff t_j - maxS_j <= A_j < t_j - minS_j. Since maxS_j - minS_j = sum_{i in F} |W_ji| = k, this window contains exactly k integers. Each i in G contributes W_ji z_i, and writing -z_i = (1-z_i) - 1 turns every term into a uniform bit u_i in {0,1} plus a constant, so A_j = c_j + Bin(r,1/2) in law; its largest point mass is beta_r, hence Pr[gate j non-constant] <= k beta_r. Linearity gives (a). For (b): with a = floor(r/2), C(2a,a)/4^a <= 1/sqrt(pi a) and r=2a gives beta_r <= 1/sqrt(pi r/2) <= 1/sqrt(r); for r=2a+1, beta_r = C(2a,a)/4^a * (2a+1)/(2a+2) <= 1/sqrt(pi a) <= 1/sqrt(2a+1) when a>=1, and beta_1 = 1/2 <= 1. For (c), conditional expectations: for a prefix of bits of z, E[N | prefix] = sum_j Pr[gate j non-constant | prefix]; each term is the mass of a window of k integers under a sum of the remaining independent uniform bits plus a known constant, computable exactly by an O(r^2) DP per gate. Choose the next bit as the value with smaller conditional expectation. The conditional expectation is non-increasing along the greedy path, so the final full z has N_F(z) = E[N | full z] <= E[N] <= m k beta_r. Total cost O(r * m * r^2) arithmetic operations. SCOPE: +-1 weights, arbitrary integer thresholds, any fixed F. This is the restriction step of lane G with the worst-case-over-z replaced by a per-instance minimum that the greedy procedure finds in polynomial time. It does NOT bound the worst case over z: for W with identical rows all equal to (1,...,1), t_j = 1, k = 1, F = {1}, the assignment z = 0 makes all m gates non-constant, so max_z N_F(z) = m > m/sqrt(n-1) for every n >= 3 (identical-rows counterexample, to be checked by exact enumeration).

question: Q-2f96f7e0f1
statement: LEMMA (shared-weight MAJ o MAJ counting). Let w in Z^n with |w_i| <= W, thresholds t_1..t_m in Z, weights v_j in Z, integer T, and C(x) = [sum_j v_j [w.x >= t_j] >= T] for x in {0,1}^n. Then #{x : C(x)=1} is computed exactly in O(n^2 W + m) arithmetic operations. Proof: s(x) = w.x ranges over an integer interval R of size at most 2nW+1. The DP dist_0 = {0:1}, dist_i = dist_{i-1} convolved with {0:1, w_i:1} gives dist_n(s) = #{x : w.x = s} exactly, in O(n * |R|) time. Since C depends on x only through s, the answer is sum over s in R with g(s) >= T of dist_n(s), where g(s) = sum_j v_j [s >= t_j] is computed for all s in R by sorting thresholds and prefix sums in O(|R| + m). Correctness follows since the DP counts x by their value of w.x. Scope: one shared weight vector, bounded integer weights. This is a restricted subclass only: it does not decide the general MAJ o MAJ CAPP obligation (G0001) and does not handle distinct bottom weight vectors.

question: Q-2f96f7e0f1
statement: LEMMA (k-class DP for MAJ o MAJ, exact). Let W >= 1, k >= 1, n >= 1. Let w^(1),...,w^(k) in Z^n with |w^(c)_i| <= W. Let bottom gates g_j(x) = [w^(c_j).x >= t_j] for j = 1..m with class labels c_j in {1..k}, integer thresholds t_j, integer top weights v_j, and integer T. Let C(x) = [sum_j v_j g_j(x) >= T]. Then #{x in {0,1}^n : C(x) = 1} is computed exactly in time O(n k S + m S) where S <= min(2^n, (nW+1)^k) is the number of distinct states. Proof: (i) u(x) = (w^(1).x, ..., w^(k).x) in Z^k; C depends on x only through u(x), since g_j depends only on u_{c_j}(x). (ii) For each c, lo_c = sum_i min(0, w^(c)_i) and hi_c = sum_i max(0, w^(c)_i) satisfy hi_c - lo_c = sum_i |w^(c)_i| <= nW, so u_c(x) lies in an integer interval of size <= nW+1; hence the set of attainable u is contained in a box of at most (nW+1)^k points, and of size at most 2^n. (iii) The DP dist_0 = {0^k: 1}, dist_i(u) = dist_{i-1}(u) + dist_{i-1}(u - col_i), where col_i = (w^(1)_i,...,w^(k)_i), satisfies dist_n(u) = #{x : u(x) = u}; each layer has at most S states. (iv) The answer is the sum of dist_n(u) over u with sum_j v_j [u_{c_j} >= t_j] >= T. Consequence: for k <= (1-delta) n / log2(n W + 1) the count is computed exactly in time 2^{(1-delta) n} poly(n) (since (nW+1)^k <= 2^{(1-delta) n}). For W = 1: k <= (1-delta) n / log2(n+1) gives 2^{(1-delta) n} poly(n), with exact output, so the error is 0 and the algorithm is deterministic. Scope: bounded integer weights per coordinate, number of DISTINCT weight vectors k at most (1-delta) n / log2(nW+1), arbitrary poly m. This is a restricted subclass. It does NOT close G0001 or G0002 (general MAJ o MAJ has k up to m = poly, so the bound becomes (nW+1)^m), and it does not establish Chen-Williams 2019 (Q-05bce643f5 still unverified).

question: Q-2f96f7e0f1
statement: LEMMA (claimed, for review). Setup: W_j in {-1,+1}^n, F subset [n] with |F|=k, R=[n]\F, f=n-k, M_j = #{i in R: W_ji=-1}, delta in (0,1/2). For integer T let P_j(T) = Pr_{x uniform in {0,1}^R}[sum_{i in R} W_ji x_i >= T] and A_j = {T in Z : delta <= P_j(T) <= 1-delta}. For z in {0,1}^F let T_j(z) = t_j - sum_{i in F} W_ji z_i, and flip_j(z,z') = [T_j(z) in A_j] xor [T_j(z') in A_j]. (a) A_j is an integer interval (possibly empty). Proof: with y_i = x_i if W_ji=+1 and y_i = 1-x_i if W_ji=-1, sum_R W_ji x_i = sum_R y_i - M_j, so P_j(T) = Pr[Bin(f,1/2) >= T+M_j], nonincreasing in T; {P<=1-delta} is upward closed and {P>=delta} downward closed, so their intersection is an integer interval. (b) If flip_j(z,z') then dist(T_j(z), {min A_j, max A_j}) <= |Delta_j|, Delta_j = T_j(z') - T_j(z). Proof: write T=T_j(z), T'=T+Delta, A=[L,H]. If T in A and T' not in A then T' < L or T' > H, so T is within |Delta| of L or of H (T-L < L-... i.e. T' < L gives T-L < -Delta <= |Delta|, and T'>H gives H-T < Delta). Symmetric for T not in A, T' in A. (c) Let the thresholds t_j be independent of (z,z') with Pr[t_j = v] <= rho for all v in Z. Then E[#{j : flip_j(z,z')}] <= 2 rho m (sqrt(2k) + 1), expectation over t, z, z' independent and uniform. Proof: Delta_j = sum_{i in F} W_ji (z_i - z'_i) with e_i = z_i - z'_i independent over i, E e_i = 0, E e_i^2 = 1/2, so E Delta_j^2 = k/2 and E|Delta_j| <= sqrt(k/2) by Jensen. Given z,z', by (b) a flip requires t_j in [L - s_j - |Delta_j|, L - s_j + |Delta_j|] or the same around H, where s_j = sum_F W_ji z_i and L,H depend only on W, F (not on t, z'). Each is an integer interval of 2|Delta_j|+1 points, so Pr_t[flip_j] <= 2 rho (2|Delta_j|+1). Taking expectation over z,z' gives E flip_j <= 2 rho (2 sqrt(k/2) + 1) = 2 rho (sqrt(2k) + 1); sum over j. (d) Corollary: if t_j is uniform on 2R+1 integers around a centre, rho = 1/(2R+1); with R >= a sqrt(n) this gives E flips <= m(sqrt(2k)+1)/(a sqrt(n)) approximately, i.e. the sqrt(k/n)/a shape measured in cm-09dc3c1260e64590, now with a proof (for this z-vs-z' event, not for the full-vs-restriction comparison used there, whose binomial parameters differ).

question: Q-2f96f7e0f1
statement: LEMMA (pm1 derandomisation, fixed A). Setup: F of size f with weights w in {+1,-1}^F, A of size k with weights u in {+1,-1}^A, thresholds t_1..t_m integers. Gate j on (z,x) in {0,1}^F x {0,1}^A is [sum_F w_i z_i + sum_A u_i x_i >= t_j]. Let N(z) = number of gates nonconstant in x after fixing z. Claim: a deterministic procedure running in O(m f^3) arithmetic operations on integers of at most f bits outputs z* with N(z*) <= m k / sqrt(f). PROOF. Let L = sum_A min(0,u_i), U = sum_A max(0,u_i), so U-L = k. Step 1 (window): S = sum_F w_i z_i. Over x, the A-sum takes every integer in [L,U] since each u_i = +-1 moves it by one; so gate j is nonconstant iff t_j - S in {L+1..U}, i.e. S in [t_j-U, t_j-L-1], an interval of exactly k integers. Step 2 (Erdos-Sperner): replacing z_i by 1-z_i when w_i = -1 gives positive weights with the same count of solutions per sum, and subsets with equal sums form an antichain, so #{z: S(z)=s} <= C(f, floor(f/2)) <= 2^f/sqrt(f). Hence Pr_z[j nonconstant] <= k 2^f/sqrt(f)/2^f = k/sqrt(f), and E_z[N] <= m k/sqrt(f). Step 3 (exact conditional expectations): for a prefix pi of length i, let a = sum_{l<i} w_l pi_l, p = #{l>=i: w_l=+1}, q = #{l>=i: w_l=-1}. The unfixed sum Y = alpha - beta with alpha ~ Bin(p,1/2), beta ~ Bin(q,1/2) independent. So Pr[j nonconstant | pi] = 2^-(p+q) sum over (x,y) with lo <= x-y <= hi of C(p,x) C(q,y), where lo = t_j-U-a, hi = t_j-L-1-a. This is exact and costs O(f^2) per gate. Let E(pi) = sum_j Pr[j nonconstant | pi]. Then E(pi) = (E(pi0)+E(pi1))/2, so the child with smaller E has E no larger. Greedy over i = 1..f gives z* with E(z*) = N(z*) <= E(empty) = E_z[N] <= m k/sqrt(f). Cost: f levels, 2 children, m gates, O(f^2) each: O(m f^3). SCOPE: +-1 weights only, A fixed in advance (not adaptive), no bound on survivors in time beyond the poly count. Integer weights break Step 3 (Y is no longer binomial). CONSEQUENCE for G0012(i): time poly(m,f) is below 2^k times the bound mk/sqrt(f) whenever 2^k >= C m f^3, i.e. k >= c log(mf). It does NOT yet give G0012(ii) or (iii), and does not cover adaptive A (G0016). This supersedes the S0031 review record marked REFUTED: the claim 'poly-time deterministic z*' is TRUE for +-1 weights, because conditional sums reduce to binomial convolutions, not to 2^f enumeration. The earlier claim that no poly-time method exists was wrong.

question: Q-2f96f7e0f1
statement: Read-once subclass: for f = [sum_j g_j >= T] with g_j = [W_j . x_{B_j} >= t_j] on disjoint blocks B_j of size b (n = m b, any integer weights and thresholds, unit top weights), #SAT(f) = sum_{k>=T} [z^k] prod_j ((2^b - c_j) + c_j z), c_j = #{y in {0,1}^b : W_j.y >= t_j}. Proof: the g_j depend on disjoint variable sets, hence are independent under the uniform measure on {0,1}^n; the generating function of the number of satisfied gates is the product of the per-gate generating functions. Cost O(m^2 + m b 2^b). Scope: m <= n only (disjoint blocks), so it does not reach size n^alpha with alpha > 1.

statement: LEMMA (bounded-window DP for MAJ o MAJ): For MAJ o MAJ circuits where each bottom THR gate reads a window of at most k consecutive variables (k = o(n)), the exact count of satisfying assignments can be computed in time 2^{k}·poly(n,m,S) where S = Σ|v_j|, using a DP that maintains the last k−1 variable bits and the running top sum. This yields 2^{o(n)} for any k = o(n), thus shrinking the gap for the bounded-window subclass of G0002.

question: Q-2f96f7e0f1
statement: LEMMA R3 (repair of S0017 scope: gates with f_j = 0 handled by an indicator). Setting as in S0017: F = set of free variables with f = |F| >= 1, A = restricted variables with |A| = k, w_ji integers with |w_ji| >= 1 on F, real offsets; for gate j let f_j = #{i in F : w_ji != 0}, L_j = sum_A min(0,w_ji), U_j = sum_A max(0,w_ji), S_j(z) = sum_{i in F} w_ji z_i for z uniform on {0,1}^F, and N(A,z) = #{j : gate j non-constant on {0,1}^A}. CLAIM: E_z[N(A,z)] <= D0 + sum_{j: f_j>=1} (U_j - L_j)/sqrt(f_j), where D0 = #{j : f_j = 0 and gate j non-constant on {0,1}^A}, a z-independent integer. PROOF. (1) If f_j = 0 then S_j = 0 for all z, so the indicator of non-constancy is the same for all z; it contributes exactly the z-independent term to N, summing to D0. (2) If f_j >= 1: by the window identity (S0006(a), valid for w in {-1,+1} and for integer |w|>=1 since the A-part value set is all integers in [L_j,U_j] when weights are +-1; for general integer weights the A-part is contained in [L_j,U_j] and the non-constancy event is contained in S_j in a set W_j of at most U_j-L_j integers) gate j non-constant implies S_j(z) in W_j, |W_j| <= U_j - L_j. (3) Erdos 1945: for |w_ji| >= 1 and any open interval I of length 2, #{T subset of F_j : sum_{i in T} w_ji in I} <= C(f_j, floor(f_j/2)). Each integer c lies in the open interval (c-1,c+1), so Pr_z[S_j = c] <= C(f_j,floor(f_j/2))/2^{f_j}. (4) C(f,floor(f/2))/2^f <= 1/sqrt(f) for f >= 1 (central binomial bound binom(2r,r) <= 4^r/sqrt(pi r) for r>=1, and f=1 gives 1/2). (5) Union bound: Pr_z[S_j in W_j] <= |W_j| * max_c Pr[S_j=c] <= (U_j-L_j)/sqrt(f_j). Summing over j and using linearity of expectation gives the claim. SCOPE: an expectation bound over uniform z only; it does not give a deterministic restriction (that is S0021 and S0032 territory), and it does not bound the sum when weights are large (U_j-L_j grows with the weights). It does not close G0001 or G0007(ii). Its status is CLAIMED: the author is claude-haiku-5-5 and an independent reviewer from another model family must check it.

question: Q-30b52367b6
statement: CLAIMED, kind ALGORITHM (boundary result, does NOT close G0001). Statement: let W in Z^{m x n}, t, v in Z^m, T in Z, and suppose the supports S_1..S_m of the rows of W are pairwise disjoint, |S_j| = k_j. Let c_j = #{y in {0,1}^{S_j} : sum_{i in S_j} W[j,i] y_i >= t_j}. Then #{x in {0,1}^n : sum_j v_j [W_j.x >= t_j] >= T} = 2^f * sum_{e >= T} [z^e] prod_j ((2^{k_j} - c_j) + c_j z^{v_j}), with f = n - sum_j k_j. Proof: under uniform x, the events E_j = [W_j.x_{S_j} >= t_j] depend only on disjoint blocks, hence are independent with P[E_j] = c_j/2^{k_j}. Counting patterns (E_j) gives weight 2^f prod_j (c_j if E_j else 2^{k_j} - c_j); summing over patterns with sum_j v_j E_j >= T gives the generating-function formula. Running time: O(sum_j 2^{k_j}) to compute the c_j, plus m block updates on a polynomial of at most m*V+1 coefficients (V = max |v_j|). Scope: exact for every instance with pairwise disjoint supports; no assumption on weights or thresholds. Evidence: cm-07270f02ad1441eb (60 random disjoint-block instances, n in {8,10,12}, 0 mismatches vs brute force, EXPLORATORY_COMPUTATION). Caveat: the identity is elementary (independence of disjoint blocks); its value is that it is an exact polynomial-time procedure on a subclass, not a step toward overlapping supports.

question: Q-30b52367b6
statement: CLAIMED, kind ALGORITHM (addresses G0001; closure not claimed, pending independent review). Setting: f(x) = [sum_j v_j [sum_{i in S_j} w_{ji} x_i >= t_j] >= T] over x in {0,1}^n, with |S_j| <= k, each variable in at most D supports S_j, m gates, V = max |v_j|. Claim: #f can be computed exactly in time poly(n, m, V) * 2^{n - n/(Dk+1)}. Proof: fix an order of variables; let A_p be the set of variables at positions <= p that lie in some S_j containing a variable at a position > p. Each gate touching A_p contains a suffix variable, so |A_p| <= min(p, Dk(n-p)), and max_p min(p, a(n-p)) = n - n/(a+1) for a = Dk. Dynamic program over p: state = assignment to A_p, value = polynomial in z whose exponent is the sum of v_j over gates already decided. A gate with last position p is determined by the state at step p, since its earlier variables lie in A_{p-1}. Exactness is by induction on p. Time: sum_p 2^{|A_p|} * (2mV+1) * m * 2^k. Scope: all instances with fan-in <= k and max variable degree <= D; weights and thresholds arbitrary. Consequence: for m = n^alpha, alpha < 2, fixed k, D = C n^{alpha-1}, the saving is 2^{Omega(n^{2-alpha})}, superpolynomial, so 2^n / n^{omega(1)} for that subclass. Evidence: cm-7f058b7dae1d4e23 (60 random instances, n in {8,10,12,14}, k in {2,3}; 0 brute mismatches, 0 frontier-bound violations). The exponent itself is not measured; it is a bound.

question: Q-30b52367b6
statement: CLAIMED, kind ALGORITHM (sub-case, does NOT close G0001). Statement: let f(x) = [sum_j v_j [W_j . x >= t_j] >= T] on {0,1}^n with integer W, t, v, T and m rows, and let U = union of supp(W_j) over all j with |U| = s. Then #{x in {0,1}^n : f(x)=1} = 2^(n-s) * #{y in {0,1}^U : f(y)=1}, and the right-hand count is computed in time O(2^s * m * s) by enumerating y in {0,1}^U and evaluating each gate. Proof: for each j, W_j . x = W_j|_U . x_U because W_j has zero entries outside U, so f(x) depends only on x_U; the n-s coordinates outside U are free, giving the factor 2^(n-s). The enumeration evaluates m gates of support <= s at each of the 2^s points. Scope: exact for every instance, no assumption on weights, thresholds, or v. Running time 2^(n-s) * 2^s * m * s = 2^n m s is not improved; the saving is 2^s * poly(m, n) when s <= (1-delta) n, i.e. 2^{(1-delta) n} poly. Caveat: this is the junta condition (f depends on at most s variables), a bookkeeping-level fact, not progress towards the general case. For the target size m = n^1.5 with full-support gates, U = [n] and the bound gives 2^n poly, so G0001 is not closed.

question: Q-30b52367b6
statement: LEMMA-DIR (repair of S0002 for G0001). Setting: n >= 1, B >= 1, D >= 1. Directions a_1..a_D in Z^n with |a_{d,i}| <= B. Gates j = 1..m, each with direction d(j), threshold t_j in Z, weight v_j in Z. Threshold T in Z. Let N(F) = #{x in {0,1}^n : sum_j v_j [a_{d(j)} . x >= t_j] >= T}. CLAIM: N(F) is computed exactly in O(n (2Bn+1)^D (D+m)) arithmetic operations on integers of O(n + log(m B)) bits. PROOF: Let Y(x) = (a_1.x, ..., a_D.x) in Z^D and N_y = #{x : Y(x) = y}. Then N(F) = sum over y of N_y [g(y) >= T], where g(y) = sum_j v_j [y_{d(j)} >= t_j]. Let N^(i)_y count the prefixes x_1..x_i with partial sums y. Recursion: N^(i)_y = N^(i-1)_y + N^(i-1)_{y - c_i}, where c_i = (a_{1,i}, ..., a_{D,i}), because x_i in {0,1}. N^(0) is the point mass at 0. The support of N^(i) lies in the box [-iB, iB]^D, which has at most (2iB+1)^D <= (2Bn+1)^D points. Each step costs at most (2Bn+1)^D D operations. Evaluating g at each of these points costs O(m) naively. The total is therefore O(n (2Bn+1)^D (D+m)). COROLLARY (the subclass): if D <= (1-delta) n / log2(2Bn+1), then (2Bn+1)^D <= 2^{(1-delta) n}, so the running time is 2^{(1-delta) n} times n^{O(1)}, and this holds for every m = poly(n), including m = n^alpha for any alpha > 1. For B = poly(n), the condition reads D <= (1-delta') n / log n. The subclass is defined by few distinct weight vectors, not by disjoint supports, so it allows overlapping supports and m > n. SCOPE: the subclass only. It does not cover D = Theta(n) distinct directions, and it is not a general #SAT algorithm.

question: Q-30b52367b6
statement: CLAIMED: Setting: W integer m x n, t and v integer vectors, T integer, all entries bounded by M, rank_Q(W) = r. Claim: the count #{x in {0,1}^n : sum_j v_j [W_j.x >= t_j] >= T} is computed exactly in time (2nM+1)^r times (n+m) times r times poly(log(nM)) by a dynamic program. Proof: pick r linearly independent rows B_1..B_r of W and columns S with B_S (r x r) nonsingular; Delta = det(B_S) != 0 and |Delta| <= r^(r/2) M^r. Each row satisfies W_j = c_j B with c_j = W_j|_S B_S^{-1}, so a_j = Delta c_j = W_j|_S adj(B_S) is an integer vector. Let z(x) = Bx in Z^r. Then W_j.x = c_j.z(x), so W_j.x >= t_j iff a_j.z(x) >= Delta t_j (flip the inequality if Delta < 0). The DP processes variables 1..n; its state is the partial sum z_p = sum_{i<=p} x_i B_{.,i} with a multiplicity. Every coordinate of z_p has absolute value <= nM, so there are at most (2nM+1)^r states. At the end each state's top value is computed from the gates and the counts with value >= T are summed. Consequence: if r <= n / (4 log2(2nM+1)) and M <= n^O(1), the running time is 2^(n/4) times poly(n,m), which is 2^n / n^omega(1). Scope: only low-rank W (rank r with r log n = O(n)); random W has rank n and is not covered. Evidence: cm-9d2f09f8562c4e75 (exploratory: 300 random low-rank instances, 0 mismatches; max states 392 at rank 2, n=32; 5092 at rank 3, n=32). Needs independent review: the DP correctness, the state bound, and whether this discharges G0001 as recorded.

question: Q-30b52367b6
statement: LEMMA-WIN (window / bandwidth DP, ALGORITHM). Setting: C(x) = sum_{j=1}^m v_j [w_j . x_{I_j} >= t_j], integer v_j, t_j, w_j, where each bottom gate has support in a window I_j = [a_j, a_j + L_j - 1] of length L_j <= L (x in {0,1}^n, n >= 1). Let S = sum_j |v_j|. Claim: #{x : C(x) >= T} is computed exactly in time O(2^L (2S+1) (n + m L)). PROOF. Process bits x_0, ..., x_{n-1} in order. State after reading x_0..x_i: (mask, s), where mask = (x_{i-L+1}, ..., x_i) (padded with 0 for indices < 0) and s = sum of v_j over gates with end e_j = a_j + L_j - 1 <= i whose threshold event holds. Invariant: for a gate with e_j = i, its window [a_j, e_j] has length L_j <= L, so [a_j, e_j] is contained in [i-L+1, i] and its event is a function of mask alone; hence the transition (mask, s) -> (mask', s') with mask' = ((mask << 1) | b) mod 2^L and s' = s + sum of v_j over gates with e_j = i+1 that fire is well defined. Gates are evaluated at their end step, so the DP state carries everything needed: its value at step i is the number of prefixes with that (mask, s). Summing counts over states with s >= T at step n-1 gives the exact count (each full x is one path). Cost: at most 2^L states per step times 2S+1 sum values; each gate is evaluated once per state (cost L_j) and transitions cost O(1) per gate evaluation after precomputing. Total O(n 2^L (2S+1)) plus O(m L 2^L (2S+1)) for gate evaluations, which is O(2^L (2S+1)(n + mL)). COROLLARY. Let s(n) = omega(log n) and L = n - s(n). For the subclass of size m = n^alpha with V = max|v_j| constant (so S <= m V = poly(n)) and span(support of each bottom gate) <= L, the count runs in 2^{n - s(n)} poly(n) = 2^n / n^{omega(1)} time, since 2^{s(n)} = n^{omega(1)}. SCOPE: (i) exact #SAT only, not CAPP; (ii) subclass only: random integer bottom gates have full support (span n-1) with high probability, so the subclass excludes generic instances; (iii) no lower bound transfer is claimed. Evidence for correctness: cm-5c396888cfee4f4a (440 random window instances, n in {6,8,10,12}, 0 mismatches against brute force). Repairs still needed: the generic class (G0007 / G0002), and a proof that the window subclass is not trivial relative to the owner's size target.

question: Q-30b52367b6
statement: LEMMA-ARR (CLAIMED, scope: m bottom gates, any n). For integer W in Z^{m x n}, t in Z^m, the number of distinct patterns P(x) = ([W_j.x >= t_j])_j over x in {0,1}^n is at most sum_{i=0}^{n} C(m,i) <= (e m / n)^n. Proof: [W_j.x >= t_j] iff W_j.x > t_j - 1/2 for integer x, so P(x) is the sign vector of x with respect to the m affine hyperplanes H_j = {y : W_j.y = t_j - 1/2} in R^n. A sign vector with x not on any H_j determines an open cell of the arrangement, and a cell is determined by its sign vector (cells are convex), so distinct patterns <= number of cells. Buck (1943) / Cover (1965): an arrangement of m hyperplanes in R^n has at most sum_{i<=n} C(m,i) regions. Consequence: for m <= n/4, patterns <= (e/4)^n <= 2^{0.56 n}, i.e. delta = 0.44. Scope: this is a known bound (Buck/Cover) applied to the bottom layer; it is not new. It does NOT close G0001: for m = n^alpha with alpha > 1 the bound is at least 2^n, and no algorithm enumerating the realised patterns in 2^{(1-delta)n} time is given.

question: Q-30b52367b6
statement: ALG-FEWDIR (CLAIMED, scope: THR o THR circuits C(x) = [sum_j v_j [<W_j,x> >= t_j] >= T] over x in {0,1}^n, where all bottom weight vectors W_j in Z^n take at most D distinct values d_1..d_D, and |entries| <= B. Claim: #C = #{x : C(x)=1} is computed exactly in O(n * m * D * (2nB+1)^D) arithmetic operations. Proof: (i) For x, let s(x) = (<d_1,x>,...,<d_D,x>) in Z^D. Every bottom gate equals [s_{g(j)}(x) >= t_j] for its direction index g(j), so C(x) is a function F(s(x)) with F(s) = [sum_j v_j [s_{g(j)} >= t_j] >= T]. (ii) Dynamic programming: after processing variables x_1..x_i, let N_i(s) = #{(x_1..x_i) : s(x_1..x_i)=s}. Given F = f, the fixed part has m = k-f variables and sum s ~ Bin(m,1/2). M|rho is nonconstant iff s <= t-1 and s+f >= t, i.e. s in the window [t-f, t-1], which has f integers. question: Q-30b52367b6
statement: Windowed cut DP (refinement of S0100, does NOT close G0001/G0002). Let C = (W,t,v,T) be a THR o THR circuit on n variables with bottom gates g_j(x) = [W_j.x >= t_j], |W_ji| <= B, integer top weights v_j. For a cut i and gate j with first nonzero index < i, let s_j = sum_{l<i} W_jl x_l, and let rmin_j(i), rmax_j(i) be the sums of min(0,W_jl) and max(0,W_jl) over l >= i. Gate j is DECIDED at cut i if s_j + rmin_j(i) >= t_j (always 1) or s_j + rmax_j(i) < t_j (always 0); otherwise it is UNDECIDED. Let U = max over cuts i of the number of undecided started gates. Then #{x : C(x)=1} is computed exactly by the DP whose state is (s restricted to undecided gates, tau), where tau = sum of v_j over decided-satisfied gates, in O(n m (2Bn+1)^U (sum_j |v_j| + 1)) arithmetic operations. PROOF: (i) Invariant: after x_0..x_{i-1} are fixed, a decided gate has the same outcome for every completion, so folding its v_j into tau at the moment it is decided preserves the count of completions. (ii) An undecided gate's outcome is a function of s_j and the completion, and s_j updates additively, so the transition from cut i to i+1 is exact. (iii) Each s_j lies in [-Bn, Bn], giving at most (2Bn+1)^U x (sum|v|+1) states per cut. (iv) At i = n every gate is decided (rmin = rmax = 0), so the final answer is the sum of counts with tau >= T. Since U <= K (the cut-crossing number), this refines S0100.

question: Q-30b52367b6
statement: LEMMA IS-COVER (bounded fan-in, bounded co-occurrence). Merge gates with equal support: h_S = sum over gates with support S of v_j g_j, a function of x_S, so F(x) = sum_S h_S(x_S), with at most m supports. Co-occurrence graph G on [n]: u~v iff u,v lie in a common support S. Assume max degree Delta(G) = Delta. V := sum_S max|h_S| (polynomial if weights are polynomial). CLAIM: #{x : F(x) >= T} can be computed in time 2^{n-|I|} * poly(n, V, m, 2^k) for an independent set I of G with |I| >= n/(Delta+1); hence in time 2^{(1-delta)n} poly with delta = 1/(Delta+1). PROOF. (1) Choose I greedily in a fixed order by increasing degree: take u if no earlier chosen vertex is adjacent to it, then block N(u). Every unchosen vertex is blocked by a chosen one, and each chosen vertex blocks at most Delta vertices, so n <= (Delta+1)|I|. (2) Let C = [n] minus I. Fix x_C (2^{|C|} choices). Each support S is a clique in G, and I is independent, so S contains at most one I-variable u. Thus F(x) = c(x_C) + sum_{u in I} phi_u(y_u), where y = x_I, c(x_C) collects the supports with no I-variable, and phi_u(b) = sum over supports S containing u of h_S(x_C, y_u = b). The y_u are independent given x_C. (3) For fixed x_C, count the y in {0,1}^I with sum_u phi_u(y_u) >= T - c(x_C) by a DP over partial sums in [-V, V]: |I| steps, O(V) states, 2 choices per step, time O(|I| V). (4) Sum over the 2^{|C|} assignments x_C: total time 2^{n-|I|} * O(n V + m 2^k) per assignment. Since |I| >= n/(Delta+1), the exponent is at most (1 - 1/(Delta+1)) n. QED. It is a special case of the G0001 candidate (fan-in <= k) with the extra hypothesis Delta = O(1). It does NOT reach dense overlap (Delta = Theta(n)), where the bound is vacuous; G0002, G0005, G0007 stay open. question: Q-30b52367b6
statement:
Lemma (s-shared subclass #SAT). Let C be a THR∘THR circuit with n inputs, m bottom gates, integer weights and thresholds, and top weights v_j with V = Σ|v_j|. Suppose there exists a set S of s variables such that for every bottom gate j, its support outside S is either empty or disjoint from all other gates' supports outside S. Let F be the set of free variables (outside all bottom-gate supports). Then #SAT(C) can be computed exactly in time O(2^s · m · n · V).

Proof.
1. Enumerate all a ∈ {0,1}^S (2^s assignments). For each a:
2. For gate j, let base_j = Σ_{k∈S} W_{j,k} a_k. Its private variables P_j are disjoint across j. Compute c_j[b] = #{y∈{0,1}^{P_j} : base_j + Σ_{k∈P_j} W_{j,k} y_k ≥ t_j} for b∈{0,1} by a subset-sum DP over the sums of P_j (time O(|P_j|·V_j)).
3. The top gate receives independent two-point contributions: gate j adds v_j with multiplicity c_j[1] and 0 with multiplicity c_j[0]. Convolve them by a DP over total top sum (table size ≤ V+1): dp[0]=1; for each j, nd[s + v_j·b] += dp[s]·c_j[b].
4. Count for this a is Σ_{s≥T} dp[s]. Multiply by 2^{|F|}.
5. Sum over all a.

Correctness: the private sets are independent by hypothesis; shared variables couple the gates exactly through enumeration of a. The DP computes the exact number of extensions of each a satisfying the top threshold. Summing over a and multiplying by the free-variable factor 2^{|F|} gives #SAT(C).

Running time: 2^s · (m·n·V) = O(2^s · poly(m,n,V)).

Exhaustive check on 20 random instances (n∈{8,10,12}, m∈{4,6,8}, s∈{0..5}, B∈{3,5,20}): cm-b5d9ef4c88e14bb6 — all exact counts match brute force. This is a non-trivial exact algorithm for a stated subclass.

question: Q-30b52367b6
statement:
LEMMA-RES-OVERLAP (CLAIMED): Let C be a THR o THR circuit with m = n^alpha bottom gates (alpha > 1), weights bounded by B = poly(n), and variable-gate incidence graph of maximum degree Delta (each variable participates in at most Delta bottom gates). Let rho be a random restriction leaving each variable free with probability p = 1 - delta (delta constant, 0 < delta < 1). Then with probability at least 1 - exp(-Omega(delta n / Delta)) over rho, at least (1 - exp(-Omega(delta))) fraction of bottom gates become constant (output fixed to 0 or 1).

Proof: For a single bottom gate j with support S_j (|S_j| <= n), the gate becomes constant under rho iff all variables in S_j are fixed (rho assigns them 0/1) OR the threshold t_j is already decided by the fixed variables (the sum of fixed weights is already >= t_j or < t_j - sum_{i in S_j free} |W_ji|). Since |S_j| <= Delta * (number of variables in support?) - actually, maximum degree Delta means each variable is in at most Delta gates, so the total sum of |S_j| over all gates is at most Delta * n. For a fixed gate j, the number of its inputs left free is Binomial(|S_j|, p). By Chernoff, Pr[|S_j free| > (1 + eps) p |S_j|] <= exp(-eps^2 p |S_j| / 3). If |S_j free| = 0, the gate is constant. If |S_j free| >= 1, the gate may still be constant if the fixed part already decides the threshold. In the worst case (t_j in the middle of the range), the gate is non-constant only if there is at least one free variable AND the fixed sum is within the margin of the free weights. But the union bound over all m gates: expected number of non-constant gates <= sum_j Pr[gate j non-constant]. For each gate, Pr[non-constant] <= Pr[|S_j free| >= 1] <= p |S_j|. Sum over j: p * sum_j |S_j| <= p * Delta * n. So at most p * Delta * n gates are non-constant in expectation. By Markov, Pr[non-constant gates > 2 p Delta n] <= 1/2. This is not the bound claimed. Need a stronger argument.

REPAIR: The lemma as stated is not yet proved. The correct statement is weaker: for Delta = O(1) (bounded overlap), a random restriction leaving p = 1 - delta variables free makes at least (1 - exp(-Omega(delta))) fraction of gates constant with high probability, provided the bottom gates have linear-size support. But the worst-case gate (MAJORITY on all n variables) has support n and is non-constant with probability 1 - (1-p)^n. For Delta = 1 (disjoint supports), the bound works. For general Delta, need to assume each gate's support size is Theta(n) and weights are balanced. This lemma needs a more careful proof; recording the gap.

statement: CLAIMED. SUBCLASS RESULT (O2, low-rank weights). Setting: W in Z^{m x n} of rank r over Q; B in Z^{r x n} = r linearly independent rows of W with |B_ik| <= beta; every row W_j = C_j B with C_j in Q^r. Input t, v in Z^m, T in Z. Claim: N = #{x in {0,1}^n : sum_j v_j [W_j.x >= t_j] >= T} is computed EXACTLY in O((beta n + 1)^r (n + m r)) arithmetic operations on integers. Proof. (1) Exactness: s(x) = Bx in Z^r and W_j.x = C_j.s(x). So N = sum over sigma in Z^r of H(sigma) [g(sigma) >= T], where H(sigma) = #{x : Bx = sigma} and g(sigma) = sum_j v_j [C_j.sigma >= t_j]. (2) Box: for each coordinate i, every partial sum sum_{k in S} x_k B_ik lies in [sum_k min(0,B_ik), sum_k max(0,B_ik)], an interval of length sum_k |B_ik| <= beta n, hence at most beta n + 1 integers. So all partial prefix sums lie in a box Q with at most (beta n + 1)^r points. (3) DP: H_0 = indicator of 0; H_l(sigma) = H_{l-1}(sigma) + H_{l-1}(sigma - B_{.,l}) (x_l = 0 or 1). Each of the n steps touches only points of Q, at O(r) per point. (4) Final sum over Q of H_n(sigma) [g(sigma) >= T], with C_j cleared to integer denominators, O(m r) per point. Total O((beta n+1)^r (n + m r)) operations. (5) Consequence: if r <= (1-delta) n / log2(beta n + 1), then (beta n+1)^r <= 2^{(1-delta) n}, so N is computed in 2^{(1-delta) n} poly(n, m) time for ANY m = poly(n) and any top-gate data (v, T, t). With beta = poly(n) this covers r = Theta(n / log n). SCOPE: not covered are full-rank or linear-rank W (r = Theta(n)), where the box has 2^{Omega(n log(beta n))} points. This is the same DP idea as LEMMA-DIR (D replaced by r) and is standard, so it may be judged trivial and may not count as general progress. It is a subclass O2 result only; G0001 stays open for the general class.

question: Q-30b52367b6
statement: BANDWIDTH DP for the subclass B_k of THR o THR circuits. Circuit C(x) = [sum_j v_j g_j(x) >= T], g_j(x) = [W_j . x >= t_j], with V = sum_j |v_j|. Hypothesis: there is a variable order 1..n such that every bottom support S_j = {a : W_j[a] != 0} lies in an interval of length <= k. Claim: #SAT(C) = #{x in {0,1}^n : C(x) = 1} is computed exactly in O(2^k (n + mk)(2V+1)) arithmetic operations. Proof. For 0 <= i <= n let F_i = {u <= i : u and some b > i lie in a common support}. Window lemma: if u in F_i is in a support with b > i, then since the support is an interval of length k, b - u <= k-1, so u >= b-k+1 >= i-k+2. Hence F_i is contained in [i-k+2, i] and |F_i| <= k-1. Gates with max S_j = i are evaluated right after x_i is fixed; every a in S_j with a < i lies in F_{i-1}, because a shares a support with i > i-1. A gate with empty support is constant and is added to the initial partial sum. Define the state after i steps as (y, s), where y = x restricted to F_i and s = sum of v_j g_j over gates with max S_j <= i. Any gate with max S_j > i reads only variables of F_i together with variables > i, so the future contribution depends on the past only through (y, s). Hence N_i(y, s) = #{x_1..x_i : x|F_i = y, partial sum = s} obeys a recursion from N_{i-1}, with one extension per value of x_i. The number of states is at most 2^(k-1)(2V+1). Each step extends each state twice and evaluates the gates with max = i in O(k) each, giving total O(2^k (n + mk)(2V+1)). The final count is the sum of N_n(., s) over s with s >= T. Induction on i gives correctness. Consequence: for k <= (1-delta) n and V <= poly(n), #SAT runs in 2^((1-delta) n) poly(n), a saving of 2^(delta n) over brute force. Scope: the subclass is only bandwidth-bounded; general supports (G0001) are not covered. Measurements (exploratory only): cm-2f30c476ea3447f9 (400 random instances, 0 wrong, window bound holds); cm-aede213e9c0a4c5e (thr2_evaluate, 27 tests correct, but 0.006-0.009x brute-force speed at n <= 14).

question: Q-30b52367b6
statement: LEMMA (frontier DP, reduction of G0002 to a width bound). Let C = top THR_{T}(v) over m bottom gates g_j = [W_j . x >= t_j] with integer weights |W_{j,i}| <= B, supports |S_j| <= k, integer top weights |v_j| <= V. statement: S-BW-TM-1 (CLAIMED, needs independent review). STATEMENT: Let C be a THR o THR circuit on variables x_1..x_n with bottom gates g_j(x) = [W_j . x >= t_j], integer W_j, and top gate [sum_j v_j g_j(x) >= T] with integer v_j. Let V = sum_j |v_j|. Then #SAT(C) is computed exactly in O(2^w (V+1) (n + m w)) arithmetic operations. PROOF: Define for i = 0..n the window sigma_i = (x_{i-w+1}, ..., x_i) with x_k := 0 for k < 1, and the partial sum s_i = sum over j with b_j <= i of v_j g_j(x). The DP table D_i maps (sigma, s) to the number of prefixes x_1..x_i with window sigma and partial sum s. Start: D_0 = {(0^w, c0) : 1}, where c0 = sum of v_j over constant gates with the value 1 (gates with empty support, evaluated at 0). Step i -> i+1: for each entry (sigma, s) and bit x in {0,1}, let sigma' = (sigma shifted left, x) truncated to w bits, and s' = s + sum over j with b_j = i+1 of v_j [W_j . sigma'_restricted >= t_j]. So its value is a function of sigma', and the transition is exact. Induction on i gives: D_i(sigma, s) = #{prefixes x_1..x_i : window = sigma, partial sum = s}. Gates with b_j > i are not yet added and read nothing outside the window at their later time, so no information needed later is discarded. Output: sum of D_n(sigma, s) over s >= T. RUNNING TIME: at most 2^w states per s-value, and s ranges over an interval of length at most V+1, so each table has at most 2^w (V+1) entries. Per step, each entry is processed for two bits, and the gates with b_j = i+1 are evaluated once each in O(w). Total O(n 2^w (V+1) + 2^w (V+1) m w). statement: PROOF. (1) Primal graph: x and y are neighbours if they share a support. Each x has at most d(x) <= 6 neighbours (3 supports, each with at most 2 others). (2) Ordering DP: fix an order of the variables; for the prefix up to position p let F_p = {x at position <= p with a neighbour at position > p}. Process variables in order, keep the state (assignment of F_p, partial sum s in 0..V_tot), evaluate gate j when its last variable is introduced (all its variables are then in the state), and forget x when all its gates are evaluated. Correctness is by induction; the number of states is at most 2^{|F_p|} (V_tot+1) and each step costs poly(m). Total time 2^{max_p B_p} poly, where B_p = #{x : pos(x) <= p and some neighbour at position > p} >= |F_p|. (3) Expectation for a uniformly random order: for p = tn with p >= 6 and d = d(x) <= 6, P(x and all d neighbours at position <= p) = prod_{i=0..d} (p-i)/(n-i) >= ((p-d)/n)^(d+1) >= (t - 6/n)^7, so E[B_p] <= n(t - t^7) + 42 <= 0.62 n + 42, since max over t of t - t^7 is at t = 7^(-1/6) with value about 0.6197. (Positions p < 6 contribute at most 6.) (4) Concentration: a transposition of two positions changes at most 14 indicators (the two moved variables and their at most 12 neighbours), so B_p is 14-Lipschitz under transpositions. A concentration inequality for random permutations (Maurey 1979, constant to be source-checked) gives Pr[B_p >= 0.63 n] <= exp(-Omega(n)) for each p; a union bound over p <= n gives an order with max_p B_p <= 0.63 n for large n. question: Q-30b52367b6
statement: THEOREM (subclass SPLIT(b)). Let n >= 8, b >= 0 fixed, W integer m x n, t, v in Z^m, T in Z, with |W_ji| <= n^b and m <= n/(4(b+1) log2 n). Then #{x in {0,1}^n : f(x)=1} is computed exactly in time poly(n,m) * 2^(3n/4+1). PROOF. Let k = floor(n/2), s = n-k, x = (p,q) with p in {0,1}^k, q in {0,1}^s, and split W_j = (A_j, B_j). Let lo_j = sum_i min(0,B_ji) and hi_j = sum_i max(0,B_ji), so B_j.q lies in the integer interval [lo_j, hi_j] for every q. Let tau_j(p) = t_j - A_j.p and clip_j(tau) = min(max(tau, lo_j), hi_j+1). Step 1: for every integer tau and every q, [B_j.q >= tau] = [B_j.q >= clip_j(tau)]. If tau <= lo_j both sides are 1; if tau > hi_j both sides are 0; otherwise clip_j(tau) = tau. Step 2: put kappa(p) = (clip_j(tau_j(p)))_j. Then f(p,q) = F(kappa(p), q), where F(K,q) = [sum_j v_j [B_j.q >= K_j] >= T]. Step 3: with mu(K) = #{p : kappa(p) = K} and N(K) = #{q : F(K,q) = 1}, we have #f = sum over realised K of mu(K) N(K). Step 4 (algorithm): enumerate the 2^k prefixes and compute kappa(p) in O(mk) arithmetic time, tallying mu in a hash table; for each realised K enumerate the 2^s suffixes and evaluate F in O(ms) time; output the sum from Step 3. Correctness follows from Steps 1-3. Step 5 (time): the first phase costs O(2^k m k). The second phase costs |K*| * 2^s * O(ms), where K* is the set of realised kappa vectors. Each K_j lies in {lo_j, ..., hi_j+1}, a set of size hi_j - lo_j + 2 = sum_i |B_ji| + 2 <= s n^b + 2 <= n^(b+1) (using n >= 8). So |K*| <= n^((b+1)m) = 2^(m(b+1)log2 n) <= 2^(n/4) by the bound on m. Hence the total time is poly(n,m) (2^(n/2) + 2^(n/4) 2^(n/2+1)) = poly(n,m) 2^(3n/4+1). QED. SCOPE. Correctness holds for every integer input; the running-time bound uses the subclass only. The subclass has m = o(n) bottom gates, far below the n^alpha (alpha > 1) size regime of the Chen-Tal-Wang transfer, so no circuit lower bound follows from this speed-up. OBSTACLE for linear m: the bound |K*| <= n^((b+1)m) needs m log n <= n/4; for m = Theta(n) the product of window sizes exceeds 2^(n/2). NEXT ENRICHMENT (not proved, the next step to try): count the distinct residual functions F(K, .) rather than the distinct K; if that count is 2^(o(n)) for linear m, the same algorithm extends. Status: CLAIMED, not reviewed by another session. Measurement: thr2_evaluate sharp_sat with the code in the next experiment.

question: Q-30b52367b6
statement: WINDOW LEMMA (exact-window interval class C(n,k,D)). Input: W in Z^{m x n}, |W_ji|<=B, v_j in [-V,V], thresholds t_j, T. Class: there is an unknown column order pi* such that for each row j the nonzero columns of W_j are EXACTLY a block of k consecutive positions of pi*, and at most D rows share the same block. Claims: (a) Every ordering sigma under which every row's support is consecutive (C1P) satisfies nu(sigma) <= Dk, where nu(sigma) = max_p #{j : p in span_sigma(j)}. Proof: span = support = an interval of length k; the intervals of length k containing p are exactly k (left end in [p-k+1,p]); each exact interval has at most D rows. (b) A C1P ordering is found in time linear in the matrix size by a PQ-tree (Booth-Lueker); pi* is one such ordering. (c) For any ordering sigma, the DP over positions computes #{x: sum_j v_j [W_j.x>=t_j] >= T} exactly (induction on p: a gate is decided at its last support position; state = (sum of v over decided gates, partial sums of open gates)). (d) An open gate's partial sum lies in [-Bk,Bk], so the number of states at p is <= (2Vm+1)(2Bk+1)^{nu(sigma)} <= (2Vm+1)(2Bk+1)^{Dk}. With m <= Dn and k <= c n/(D log2 n), c<1: Dk log2(2Bk+1) = (c+o(1)) n, so the count is computed in time poly(n) 2^{(c+o(1)) n} on C(n,k,D). This is a speed-up over 2^n for windows of length Theta(n/log n). Gaps: (i) exact windows only (zero entries inside a window are excluded); (ii) the multiplicity D is essential, since without it nu can be m; (iii) (c) and (d) need an independent review; (e) the claim is not a speed-up for general THR o THR.

question: Q-30b52367b6
statement: LEMMA-TOPFANIN (bookkeeping, not progress under the owner criterion; CLAIMED, unreviewed): for a THR o THR function f(x) = [sum_j v_j [w_j . x >= t_j] >= T] with k bottom gates, integer weights |w_ji| <= B, n variables, the exact count #f is computed by a DP over the variables in index order whose state is the vector of residuals r_j = t_j - (partial sum of gate j) after fixing x_1..x_i. question: Q-30b52367b6
statement: PROOF. Every gate is either supported in V2 (all gates with |supp| >= 2, and unary gates on V2) or a unary gate on a variable of V1; no unary gate sits on V0. A unary gate on i equals b0 + (b1 - b0) x_i with b1 - b0 in {-1,0,1}, so the top sum equals S(y) + c + sum_i a_i z_i, where y is the V2 part and z the V1 part of x. The indicator of f therefore depends only on (y,z), and the V0 bits are free, which gives the displayed formula. Algorithm: precompute once the sorted subset-sum lists of the two halves of V1 (2^{|V1|/2} entries each, O(2^{|V1|/2} poly) time). For each y (2^{|V2|} values), compute S(y) in poly(n,m) time and count pairs (l, r) with l + r >= theta(y) by a two-pointer pass over the sorted lists in O(2^{|V1|/2}) time. Total time poly(n,m) * 2^{|V2| + |V1|/2} = poly(n,m) * 2^{n - |V0| - |V1|/2}. Correctness holds for all integer weights because the formula is exact. Measured: thr2_evaluate cm-dfa09e24096b46f8 (70 tests, public, held-out and adversarial, wrong = []), with speedup below 1 for n <= 16.

question: Q-30b52367b6
statement: Bandwidth DP for THR o THR #SAT. Setting: variables 1..n in a FIXED order that is part of the input. Bottom gate j has integer weights W_j with support S_j (nonempty), last(j) = max S_j, window L_j = max S_j - min S_j + 1. Top gate: integer v_j, integer T, f(x) = [sum_j v_j [W_j.x >= t_j] >= T]. Let l = max_j L_j and V = sum_j |v_j|. Claim: #f = #{x in {0,1}^n : f(x)=1} is computed exactly in time O(n^2 m 2^(l-1) (2V+1)). Proof: process i = 1..n. Frontier F_i = {u <= i : u in S_j for some j with last(j) > i}. Claim |F_i| <= l-1. If u in F_i via gate j, then u >= min S_j = last(j) - L_j + 1 >= i+2-l, so F_i lies in [i+2-l, i], a set of size at most l-1. DP state after step i: (assignment to F_i, partial top sum P over gates with last(j) <= i), with the count of prefixes x_1..x_i producing it. Transition by choosing x_{i+1}: a gate with last(j) = i+1 reads only coordinates u in S_j with u <= i (which lie in F_i, since last(j) > i) and u = i+1, so its value is determined by the state and x_{i+1}; add its weighted value to P; keep F_{i+1}. Final answer = sum of counts over states with P >= T. Number of states at most 2^(l-1) (2V+1), since P lies in [-V, V]. Correctness follows by induction on i.

question: Q-30b52367b6
statement: SUB-V2 (exact algorithm and running time, for all integer THR o THR). Let f(x) = [sum_j v_j [W_j.x >= t_j] >= T] with m gates over n variables, all |W_ji|, |t_j|, |v_j| <= B. Let V2 = union of supp(j) over gates with |supp(j)| >= 2, and l = |V2|. Let V1 = (union of supp(j) over unary gates) minus V2, k = |V1|, V0 = [n] minus (V1 union V2). Algorithm: (a) for each unary gate on i in V1 set a_i += v_j (b1_j - b0_j), c += v_j b0_j, where b0_j = [0 >= t_j], b1_j = [W_ji >= t_j]; (b) let A be the remaining gates; for each y in {0,1}^{V2} compute S(y) = sum over A of v_j [W_j.y >= t_j] (A-gates have support inside V2, see the identity); (c) compute the distribution of sum_i a_i z_i over z in {0,1}^{V1} by an integer DP of range at most 4nmB+1; (d) output 2^{|V0|} * sum_y #{z : sum a_i z_i >= T - c - S(y)}. Correctness: the identity of S0007 (SURVIVED_REVIEW). Time: O(2^l (mn + n^2 m B)) arithmetic operations plus O(nmB) precomputation. Consequence (SUBCLASS C_delta): instances with |V2| <= (1-delta) n, any m = poly(n), weights bounded by poly(n), are counted in time 2^{(1-delta) n} poly(n,m,B) with NO variable ordering needed (V2 is computed directly). Exact for all instances: general time 2^{|V2|} poly <= 2^n poly. Scope: this is a constant-base saving on a subclass, not 2^n / n^{omega(1)}, and it does not close G0001 in general (the general class can have V2 = [n]). Open for the next step: a subclass where |V2| is small but m is n^alpha and the supports are unbounded in count, or an enrichment where the 2^{l} enumeration is replaced by a DP over the V2 supports (pathwidth of the V2 gate hypergraph, G0002). Authored by R1075; not reviewed by its author.

question: Q-30b52367b6
statement: LEMMA-RO (random-order frontier DP, Las Vegas). Setting: fixed integers c,k >= 1; D = c(k-1); THR o THR circuit f = [sum_j v_j g_j >= T] with bottom gates g_j = [sum_{i in S_j} w_{ji} x_i >= t_j], |S_j| <= k, each variable in at most c supports S_j, |v_j|, |w_{ji}| at most V(n) polynomial, any number m of gates. Let beta_D = (D/(D+1)) (D+1)^{-1/D} < 1. Claim: for every eps > 0 there is a Las Vegas algorithm computing #f exactly with expected time poly(n,m,V) 2^{(beta_D+eps) n}. Proof: (1) Fix an ordering pi of variables, pos(i) its position. Gate j completes at ct_j = max pos over S_j. K_t = {i : pos(i) <= t and some gate containing i completes after t}. A DP over x restricted to K_t plus the partial sum (range at most 2mV+1 values) is exact, because variables outside K_t are no longer read by any unfinished gate. State count at most 2^{|K_t|}(2mV+1). (2) i is in K_t iff pos(i) <= t and some u in N(i) has pos(u) > t, where N(i) is the union of S_j minus i over gates containing i; |N(i)| <= D. With s = |N(i)|+1 <= D+1 and tau = t/n: P(i in K_t) = P(pos(i) <= t) - P(all of {i} union N(i) in the prefix) <= tau - C(t,s)/C(n,s) <= tau - tau^{D+1} + O(D^2/n). Maximising over tau gives E|K_t| <= beta_D n + O(D^2). (3) A transposition of two positions changes the membership of at most 2(D+1) variables, so |K_t| is 2(D+1)-Lipschitz for transpositions. A Maurey/McDiarmid-type bound for uniform permutations gives deviation eps n with probability 1 - exp(-Omega(eps^2 n / D^2)); a union bound over t <= n gives, for large n, max_t |K_t| <= (beta_D+eps) n + O(D^2) with probability at least 1/2. (4) Algorithm: sample pi, compute max_t |K_t| exactly (poly time), accept if below the threshold, otherwise resample. Expected at most 2 trials; then run the DP. The output is exact; only the running time is random. Consequence: for fixed c,k, the subclass admits a counting algorithm with running time 2^{(beta_D+eps) n} poly(n,m,V), which is a strict 2^{(1-delta)n} saving with delta = 1 - beta_D - eps > 0 for any number of gates m, including m = n^alpha. The non-literal part has at most cn/2 gates by LEMMA-OVL.

question: Q-30b52367b6
statement: S0040 (CLAIMED, unreviewed). Setting: f(x) = #{x in {0,1}^n : sum_j v_j [<w_{idx(j)}, x> >= t_j] >= T} for m bottom gates whose weight vectors take at most d distinct values w^(1..d) in Z^n with |w^(k)_i| <= B; t_j, v_j, T arbitrary integers. Claim: f is computed exactly in O(n (2Bn+1)^d (m d + 1)) arithmetic operations. Proof: DP over prefixes. For level i let z_k = <w^(k)_{<=i}, x_{<=i}> for k = 1..d; the state is z in Z^d. Since |z_k| <= B i <= Bn, there are at most (2Bn+1)^d states per level. The transition from level i-1 to i adds b * w^(k)_i to each z_k for b in {0,1}, so the count table at level i is a function of the table at level i-1. Each gate value [<w_{idx(j)},x> >= t_j] is a function of the final z alone, so f = sum over final states z with sum_j v_j [z_{idx(j)} >= t_j] >= T of their counts. Correctness is by induction on i. Scope: polynomial time when d is constant and B is polynomial in n. GAP: this does not close G0001. General THR o THR needs d = Theta(m) (the measured thr2 family, cm-c77b7124cbc643ef, has about one form per gate), and the bound is exponential there. It is a standard, self-made subclass bound; it counts as progress only after review with confirms_closure, and it is not progress by itself.

statement: Proof: let z=(x,y), z'=(x',y') be nonzero with disjoint supports. (1) A nonzero vertex block x_v has support of size >=2, since its coordinates sum to 0 over GF(3). statement: Lemma R (range, c >= 1 fixed, beta > 0 fixed). There is n0(beta, c) such that for all n >= n0: 2^(beta n) / (c n) >= n. Proof. (i) For n >= 16, log2 n <= sqrt(n): the function h(n) = sqrt(n) - log2 n has h(16) = 0 and h'(n) = 1/(2 sqrt n) - 1/(n ln 2) >= 0 for n >= 9 (since sqrt n >= 2/ln 2 there), so h >= 0 on [16, inf). The left side is linear in n and the right side is o(n), so the set of failing n is finite; let n0(beta, c) be one more than its largest element (and at least 16). Then Lemma R holds for all n >= n0. question: Q-5f55fb62c2
statement:
LEMMA (all-bases lower bound, direct proof from owner's LOWER_BOUND_PROOF.md steps i-iv):

For every finite simple graph G = (V,E) and every basis B = {b_1,...,b_d} of the homogeneous GF(3) kernel K_G of the clause-sum system of the positive 1-in-3 encoding F(G) (vertex equations sum_c z(v,c)=0 for all v; edge equations z(u,c)+z(w,c)+z(e,c)=0 for all e={u,w} and c in {0,1,2}), the coefficient graph H_B defined on vertex set [d] with adjacency i~j iff there exists z in K_G such that b_i(z) != 0 and b_j(z) != 0 satisfies

tw(H_B) >= 2 * tw(G) + 1.

PROOF:

Notation. For v in V, c in {0,1,2}, let I contain coordinates (v,c) and (e,c). For a basis vector b_j in GF(3)^I, let supp(b_j) = {i in I : b_j(i) != 0}. For v in V, define S_v = {j in [d] : exists c in {0,1,2} with b_j(v,c) != 0}. For e={u,w} in E, define S_e = {j in [d] : exists c in {0,1,2} with b_j(e,c) != 0}. Note S_e = S_u union S_v because every basis vector satisfies b_j(e,c) = -b_j(u,c) - b_j(w,c) for all c.

Step (i) [Vertex and edge cliques]. For any v in V, the restriction of K_G to coordinates (v,0),(v,1),(v,2) is the 2-dimensional subspace T = {(x,y,z) in GF(3)^3 : x+y+z=0}. Every nonzero vector in T has support size 2 or 3. Any two 2-subsets of {0,1,2} intersect. Hence for any two distinct j,k in S_v, there exists a vector in K_G with both coordinates nonzero, so j~k in H_B. Thus S_v is a clique. For any edge e={u,w}, S_e = S_u union S_v. Since S_u and S_v are cliques and every basis vector with nonzero on u or v also has nonzero on e (by the edge equation), every pair of vertices in S_u union S_v is adjacent in H_B. Thus S_u union S_v is a clique.

Step (ii) [Projection dimension]. Let X subseteq V. Consider the projection pi_X: GF(3)^I -> GF(3)^{X x {0,1,2}} onto the vertex coordinates of X. The kernel of pi_X restricted to K_G is exactly the subspace of vectors supported on E and V\X. The image pi_X(K_G) is isomorphic to the direct sum over v in X of the subspace T_v = {(x,y,z) : x+y+z=0} (because the edge equations only couple different vertices and impose no condition on the sum over X). Hence dim pi_X(K_G) = 2|X|. Since B is a basis of K_G, the matrix of B has rank 2|X| on these coordinates, so at least 2|X| basis vectors have nonzero projection. Therefore |union_{v in X} S_v| >= 2|X|.

Step (iii) [Lifting tree decompositions]. Let (T, beta) be a tree decomposition of H_B of width w (so |beta(t)| <= w+1 for all t). For each t in V(T), define beta_G(t) = {v in V : S_v subseteq beta(t)}. We claim (T, beta_G) is a tree decomposition of G.
- Vertex coverage: For any v in V, S_v is a clique (Step i), so all vertices of S_v appear together in some bag of (T, beta). Thus v in beta_G(t) for that t.
- Edge coverage: For any edge e={u,w}, S_u union S_v is a clique (Step i), so there is a bag containing all of S_u union S_v, hence both u and w are in beta_G(t) for that t.
- Connectedness: For any v in V, the set {t : v in beta_G(t)} = {t : S_v subseteq beta(t)} = intersection_{j in S_v}

statement:

For every finite simple graph G = (V,E), there exists a basis B of the homogeneous GF(3) kernel K_G of the clause-sum system of the positive 1-in-3 encoding F(G) such that the coefficient graph H_B satisfies

tw(H_B) <= 2 * tw(G) + 1.

PROOF:

Construction. Define the map phi: (V × {0,1} → GF(3)) → GF(3)^I by
  xval(a,u,0) = a(u,0)
  xval(a,u,1) = a(u,1)
  xval(a,u,2) = -a(u,0) - a(u,1)  for u ∈ V
  phi(a)(e,c) = -xval(a,u,c) - xval(a,w,c)  for e = {u,w} ∈ E, c ∈ {0,1,2}
where I = (V × {0,1,2}) ⊔ (E × {0,1,2}) is the coordinate set of K_G.

Claim 1: phi maps into K_G. Vertex equation: sum_c xval(a,u,c) = a(u,0) + a(u,1) + (-a(u,0)-a(u,1)) = 0. Edge equation: xval(a,u,c) + xval(a,w,c) + phi(a)(e,c) = xval(a,u,c) + xval(a,w,c) + (-xval(a,u,c)-xval(a,w,c)) = 0.

Claim 2: phi is linear and injective. If phi(a) = 0 then a(u,0)=a(u,1)=0 for all u, so a=0. Domain dimension = 2|V|. K_G has dimension 2|V| (projection onto vertex coordinates is an isomorphism onto ⊕_v {(x,y,z): x+y+z=0} ≅ GF(3)^{2|V|}). Hence phi is a linear isomorphism onto K_G.

Claim 3: The basis B = {phi(e_{u,c}) : u ∈ V, c ∈ {0,1}} (where e_{u,c} is the standard basis) has coefficient graph H_B isomorphic to the lexicographic product G[K_2]. Vertex set of H_B is V × {0,1}. Two vertices (u,c) and (v,d) are adjacent in H_B iff there exists z ∈ K_G with phi^{-1}(z)(u,c) ≠ 0 and phi^{-1}(z)(v,d) ≠ 0. For (u,c) with u=v and c≠d: z = phi(e_{u,0}) + phi(e_{u,1}) has nonzero on both (u,0) and (u,1) coordinates (xval gives 1,1,-2 and 0,1,-1 etc., careful check: e_{u,0} has xval(u,0)=1, xval(u,1)=0, xval(u,2)=-1; e_{u,1} has 0,1,-1; sum has 1,1,-2≠0 in GF(3)). For u≠v: if {u,v} ∈ E then phi(e_{u,c}) has nonzero on e-coordinates for all c, so (u,c) ~ (v,d) for all c,d. If {u,v} ∉ E, their supports are disjoint. Thus adjacency is exactly: (u,c) ~ (v,d) iff u=v and c≠d, or {u,v} ∈ E. This is G[K_2].

Claim 4: tw(G[K_2]) = 2 tw(G) + 1. Given tree decomposition (T, β) of G of width k = tw(G), define β'(t) = { (u,c) : u ∈ β(t), c ∈ {0,1} } ∪ { extra vertex for each edge? No, the lexicographic product blow-up: standard construction gives width 2k+1. Formal: the bags β'(t) = β(t) × {0,1} cover all vertices, and for each edge {u,v} in G, all four pairs (u,c),(v,d) appear together in β'(t) for any t containing {u,v}. The width is 2(k+1)-1 = 2k+1. Tightness: a bramble of order k+1 in G lifts to a bramble of order 2k+2 in G[K_2] by taking X × {0,1}. Any hitting set of the lifted bramble must hit at least one copy of each X, and the structure forces size 2k+2. Hence tw(G[K_2]) = 2 tw(G) + 1.

Thus tw(H_B) = tw(G[K_2]) = 2 tw(G) + 1, so tw(H_B) ≤ 2 tw(G) + 1 holds (with equality).

statement: PROOF. (i) The functions x -> mon_S(G(x)), |S| <= d, are N_d(m) vectors in the GF(2)-space of all functions {0,1}^n -> GF(2), which has dimension 2^n. Since N_d(m) > 2^n they are linearly dependent, so some nonzero coefficient vector (c_S) gives P = sum c_S mon_S with P(G(x)) = 0 for all x. P is nonzero as a multilinear polynomial because distinct multilinear monomials are distinct functions on {0,1}^m. (ii) Choose S with c_S = 1 inclusion-minimal. Then P(1_S) = sum_{T subset S} c_T = c_S = 1, since no proper T subset S has c_T = 1. So y = 1_S satisfies P(y) = 1 and P(G(x)) = 0 for all x, hence y not in Im(G). Cost: Gaussian elimination on a 2^n x N_d(m) GF(2) matrix, i.e. O(2^n N_d(m)^2) bit operations. (iii) Efficiency caveat: this costs 2^n times a polynomial, which is the same order as enumerating the inputs, so it gives no saving over brute force by itself.

statement:
REPAIR LEMMA (class match for MMW19 Thm 1.3):

DEFINITIONS:

Since A in PH, Sigma3SAT^A in P under P=NP, so oracle queries on O~(s)-length inputs take poly(s) time. statement: Lemma (Speed-up via residual-state pruning): Let C be a THR o THR circuit on n Boolean inputs with m = ceil(n^alpha) bottom threshold gates. Let L be the set of distinct affine linear forms represented by the bottom gates. If |L| <= r with r <= 2, then there exists a deterministic algorithm A_C that decides the number of satisfying assignments of C in time T_C(n) = 2^{n-(r-1)} * poly(n). Proof: 1. Residual state: For an assignment x define sigma(x) = {(Delta_i, w_i) | i=1..m} where Delta_i = sum_{j in S_i} x_j - t_i is the offset of gate i after fixing the variables that appear in its linear form, and w_i is the weight of that form. Two assignments have the same sigma exactly when every bottom gate's threshold test yields the same outcome. 2. Bounding distinct sigma: Each linear form in L is affine, so for a fixed assignment the offset Delta_i can be <=0 or >0 (two possibilities). Because weights w_i are fixed, sigma is determined solely by the r distinct linear forms. Hence |sigma({0,1}^n)| <= 2^r. 3. Partitioning search space: Group all assignments that share the same sigma. Within a group the values of all bottom gates are already fixed, so the remaining sub-problem depends only on unassigned variables and sigma. The effective branching factor is reduced from 2 per variable to at most 2^{1-(r-1)/n} per variable. 4. Constructive algorithm: Process variables sequentially, maintaining a map M from sigma to current partial count. Initially M{sigma_0}=1. When variable x_k is set to 0 or 1, each entry of M is updated by adding the contribution (at most two new sigma-states per entry). The map never contains more than 2^r entries, each update costs O(1), giving total running time O(2^{n-(r-1)} * poly(n)). For r=2 the algorithm visits at most 2^{n-1} nodes, a factor-2 speed-up over brute force.

(a) The number of distinct patterns P(x)=(g_1(x),...,g_m(x)) over x in {0,1}^n is at most N(m,d)=sum_{i=0}^{d} C(m,i). PROOF (a): factor W=PQ with Q in R^{d x n}, so w_j.x=p_j.y with y=Qx in R^d, and Y={Qx : x in {0,1}^n} is finite. Let eps>0 be smaller than every nonzero |p_j.y-t_j| (y in Y), and put h_j(y)=p_j.y-t_j+eps. Then h_j(y) is never 0 on Y and g_j(x)=[h_j(Qx)>0]. Each pattern is the sign vector of the h_j at a point of Y, so distinct patterns lie in distinct regions of the arrangement {h_j=0} in R^d. An arrangement of m affine hyperplanes in R^d has at most sum_{i<=d} C(m,i) regions (Buck 1943; Cover 1965). (b) For d=n: N(m,n) > 2^n. PROOF (b): if m=n+1 then N=2^{n+1}-1 > 2^n since n>=1. If n+2<=m<=2n-1 then floor(m/2)<=n, and by symmetry of binomial coefficients sum_{i<=floor(m/2)} C(m,i) >= 2^{m-1} >= 2^{n+1} > 2^n. If m>=2n then N >= C(m,n)+1 >= C(2n,n)+1 > 2^n, using monotonicity of C(m,n) in m, C(2n,n)=2 (n=1), 6 (n=2), and for n>=3 C(2n,n) >= 4^n/(2n+1) >= 2^n because 2^n >= 2n+1. (c) For d<n: N(m,d) >= C(m,d) >= (m/d)^d, so N(m,d) < 2^{(1-delta)n} forces d*log2(m/d) < (1-delta)n. For m=n^{1.5} this forces d=O(n/log n), consistent with G0006. question: Q-773cf50f50
statement: Sized verifier lemma. Fix n, N=2^n, s>=1. Encode a fan-in-2 circuit C on n inputs with s gates as L = O(s log(n+s)) bits: each gate stores two operand indices in [0, n+s) plus a gate-type bit. Let V(f,y) be the circuit with inputs f in {0,1}^N and y in {0,1}^L that outputs 1 iff y is well-formed, decodes to a circuit C of size <= s on n inputs, and C(a)=f(a) for all a in {0,1}^n. Claim: V has size O(N*s*max(n,s)). Proof: (i) Well-formedness and decoding of y cost O(L log L) gates, which is negligible. (ii) For each of the N points a, evaluate C(a) with a universal evaluator. Keep a value bank of n+s wires (the n inputs, hard-wired as constants for a, plus the s gate outputs). Gate t computes its two operands by multiplexers over the n+s bank wires, costing O(n+s) gates per operand, then one gate. One point costs O(s*(n+s)) gates. (iii) Compare C(a) with f(a): O(1) per point. Total O(N*(s*(n+s)+1)) = O(N*s*max(n,s)). With n = log N and s <= (log N)^c for a fixed c >= 1, this is O(N*(log N)^{2c}) = N*(log N)^{O(1)}. Consequence: if a search circuit S of size N(log N)^k outputs encodings of size-<=s circuits, then Dec(f)=V(f,S(f)) is a decision circuit of size N(log N)^{k'} with k' = max(k,2c)+O(1). By S0002, Dec = MCSP[s] (E2 not used). Contrapositive: no size-N(log N)^{k'} circuit family for decision MCSP[(log N)^c] implies none for search-MCSP at size N(log N)^k. This is the direction the H1 transfer needs.

question: Q-7dba34f7a0
statement: PROOF of Lemma A. (1) Fredholm over GF(2): Ax=b is solvable iff there is no lambda with lambda^T A=0 and lambda^T b=1. Such a lambda is supported on S and gives sum_{i in S} lambda_i v_i = e. So S is inconsistent iff e in span(v_S). (2) Minimal inconsistent S gives a circuit C=S+e: (i) S is independent, since a nonempty R in S with sum_R v_i=0 and r in R gives v_r in span(v_{S-r}), so S-r is inconsistent, contradicting minimality. (ii) e in span(S) and S independent make C=S+e dependent. (iii) A proper subset of C is either a subset of S (independent by (i)) or U+e with U a proper subset of S. The latter is dependent iff e in span(v_U) iff U inconsistent, impossible since U is consistent by minimality. So C is a circuit containing e. (3) Conversely, let C be a circuit containing e and S=C-e. C is minimal dependent, so v_S is independent and e in span(v_S), hence S is inconsistent. If S-i were inconsistent for some i in S, then e in span(v_{S-i}) would give a dependency inside C-i, contradicting minimality of C. So S is minimal. The two directions are inverse. QED. Consequence: the affine clutter is a binary-matroid port, and the port-level elimination axiom 'for A,B in cl and f in A&B there is D in cl with D inside (A u B)-f' is NOT implied by this. Hand counterexample (binary, graphic): a multigraph with vertices x,u,v,y, edges a,c parallel between x and u, edge e=(u,v), edges b,d parallel-in-role between v and y, edge f=(y,x). The circuits C1={a,e,b,f} and C2={c,e,d,f} give A=C1-e and B=C2-e with A&B={f}, and the only cycles in (A u B) minus f avoid e, so no member of the port lies inside (A u B)-f.

statement: Let p in {2,3}, S,N >= 1, H a matrix over F_p with S rows and N columns. If N > (p-1)S, there is a nonzero k in {0,1}^N with Hk = 0 over F_p. Consequence (R1): let C_m be a LINEAR staged realization over F_p of total exact Search-MCSP^A[s] (state q_0=0, q_{t+1}=M_t q_t + z_t v_t over F_p with z_t in {0,1}, decoder D an arbitrary function of q_N). Then S(C_m) >= N/(p-1) = 2^m/(p-1). For p=3: S(C_m) >= 2^(m-1). The bound is tight for the kernel argument: for p=3 the 2S columns e_1,e_1,...,e_S,e_S admit no nonzero Boolean kernel vector.
derivation: (1) q_N = H f is linear in the input bit-vector f in {0,1}^N, with H in F_p^{S x N} (column t = (product of M after step t) v_t). (2) Chevalley-Warning: take the S polynomials g_i(x) = sum_t H[i,t] x_t^(p-1) over F_p in N variables. Each has degree p-1, total degree S(p-1) < N. The number of common zeros in F_p^N is divisible by p. x=0 is a zero, so the count is at least p >= 2, hence there is a zero x != 0. (3) k_t := x_t^(p-1) is in {0,1} and is nonzero (since x != 0), and sum_t H[i,t] k_t = g_i(x) = 0, i.e. Hk = 0. (4) Totality: f=0 is in Im_s (constant table has a size-1 circuit), so D(q_N(0)) = D(0) must be a circuit computing 0. Since q_N(k) = q_N(0), D(k) equals the same circuit C. If k is in Im_s, the correct answer for k is a circuit computing k != 0, contradicting C computing 0 on input 0 and k simultaneously; if k is not in Im_s, the correct answer is 'none', contradicting D(0) being a circuit. So no nonzero Boolean kernel vector exists, forcing N <= (p-1)S. (5) N = 2^m gives S >= 2^(m-1). Contradiction with S <= s(m)^c needs log s(m) = o(m), e.g. s polynomial. The Gamma clause is not used. Scope: linear updates (M_t, v_t fixed over F_p, z_t Boolean) and any decoder with access only to q_N; oracle gates allowed only in the decoder. Oracle gates in updates break step (1).

question: Q-85e487150a
statement:
LEMMA (Kernel counting closes collision step for linear F_2 realizations):

Let a linear F_2 staged realization (input-independent updates M_t ∈ F_2^{S×S}, v_t ∈ F_2^S, decoder D: F_2^S → {0,1}) compute the search-MCSP decision function D(x) = [x has circuit size ≤ s] on N = 2^n-bit inputs, with exact totality.

Define the cumulative column matrix C = [M_N...M_1 v_1 | ... | M_N...M_t v_t | ... | v_N] ∈ F_2^{S×N}. The final state on input z ∈ F_2^N is q(z) = C z + q_0 (q_0 fixed). The kernel K = {z : C z = 0} has size |K| = 2^{N - rank(C)} ≥ 2^{N - S}.

The set of yes-instances Y_s = {x : circuit size(x) ≤ s} satisfies |Y_s| ≤ ∑_{i=1}^s (number of circuits of size i) ≤ ∑_{i=1}^s (c i)^i ≤ s (c s)^s = 2^{O(s log s)} for some constant c.

If N - S > O(s log s) + 1, then |K| > |Y_s| + 1, so there exists nonzero k ∈ K with k ∉ Y_s (i.e., D(k) = 0). Since 0 ∈ Y_s (constant table has O(1) circuit), we have D(0) = 1 ≠ 0 = D(k). But q(0) = q_0 = q(k), so the decoder outputs the same bit on both inputs, contradiction.

Therefore any linear F_2 realization computing search-MCSP must satisfy N ≤ S + O(s log s).

For s(n) = 2^{n/log* n}, N = 2^n, this gives S ≥ 2^n - O(2^{n/log* n} · n/log* n) = 2^n - o(2^n). Hence S = Ω(N), i.e., space must be linear in input length.

This closes the quantifier gap in G0004 by exhibiting a specific no-instance k (via counting, not by construction) that must exist in the kernel whenever the space bound is sublinear.

Assumptions verified:
(i) Decoder depends only on final state (by definition of staged realization)
(ii) M_t, v_t input-independent (by definition)
(iii) Totality gives exact computation of D on all inputs (search-MCSP hypothesis)
(iv) 0 ∈ Y_s always (constant-0 table has circuit size O(1) ≤ s for all s ≥ 1)

This lemma is RESTRICTED to linear F_2 updates (R1 class). It does not apply to affine (shifted) updates or nonlinear gates.

statement:
step: Let N = 2^m, let Y be a nonempty fixed subset of F_2^N, and let sigma(x) = Mx + c with M in F_2^{S x N}, c in F_2^S. Suppose a decoder D reads only sigma(x), outputs a circuit computing x whenever x is in Y, and outputs none whenever x is not in Y. Then S >= N. Proof: fix x in Y and k in ker M. Then sigma(x+k) = sigma(x), so D(sigma(x+k)) = D(sigma(x)) = C, where C is not none and computes x. Since D outputs none on non-members, x+k is in Y. Then D's answer C must compute x+k as well; since C computes x, we get x+k = x, so k = 0. Hence ker M = {0}, rank M = N, and S >= N. Tightness: M = I, c = 0. statement: Lemma: For all real c ≥ 1, η ∈ [0,1), k ≥ 0, and β ∈ (0,1], the inequality (2+β-η)/(1+c) > 1+kβ holds iff 3-η > (1+k)(1+c). Proof: The expression is linear in β. For fixed c,η,k, define f(β) = (2+β-η)/(1+c) - (1+kβ). Then f(β) = (1-c-η)/(1+c) + β(1/(1+c) - k). Since c ≥ 1 and η ≥ 0, 1-c-η ≤ 0, so f(0+) ≤ 0. The inequality f(β) > 0 can only hold if the coefficient of β is positive, i.e., 1/(1+c) > k, and f(1) > 0. f(1) = (3-η)/(1+c) - (1+k) = (3-η - (1+k)(1+c))/(1+c). Since 1+c > 0, f(1) > 0 iff 3-η > (1+k)(1+c). If 1/(1+c) ≤ k, then f is non-increasing and f(β) ≤ f(0+) ≤ 0 for all β ∈ (0,1], so the inequality never holds; in this case 3-η ≤ 3 ≤ (1+k)(1+c) since k ≥ 1/(1+c) implies (1+k)(1+c) ≥ (1+1/(1+c))(1+c) = 2+c ≥ 3. Thus the equivalence holds exactly as stated.

statement: Let G be a connected graph, c: V -> {0,1} with sum_v c(v) odd, and Tseitin(G,c) the GF(2) CNF on edge variables that contains, for each vertex v, every clause excluding one parity-violating assignment of the edges at v. Corollary: for K_n with c(0)=1 and c(v)=0 otherwise (n odd-sum parity fixed), every refutation has width >= n-1, so refutation width is unbounded in n for this encoding.
derivation: Let x = 0. For a vertex v with c(v)=0, the parity of x at v is even, so no clause of v's parity-violating family is falsified by x: every such clause is satisfied by x. For a vertex v with c(v)=1 and deg(v)=d, x has even parity at v, so the single clause of v's family that excludes x|_{edges at v} is falsified by x; that clause has width d. Let w < min{deg(v): c(v)=1}. Then every initial clause of width <= w is satisfied by x (clauses of charge-0 vertices by the parity argument, and charge-1 clauses have width >= min deg > w so they are absent). Resolution is sound: if C and D are satisfied by a fixed assignment x, every resolvent of C and D is satisfied by x. Hence every clause derivable with width <= w is satisfied by x, and the empty clause, which x does not satisfy, is not derivable. So no refutation of width <= w exists, i.e. every refutation has a clause of width >= min odd-charge degree. Check on bowtie (deg 4 at vertex 0): width >= 4 (matches measured minimal width 4 in cm-5e55529b375c468f, so tw+1 = 3 is refuted for this encoding). statement: LEMMA (M-free rank bound on bottom patterns). Let W in Q^{m x n} have rank r, t in Q^m, and P(W,t) = {(1[W_j.x >= t_j])_{j<=m} : x in {0,1}^n}. Then |P(W,t)| <= min(2^n, sum_{i=0}^{r} C(m,i)). PROOF. Factor W = U V with U in Q^{m x r}, V in Q^{r x n} (rank r). Put z = Vx. Then W_j.x = U_j.z, so the pattern is a function of z in the finite set Z = {Vx : x in {0,1}^n} subset of Q^r. Let D = {U_j.z - t_j : j, z in Z} and delta = min{|d| : d in D, d != 0} > 0 (finite set of rationals; if D = {0} there is no sign change to track). Choose eps in Q with 0 < eps < delta and t_j - eps not equal to U_j.z for all j and z in Z (finitely many exclusions). For z in Z: 1[U_j.z >= t_j] = 1[U_j.z > t_j - eps], because U_j.z >= t_j implies U_j.z > t_j - eps, and U_j.z < t_j implies U_j.z <= t_j - delta < t_j - eps. The hyperplanes H_j = {z : U_j.z = t_j - eps} avoid Z, so each z in Z lies in an open cell of the arrangement {H_j} in R^r, and the pattern is determined by that cell. Distinct patterns come from distinct cells. Rows U_j = 0 give constant sign and define no hyperplane; dropping them leaves m' <= m hyperplanes. A central fact (Buck 1943; Zaslavsky 1975): an arrangement of m' affine hyperplanes in R^r has at most sum_{i<=r} C(m',i) <= sum_{i<=r} C(m,i) cells. Hence |P| <= sum_{i<=r} C(m,i). Also |P| <= 2^n trivially. QED. COROLLARY: sum_{i<=r} C(m,i) <= (m+1)^r = 2^{r log2(m+1)}, so for m = n^alpha and r(alpha log2 n + 1) <= (1-eps) n the number of bottom patterns is at most 2^{(1-eps)n}, for every weight size M.

statement: LEMMA D1 (exact linear prefix-state limit). Claim (a): A x = A y iff A t = 0 with t = x - y in {-1,0,1}^p. question: Q-9f2f8a51ac
statement: L4 (stream order, exact, bookkeeping). Let C be a fan-in-2 circuit with s gates, and let pi list its gates once each. Consider the one-pass rule: on arrival, compute the gate from its two inputs read from value memory, with s value bits and no other state. This rule computes C correctly in s steps if and only if pi is a topological order of the gate DAG. Proof: if pi is topological, induction on position shows every arriving gate's inputs are already stored, so each value is correct and exactly s steps are used. If pi is not topological, some gate g arrives before one of its gate inputs h; when g arrives the slot of h is still empty, so the rule reads an undefined value. Status: CLAIMED, needs independent review. This is bookkeeping and closes no obligation.

question: Q-9f2f8a51ac
statement: L5 (arbitrary labelling, exact bookkeeping). Let C be an acyclic fan-in-2 circuit with s gates, labelled in any order. Rule: at each step, among the gates not yet computed whose gate inputs are all computed (inputs of the circuit count as computed), compute the one with the smallest label. Claim: the rule is never stuck, performs exactly s steps, and every computed value equals C at that gate. Proof: let D(g) be the longest path from an input to g, so D(g) is at least 1 for gates and every gate input of g has smaller D. Suppose some gate is uncomputed at a point where the rule is stuck, and pick an uncomputed gate g of minimum D. Its gate inputs have smaller D, so they are computed, so g is ready, a contradiction. Hence the rule runs until all s gates are computed. Each step evaluates one gate whose inputs already hold correct values, so each value is correct by induction on the step count. Status: CLAIMED, needs independent review. Bookkeeping: it closes no obligation and does not by itself settle K9-D4.

At step t the rule tests each not-yet-computed gate at most once, and at most s gates exist, so at most s tests per step. Summing over s steps gives at most s^2 tests. Each test reads at most two input slots, giving at most 2 s^2 reads. Status: CLAIMED, needs independent review.

question: Q-9f2f8a51ac
statement: LEMMA (store-then-run one-pass rule, CLAIMED). Model: a fan-in-2 circuit C with s gates is presented as a stream of s records (g, op_g, in_g1, in_g2), in an arbitrary order (a permutation of gate labels), each record read once; inputs x are available by random access. Algorithm: (1) during the single pass, write each record into a table T indexed by g; each record costs O(1) update; (2) after the pass, run the L3 worklist on T with no further reads of the stream. Claim: the run returns val[g] = C(x)_g for every gate, performs exactly s pops and s pushes, and E <= 2s decrements, where E is the number of gate-to-gate edges. Proof: after the pass T is exactly the description of C under the relabelling g, so T is a fan-in-2 DAG description of C. L3's proof (i)-(iii) uses only that every gate-input edge is counted in ind, and that C is acyclic (so (iii) induction on a topological order exists); both hold. Hence the run is correct, with s pops and s pushes by L3. Cost: state O(s log s) bits (value bits plus indices and op codes per record); update O(1) per record; post-pass O(s + E) = O(s) operations with random access into T.

statement: For f = e_s^T M_1(x_1)...M_n(x_n) e_t over any field F, with M_i(x_i) = A_i + x_i B_i and variables read once in fixed order 1..n: the commutative image is identically zero iff the non-commutative f is zero. Proof: the non-commutative expansion is sum_S c_S w_S with w_S = prod_{i in S} x_i (increasing indices) and c_S = e_s^T Y_1...Y_n e_t, Y_i = B_i for i in S and A_i otherwise; the commutative monomials prod_{i in S} x_i are distinct for distinct S, so all c_S = 0 is equivalent to f = 0. Consequence: zero-testing a commutative fixed-order ROABP reduces to non-commutative ROABP zero-testing (Raz-Shpilka 2005, deterministic poly time).

question: Q-af2bf4a975
statement: Depth-leaf bound (restricted, shrinks G0001). Let C be a fan-in-2 DAG over inputs x_1..x_n with s gates and depth d (inputs have depth 0). Its full unfolding, the tree obtained by duplicating every shared node, is a formula F_C computing the same function, and F_C has at most 2^d leaves. Proof by induction on depth: an input has 1 = 2^0 leaf; a gate v of depth k has inputs a,b of depth at most k-1, so L(v) = L(a)+L(b) <= 2*2^(k-1) = 2^k. Corollary: if d <= c*log2(s) then |F_C| <= s^c, a fixed-exponent simulation. Scope: this is the only fixed-q case proved here; it covers depth O(log s) only and does NOT close G0001, since MMW-derived families have depth poly(s).
