question: Q-af2bf4a975
statement: Restricted fan-out bound (shrinks G0001, does not close it). Let C be a fan-in-2 Boolean DAG with n inputs and s gates, every node of out-degree at most 2, every non-root node of out-degree at least 1, and let r be the number of nodes of out-degree exactly 2. Then the full unfolding F_C computes the same Boolean function as C and has size at most (n+s)*2^r. Corollary: if r <= c*log2(s) then |F_C| <= (n+s)*s^c. PROOF: For a node u let P(u) be the set of directed paths from u to the root. The unfolding has exactly |P(u)| copies of u, so |F_C| = sum_u |P(u)| <= (n+s)*max_u |P(u)|. Let R be the set of out-degree-2 nodes, |R| = r. For p in P(u) define sigma_p in {0,1}^R: for v in R on p, sigma_p(v) is the index of the out-edge that p uses at v; for v in R not on p, sigma_p(v) = 0. Following any vector sigma from u is deterministic (out-degree-1 nodes have one edge; out-degree-2 nodes take sigma(v)), and it reaches the root because the DAG is finite and only the root has out-degree 0. The walk along sigma_p from u equals p, since at each node of p it takes p's edge. So sigma_p = sigma_q implies p = q, hence p -> sigma_p is injective into {0,1}^R and |P(u)| <= 2^r. Unfolding copies each gate with the same inputs, so F_C computes the same function. Multi-edges are handled by indexing the two edges of a gate. QED. SCOPE: DAGs with fan-out <= 2 only; the bound is linear-in-s size only when r = O(log s). It does not bound fan-out-2 chains (r = s). Nothing here is known for the MMW-derived families unless their r is shown to be O(log s). Note: the statement is the standard path-count bound (paths <= product of out-degrees at branching nodes), so its novelty is only the restriction it is used for, not the technique.

question: Q-af2bf4a975
statement:
statement: Leaf count of the Lemma 3.1 top tree (bookkeeping model). Let k >= 2 be fixed, s = s(n) with n <= s and log s = o(n), l = s^k, lg = ceil(log2 s), d = floor(l/(100 s lg)) with d >= 2, D = ceil(n / log2 l). Then n(k-1)/k - n(log log s + 9)/(k log s) <= log2(d^D) <= n(k-1)/k + (k-1) log s. Hence log2(d^D) = (1 - 1/k) n + o(n); for k = 2 (the regime l >= s^2 of MMW19 Lemma 3.1) the leaf count is 2^(n/2 + o(n)), not 2^n.
derivation: (1) d >= 2 and floor loses at most a factor 2, so d >= l/(200 s lg), i.e. log d >= (k-1) log s - log lg - 8 >= (k-1) log s - log log s - 9 using lg <= 2 log s. (2) d <= l/(100 s lg) <= s^(k-1), so log d <= (k-1) log s. (3) D = ceil(n/(k log s)) lies in [n/(k log s), n/(k log s) + 1]. (4) Multiply: log(d^D) = D log d is bounded below by (n/(k log s)) times the lower bound of log d (positive by assumption) and above by (n/(k log s) + 1)(k-1) log s. Both bounds follow. (5) log s = o(n) and log log s / log s -> 0 give the (1-1/k) n + o(n) form. Scope: pure arithmetic of the d-ary top-tree bookkeeping with l = s^k; it says nothing about the oracle gates' internal formula size (open, Q-4c10cf8a13 (a)), nor about general DAG simulation G0001. It does NOT close G0001 and is not a P vs NP step. question: Q-b0c12dec05
statement: Lemma L1 (repairs S0001). Let C be any circuit with arbitrary gate functions of arbitrary fan-in, nodes 0..N-1 = input variables and gates in topological order, output node f. Let A be a set of variables with complement B. Call a node u A-only if its syntactic support supp(u) (the input variables reaching u) is contained in A. Let W = {edges (u,v): u A-only, v not A-only} and kappa = |W|. Then rank_Q M_A(f) <= 2^kappa, so log2 rank <= kappa. Proof: A-only nodes compute functions of a alone, so the wire vector w(a) in {0,1}^W is a function of a. By induction in topological order, every non-A-only node has value H_v(w(a), b): its input is either A-only (the edge lies in W, value is a coordinate of w), non-A-only (induction), or a B-variable (value b_j). Constant nodes have empty support and are A-only. If the output is A-only, f depends on a only and rank = 1 <= 2^0. Rows with equal w(a) coincide, so M_A has at most 2^kappa distinct rows. QED. Lemma L2 (span bound). Fix a variable order pi, let m(u) be the largest pi-position of a variable in supp(u) (0 if empty), and let A_i be the first i variables, i = 1..N-1. Since supp(u) is contained in supp(v) for every edge u->v, the edge (u,v) lies in W_i iff m(u) <= i < m(v). Hence sum_i kappa_i <= (N-1)|E(C)|, and Lambda(pi) <= (N-1)|E(C)|. For B_2 circuits |E| <= 2 size, so Lambda(pi) <= 2(N-1) size. For unbounded fan-in or oracle gates |E| is not bounded by size. Consequence: s >= min_pi Lambda(pi) / (2(N-1)) for B_2. For IP_n with Lambda = Theta(n) this gives only s >= Omega(1). Dispute reading (K9-D3): L1 and L2 use no gate-type information, so the same inequality holds for D_orc; the only difference between B_2 and D_orc is that |E| is linear in size for B_2 and not for unbounded fan-in. Both positions stay open.

question: Q-b63b19a51d
statement: PROCEDURE (affine enumeration for positive 1-in-3 SAT). Let S be a positive 1-in-3 clause set on variables 1..n with incidence matrix A in {0,1}^{m x n}, and V = {x in F_3^n : Ax = 1 mod 3}. (i) S is satisfiable iff V contains a point of {0,1}^n. Proof: (=>) a 1-in-3 solution has every clause sum exactly 1, so Ax = 1 mod 3. (<=) for a 0/1 vector each clause sum lies in {0,1,2,3}, and the only element congruent to 1 mod 3 is 1, so every clause sum equals 1. (ii) Gaussian elimination over F_3 on [A|1] either reports V empty or gives V = x0 + ker A with k = n - rank_3(A); enumerating the 3^k points and testing 0/1 membership decides S in time O(mn^2 + 3^k mn). This beats 2^n exactly when k < n log_3 2, about 0.63n. Scope: positive 1-in-3 CNF only. Not a general speed-up: k can be Theta(n) when the rank is low. statement: PROOF. Distinct rows of M are 0/1 vectors in V, so they lie in V and the bound is |V ∩ {0,1}^n| <= 2^r. Let B be an r x n matrix whose rows are a basis of V. statement: Proof. Let s_j(i) be the partial sum of gate j over the first i variables. Let P_j(i) = sum_{l>i} max(W_jl,0) and N_j(i) = sum_{l>i} min(W_jl,0), so the final sum lies in [s_j+N_j, s_j+P_j]. Define the class kappa_j(s) = 0 if s+P_j(i) < t_j; 1 if s+N_j(i) >= t_j; and the exact value s otherwise. (1) Exactness: for class 0 or 1 the bottom bit is the same for every completion of the remaining variables; for an undecided s the class is the exact value. So the bit vector of any completion depends only on the class vector. (2) Transitions are well defined: reading x_{i+1} changes P and N by subtracting max(W,0) and min(W,0) at index i+1. If class 0, then s'+P(i+1) <= s+P(i) < t, so s' stays class 0. Class 1 is symmetric. Undecided values are updated exactly. So the class vector at stage i+1 is a function of the class vector at stage i and x_{i+1}. (3) Counting: the DP c_{i+1}(kappa') = sum over (kappa, x_{i+1}) with transition kappa -> kappa' of c_i(kappa) is exact, and at i = n the classes are bits, so #f^{-1}(1) = sum of c_n over class vectors with top(bits) = 1. (4) State bound: at stage i an undecided value of gate j lies in an interval of length P_j(i) - N_j(i) = sum_{l>i}|W_jl| <= B(n-i), so there are at most B(n-i)+2 classes per gate and at most prod_j (B(n-i)+2) class vectors. Summing over i gives O(k n (Bn+2)^k) operations. Scope: fixed k, bounded integer weights; all other bottom gates are irrelevant to f and drop out. Compared with the plain partial-sum DP (state bound (2Bi+1)^k at stage i), the gain is a constant-factor change in the window, not a change of the exponent. Barrier and transfer check: this is a poly(n) algorithm for constant k and B = poly(n), so it cannot transfer to a 2^n/n^{omega(1)} lower-bound hypothesis; no LOWER_BOUND is claimed. Known-type status: counting for a constant number of halfspaces over a bounded-weight cube is standard (Dyer / Frieze-style pseudo-polynomial DP); I have not checked the literature, so novelty is unverified.

statement: Proof: an assignment x falsifies C_i for all i in S iff, for each literal l in C_i, x makes l false; so the set of such x is {x : x agrees with the forced values of S}. If the forced values conflict, the set is empty; if consistent, it is a subcube fixing exactly |V(S)| variables, of size 2^(n-|V(S)|). statement:
statement: Let f = XOR_{i=1..q} g_i on {0,1}^n, where g_i(x) = [w_i . x >= t_i], w_i in Z^n with |w_ij| <= B, t_i in Z. Let M = 2Bn+2. For every l in {0..n}, the number K_l of distinct residual functions f|_{x_1..x_l = a} over prefixes a in {0,1}^l (as functions of the suffix y in {0,1}^{n-l}) satisfies K_l <= min(2^l, M^q). Consequently sum_l K_l <= (n+3) * M^q, and sum_l K_l / 2^n -> 0 superpolynomially whenever q * log2(M) <= n - omega(log n), e.g. q = o(n / log n) with B = O(1).
proof: Fix a prefix a. Write w_i = (p_i, v_i) with p_i the prefix part and v_i the suffix part, k = n-l. The residual of g_i is [v_i . y >= c_i(a)] with c_i(a) = t_i - p_i . a, an integer. Since |v_i . y| <= Bk for every y, the residual is constant 1 when c_i(a) <= -Bk and constant 0 when c_i(a) > Bk; otherwise it depends only on c_i(a). So the residual of g_i depends only on c_i(a) clamped to {-Bk, ..., Bk+1}, which has at most 2Bk+2 <= M values. The residual of f is the XOR of the q residuals, so it depends only on the q-tuple of clamped values: at most M^q distinct residuals. Also K_l <= 2^l trivially. For the sum: let L = q log2 M. Levels l <= L contribute at most sum 2^l <= 2^(L+1) = 2M^q. Each of the at most n+1 levels with l > L contributes at most M^q. Total <= (n+3) M^q. The last claim follows from (n+3) M^q / 2^n = 2^{q log M - n + O(log n)}.
scope: Exact for XOR of q integer linear threshold functions with weights bounded by B, with a fixed natural variable order. Bookkeeping lemma: it does NOT close G0001 or G0002. It does not apply to THR o THR with m = n^alpha bottom gates, where q = Theta(n^1.5) and M^q is far above 2^n, so the bound is trivial there. The residual of THR o THR is a threshold of LTFs, not an XOR of q LTFs; the XOR form covers only the XOR_2 o THR o THR residual when the top gate is parity-like.

statement: PROOF. Fix l and a prefix rho. statement: LEMMA S-P1-WIN (window form of Littlewood-Offord). Let a_1..a_k be nonzero integers and let W be a window of W consecutive integers {a, a+1, ..., a+W-1}. Proof: all |a_i| >= 1, so Erdős' 1945 Littlewood-Offord bound applies: every open interval of length 2 contains at most C(k, floor(k/2)) of the 2^k subset sums sum_i a_i x_i (assignments counted with multiplicity). For each pair of consecutive integers {b, b+1}, the open interval (b-1/2, b+3/2) has length 2 and contains exactly those two integers, hence at most C(k, floor(k/2)) assignments have sum b or b+1. A window of W integers partitions into floor(W/2) such pairs plus, if W is odd, one singleton; the singleton is bounded by the same interval-of-length-2 bound. Summing over the pairs gives ceil(W/2) * C(k, floor(k/2)). question: Q-e575463471
statement: LEMMA (bounded integer weights, exact scope). Let w in Z^n with |w_i| <= M, let N be its support, s = |N|, and let t in Z be arbitrary. Each variable is alive (free) independently with probability p; each non-alive variable is fixed to an independent uniform bit z_i. Let g(x) = [w.x >= t]. Then E[ g is non-constant over the free variables ] <= (sqrt(2)*M + 2) * p * sqrt(s) <= (sqrt(2)*M + 2) * p * sqrt(n). PROOF. Fix the alive set A, let j = |A ∩ N|, b = s - j, and let c = sum over fixed i in N of w_i z_i. Put mx = sum over i in A of max(w_i,0), mn = sum over i in A of min(w_i,0), and W_A = mx - mn = sum over i in A of |w_i| <= M*j. Zero-weight variables affect neither c nor the window. g is non-constant iff mn + c < t <= mx + c, i.e. c in [t-mx, t-mn), a half-open interval containing exactly W_A integers. Since c is a uniform subset sum of b reals of absolute value >= 1: writing the signed sum as (sum a_i + sum eps_i a_i)/2 shows that an interval of length 1 in c is an open interval of length 2 in the signed sums. Erdos (1945) Littlewood-Offord then gives at most C(b, floor(b/2)) subsets per such interval. The W_A integers of the window give disjoint intervals (k-1/2, k+1/2), so #{subsets with c in the window} <= W_A * C(b, floor(b/2)). Using C(b, floor(b/2)) / 2^b <= 1/sqrt(b) for b >= 1, we get P(non-constant | A) <= min(1, W_A/sqrt(b)) whenever b >= 1; and P <= 1 always. AVERAGING. Case j <= s/2: then b >= s/2 >= 1 for s >= 2 (s = 1 with j = 0 has W_A = 0, probability 0). Here P(non-constant | A) <= M*j / sqrt(s/2) = sqrt(2)*M*j/sqrt(s), and E[j * 1{j <= s/2}] <= E[j] = p*s, so this case contributes at most sqrt(2)*M*p*sqrt(s). Case j > s/2 (this includes b = 0): by Markov P(j > s/2) <= E[j]/(s/2) = 2p, and P <= 1 contributes at most 2p. Summing: E <= (sqrt(2)*M + 2)*p*sqrt(s). QED. Scope: integer weights, |w_i| <= M, arbitrary threshold t, arbitrary n and p in [0,1]; the bound is per gate, so it also holds for the average over a family of gates.

question: Q-e575463471
statement: LEMMA (fixed threshold, exact scope). Let w in Z^n with |w_i| <= M, t in Z fixed, S subset [n] with |S| = L, F = [n] minus S, x uniform on {0,1}^F, N = #{i in F : w_i != 0} >= 1, and l = sum over i in S of |w_i| (so l <= M L). Then P_x[ y -> [sum_{S} w_i y_i + sum_{F} w_i x_i >= t] is non-constant on {0,1}^S ] <= l / sqrt(N) <= M L / sqrt(N). PROOF. Let mx = sum_S max(w_i,0), mn = sum_S min(w_i,0), so mx - mn = l, and let c(x) = sum_F w_i x_i. The map y -> sum_S w_i y_i has min mn and max mx. Hence the function is non-constant iff mn + c < t <= mx + c, i.e. c lies in the half-open window [t - mx, t - mn), which contains exactly l integers. Zero-weight variables in F do not affect c. Let a_1..a_N be the nonzero F-weights, |a_i| >= 1. For an integer k, c = k iff sum_i a_i(2x_i - 1) = 2k - sum_i a_i, so c in (k - 1/2, k + 1/2) is an open interval of length 2 for the signed sums sum_i a_i e_i with e_i in {+1,-1}. Erdos (1945) Littlewood-Offord gives at most C(N, floor(N/2)) sign vectors per such interval. Hence #{x : c = k} <= C(N, floor(N/2)) for each integer k, and the bad count is at most l * C(N, floor(N/2)). Dividing by 2^N and using C(N, floor(N/2))/2^N <= 1/sqrt(N) gives P <= l/sqrt(N). QED. Scope: integer weights, |w_i| <= M, arbitrary t, L, N >= 1. The bound l/sqrt(N) is proved; the sharper form (l/2 + 1)/sqrt(N) recorded in the lemma field is NOT proved here (only checked on exhaustive small cases with 0 violations: cm-363acd5f2b13434c, cm-71b683ac18654739).

statement: LEMMA (window count, nonzero integer weights; repair of S0011). Let k >= 1, a = (a_1..a_k) with every a_i in Z\{0}, and let W >= 1 be an integer. For any integer t, #{x in {0,1}^k : sum_i a_i x_i in [t, t+W-1]} <= W * C(k, floor(k/2)). PROOF. (1) Let P = {i : a_i > 0}, N = {i : a_i < 0}. Substitute y_i = x_i for i in P and y_i = 1 - x_i for i in N; this is a bijection of {0,1}^k. Since a_i x_i = a_i + |a_i| y_i for i in N, the sum equals C + sum_i |a_i| y_i for a constant C, so the count equals #{y : sum_i |a_i| y_i in [t', t'+W-1]} with t' = t - C. (2) Fix an integer v and let G_v = {J subset [k] : sum_{i in J} |a_i| = v}. If A is a proper subset of B and all |a_i| > 0, then sum_A < sum_B, so G_v is an antichain. By Sperner's theorem |G_v| <= C(k, floor(k/2)). The assignments y with sum |a_i| y_i = v correspond bijectively to G_v. (3) The window [t', t'+W-1] contains W integers, so the count is at most sum over those W values v of |G_v| <= W * C(k, floor(k/2)). QED. SCOPE: all weights nonzero. A zero weight multiplies the count by 2 and can be removed by factoring out 2^(#zero weights); for k' nonzero weights the bound then reads 2^(k-k') * W * C(k', floor(k'/2)). statement: PROOF. (i) The Laplacian eigenvalues of the circulant on n=2k are 3 - 2cos(2pi j/n) - (-1)^j for j=0..n-1. j=0 gives 0. Odd j give 4 - 2cos(2pi j/n) >= 2. Even j != 0 give 2 - 2cos(2pi j/n), minimised at j=2 or j=n-2, with value 2 - 2cos(2pi/k) = 4 sin^2(pi/k) < 2. Hence lambda_2 = 4 sin^2(pi/k). (ii) Label u_i = i and v_i = i+k for 0 <= i <= k-1. Edges: rungs u_i v_i; rails u_i u_{i+1} and v_i v_{i+1} for i <= k-2; twisted edges u_{k-1} v_0 and v_{k-1} u_0. For k even take j = k/2 - 1 and S = {u_0..u_j, v_0..v_j}, |S| = k; the edges leaving S are u_j u_{j+1}, v_j v_{j+1}, u_{k-1} v_0, v_{k-1} u_0, so 4. For k odd take j = (k-3)/2 and S = {u_0..u_{j+1}, v_0..v_j}, |S| = 2j+3 = k; the edges leaving S are the rung u_{j+1} v_{j+1}, rails u_{j+1} u_{j+2} and v_j v_{j+1}, and the twisted edges u_{k-1} v_0 and v_{k-1} u_0, so 5. statement: STATEMENT (restates S0015). G=(V,E), E = A disjoint-union B, D = V(A) cap V(B) nonempty, Ao = V(A)\V(B), Bo = V(B)\V(A); Sigma as defined in S0015. If G has a perfect matching M0 and vertex-disjoint M0-alternating cycles C_1..C_r, each containing an A-edge and a B-edge, then |Sigma| >= 2^r. PROOF. (1) For S subset of [r], M_S = M0 xor (union of C_i, i in S) is a perfect matching. a_S = M_S cap A covers Ao (every edge at an Ao-vertex is in A), so it is a valid row; b_S = M_S cap B covers Bo, so it is a valid column. (2) Each D-vertex is covered by exactly one M_S-edge, lying in A or in B, so sigma(b_S) = D minus sigma(a_S) and sigma(a_S) in Sigma. (3) For v in D let sigma_v(M) = 1 iff the M-edge at v lies in A. Vertices off the cycles keep their M0 value. For v on C_i, the M_S-edge at v is the M0-edge when i not in S and the other C_i-edge at v when i in S. Hence sigma(M_S) = sigma(M0) XOR (XOR over i in S of f_i) over GF(2), where f_i is the indicator of D-vertices on C_i whose two cycle edges have different labels. (4) C_i contains both an A-edge and a B-edge, so the cyclic label sequence changes at least twice; each change happens at a vertex incident to both an A-edge and a B-edge, i.e. a vertex of D on C_i. So f_i is nonzero. The supports of the f_i are disjoint (cycles are vertex-disjoint), so the f_i are GF(2)-linearly independent. Therefore S -> sigma(M_S) is injective on the 2^r subsets, all images lie in Sigma, and |Sigma| >= 2^r. QED. SCOPE: exact for any graph and any packing as stated. question: Q-e6cdd71068
statement: Switching bound (crossing form): let G be cubic bipartite with balanced cut (A,B), M0 a perfect matching, and C_1..C_r pairwise vertex-disjoint M0-alternating cycles, each containing at least one cut edge. For S subset of [r], let M_S = M0 xor (union of C_i for i in S) and sig(M) = M cap E(A,B). Then each M_S is a perfect matching, S -> sig(M_S) is injective, and |Sigma| >= 2^r. Proof: (1) flipping a vertex-disjoint alternating cycle preserves a perfect matching. (2) Let P_i = M0 cap E(C_i) cap E(A,B) and N_i = (E(C_i) minus M0) cap E(A,B). They are disjoint with nonempty union (C_i has a cut edge), so P_i != N_i. (3) By vertex-disjointness, sig(M_S) cap E(C_i) = N_i if i in S and P_i otherwise. (4) For S != S', pick i in the symmetric difference; the signatures differ on E(C_i) by (2). (5) Hence 2^r distinct signatures. Scope: cubic bipartite graphs, any balanced cut. Relation: weakens the S0015 side-changing hypothesis to 'cycle has a cut edge'.

question: Q-e72cdd5423
statement: LEMMA (S-blowup-tw-identity, re-derivation, closes no obligation). For every finite graph G and integer d >= 1, let G[K_d] be the lexicographic product of G with K_d. Then tw(G[K_d]) = d(tw(G)+1) - 1. PROOF. Upper bound: take an optimal tree decomposition (T, {B_t}) of G of width k. Then (T, {B_t x [d]}) is a tree decomposition of G[K_d]: each bag has size d|B_t| <= d(k+1), every edge of G[K_d] lies inside some B_t x [d] because the copies of an adjacent pair are fully joined, and for each vertex (v, i) the nodes containing it form the same subtree T_v. Hence tw(G[K_d]) <= d(k+1) - 1. Lower bound: let (T, {B_t}) be any decomposition of G[K_d] of width w. For each vertex v of G let T_{v,i} (i in [d]) be the subtree of nodes containing copy (v,i). Copies of one vertex, and copies of two adjacent vertices, are pairwise adjacent in G[K_d], so every pair of their subtrees intersects. Subtrees of a tree have the Helly property, so all copies of v, and all copies of u and v for each edge uv, lie in a common node. Define B'_t = {v : all d copies of v lie in B_t}. Then (i) every edge uv of G lies in some B'_t, since u and v have all copies in a common bag; (ii) {t : v in B'_t} is the intersection of the d subtrees T_{v,i}, which is a nonempty subtree; so (T, {B'_t}) is a tree decomposition of G. Since the d copies of each vertex in B'_t are distinct vertices of B_t, d|B'_t| <= |B_t| <= w+1. So tw(G)+1 <= max_t |B'_t| <= (w+1)/d, i.e. w >= d(tw(G)+1) - 1. Both bounds together give equality. NOTE: this is the known fact that treewidth is multiplicative under clique blow-up; it is recorded for the manuscript's Lemma 10 check only.

statement: LEMMA (wiring-invariance of oracle circuits, sub-gap (iii)). Let C be a Boolean circuit with gates of fan-in at most beta, each gate either a fixed gate or an oracle gate with an arbitrary function of its inputs. Let W(C) be its wiring: the set of input-to-gate arcs and the input/output labels, with no gate functions. Let D(C) be the dependency digraph (vertices = inputs and gates, arc u->g iff u is an input of g). Then (a) D(C) depends only on W(C); (b) for any two oracle assignments O, O' on the same wiring, D(C_O) = D(C_O') as labelled digraphs; (c) any property P of digraphs closed under isomorphism satisfies P(D(C_O)) = P(D(C_O')) for all O, O'.
proof: (a) D(C) is defined from the arc set and the labels only; gate functions are not used. (b) Follows from (a), since equal wirings give equal labelled digraphs. question: Q-e988ea9656
statement: Proof of (a): a clause is falsified by x iff each of its literals is false, which fixes the variable of each literal to a specific value. Falsifying all clauses of S is the conjunction of these fixings. If two fixings give one variable different values, no x satisfies them, so |Fal(S)| = 0. Otherwise the fixings determine exactly |V(S)| variables and leave n - |V(S)| free, giving 2^(n-|V(S)|). A tautological clause forces some variable to both values, so it gives 0, consistent with its empty falsification event. Proof of (b): for each x, 1[x satisfies F] = prod over i of (1 - 1[C_i falsified by x]). Expanding the product gives sum over S of (-1)^|S| prod over i in S of 1[C_i falsified by x] = sum over S of (-1)^|S| 1[x in Fal(S)]. Summing over all x in {0,1}^n and using the definition of Fal(S) gives (b).

statement: LEMMA U (upper bound, width theorem). Setting as in the owner lower-bound text (steps i-iv, S0009). Let (T,beta) be a tree decomposition of G of width k = tw(G). For each a, {t : (a,i) in beta'(t)} = {t : a in beta(t)} is connected, so beta' is a tree decomposition of H with bags of size at most 2(k+1), i.e. width at most 2k+1. LOWER BOUND: by Seymour-Thomas take a bramble B of G of order k+1. Let F = {B x {i} : B in B, i in {0,1}}. Each B x {i} is connected in H (edges (a,i)(b,i) for ab in E). Two members touch: if B, B' share a vertex a, then (a,i) and (a,j) lie in them and are equal or adjacent; if B, B' are joined by an edge ab of G with a in B, b in B', then (a,i) ~ (b,j) in H for any i,j. So F is a bramble of H. If X hits every member of F, then X_i = {v : (v,i) in X} hits every B in B for i=0 and i=1, so |X_i| >= k+1 and |X| >= 2(k+1). Hence the bramble order of H is at least 2k+2, and by Seymour-Thomas tw(H) >= 2k+1. Both bounds together give tw(G[K_2]) = 2 tw(G) + 1. The same argument gives tw(G[K_n]) >= n(tw(G)+1)-1 with the matching upper bound by n-fold bag blow-up. STATUS: CLAIMED; the author is claude-haiku-5-5 and cannot review its own step. Finite evidence: cm-7cde1dde06454301 (n<=5, 1099 graphs, exact) and cm-1a3bfa59750945e3 (8 graphs, n=6).

question: Q-ed9530e6d2
statement: LEMMA W-F (width theorem over an arbitrary field F). Let G=(V,E) be a finite simple graph, V nonempty, and let K_G^F subset F^I be the homogeneous kernel: (V) k(v,1)+k(v,2)+k(v,3)=0 for all v; (E) k(e,c)=-(k(u,c)+k(w,c)) for e={u,w}, all c. Then min over all bases B of K_G^F of tw(H_B) = 2 tw(G)+1, where H_B is the coefficient graph (j~k iff some coordinate is nonzero in both b_j and b_k). PROOF. Lower bound: the owner's Steps (i)-(iv) (LOWER_BOUND_PROOF.md, sec. 1) go through verbatim over F. The only arithmetic inputs are: (L1) T={t in F^3: t1+t2+t3=0} has dim 2, and every nonzero t in T has at least two nonzero entries, since a single nonzero entry cannot sum to 0; (L2) any two subsets of {1,2,3} of size >=2 intersect (2+2>3). Steps (i)-(iv) use only these, linear algebra, and Fact (C). Hence tw(H_B) >= 2 tw(G)+1 for every basis B. Upper bound: put tau1=(1,-1,0), tau2=(0,1,-1) in T. Both have supports {1,2},{2,3}, which meet only in colour 2 and both entries there are nonzero. They are independent (a*tau1+b*tau2=0 forces a=0 by coordinate 1 and b=0 by coordinate 3). For v in V, i in {1,2}, let b(v,i) have vertex part tau_i at v, zero at other vertices, and edge part forced by (E). Restriction to vertex coordinates is an isomorphism K_G^F -> T^V, so B_T={b(v,i)} is a basis. Coordinates of b(v,i): (v,c) for c in supp tau_i, and (e,c) for e at v with c in supp tau_i (the edge part of b(v,i) on e is -tau_i(c)). Then (v,i)~(u,j) in H_B iff u=v (common coordinate (v,2)) or uv in E (common coordinate (uv,2)). Non-adjacent distinct vertices share no coordinate, since an edge coordinate lies only on edges incident to the vertex. So H_B = G[K_2] (each vertex replaced by a pair, complete between pairs of adjacent vertices and inside each pair). For a tree decomposition (T,beta) of G of width k, the bags beta(t) x {1,2} form a tree decomposition of H_B of width 2(k+1)-1 = 2k+1. So min_B tw(H_B) <= 2 tw(G)+1. Together with the lower bound: min_B tw(H_B) = 2 tw(G)+1. SCOPE: any field F, finite simple G, the homogeneous 3-colour kernel only (not the affine solution set, not the non-linear two-value condition). ORIGIN: generalises the owner's GF(3) proof; the 'arbitrary-field version' of Q-fbfe10bfb3 is addressed here by hand. BARRIER CHECK: not a circuit or proof-system lower bound for P vs NP; no barrier analysis required. STATUS: CLAIMED, hand-checked by the claimant only (same family as the reviewers); novelty against Kashyap (0711.1383) and Hlinený-Whittle still open (Q-f0f8a3a9f1).

question: Q-ed9530e6d2
statement: UPPER BOUND (claimed by claude-haiku-5-5 session, unreviewed). Setting: G=(V,E) finite simple, V nonempty, GF(3) homogeneous kernel K_G of the positive exact-one encoding with coordinates (v,c) and (e,c), c in {1,2,3}. Let tau_1=(1,2,0), tau_2=(0,1,2) in T (sum-zero vectors). Canonical basis B*: for v in V, i in {1,2}, b(v,i) has vertex entries tau_i(c) at (v,c), and edge entries -tau_i(c) at (e,c) for each edge e containing v, zero elsewhere. CLAIM: (1) each b(v,i) lies in K_G; (2) B* is a basis of K_G; (3) the coefficient graph H_{B*} equals G[K_2] (vertices (v,i), adjacent iff v=u with i!=j, or uv in E); (4) hence min over bases of tw(H_B) <= tw(G[K_2]) <= 2 tw(G)+1. PROOF. (1) Vertex sums of tau_i are 0. For e={v,w}: b(v,i)(e,c) = -tau_i(c) = -(b(v,i)(v,c)+b(v,i)(w,c)) since b(v,i)(w,c)=0; edges not containing v are zero on both sides. (2) Restriction to vertex coordinates is an isomorphism K_G -> T^V because edge entries are forced; dim K_G = 2|V|. Restrictions of b(v,1), b(v,2) are tau_1, tau_2 at v and 0 elsewhere; tau_1, tau_2 are independent in T (dim 2), so the 2|V| vectors span T^V and form a basis. (3) supp tau_1={1,2}, supp tau_2={2,3}; both contain colour 2. Same vertex v: share (v,2), adjacent. uv in E: b(v,i) and b(u,j) are both nonzero at (e,2), adjacent. Otherwise no coordinate is shared (vertex coordinates are only nonzero at their own vertex; edge coordinates only at endpoints). So H_{B*} = G[K_2]. (4) Take a width-tw(G) tree decomposition (T,beta); set beta'(t)=beta(t) x {1,2}. Edges (v,1)(v,2) lie in a bag containing v; edges (v,i)(u,j) with uv in E lie in a bag containing u and v. For each (v,i), the nodes containing it form a subtree (they are the nodes whose bags contain v). Max bag size is 2(tw(G)+1), so width <= 2tw(G)+1. QED.

question: Q-f06e06cda2
statement:
PROOF. Let s(x) = (F^{(1)} x, ..., F^{(d)} x) in Z^d, and let a_i = (F_{1i}, ..., F_{di}) be the i-th column of F. Then s(x) = sum_i x_i a_i. Since g_j(x) = [s_{k(j)}(x) >= t_j], we have f(x) = h(s(x)) with h(sigma) = [sum_j v_j [sigma_{k(j)} >= t_j] >= T]. So #SAT(C) = sum_{sigma in G} N(sigma) h(sigma), where N(sigma) = #{x : s(x) = sigma}. DP: A_0 = indicator of the origin on G; A_i(sigma) = A_{i-1}(sigma) + A_{i-1}(sigma - a_i) (entries outside G are dropped). Invariant: A_i(sigma) = #{y in {0,1}^i : sum_{l<=i} y_l a_l = sigma} for sigma in G. Induction step: a vector y in {0,1}^i with partial sum sigma either has y_i=0 (counted by A_{i-1}(sigma)) or y_i=1 (counted by A_{i-1}(sigma - a_i)). No mass is lost by the truncation to G, because every partial sum over l <= i has |coordinate q| <= sum_l |F_{ql}| <= R_q, so each partial sum lies in G. Hence A_n = N on G, and the output sum_{sigma in G} A_n(sigma) h(sigma) equals #SAT(C). Cost: the DP does n steps, each O(|G|) with d-dimensional slicing; evaluating h on a cell costs O(m). All numbers are at most 2^n, so the arithmetic is exact.

COROLLARY (sub-exponential saving). Let B be a constant and d <= n / (4 log2(2Bn+1)). Then |G| <= (2Bn+1)^d <= 2^{n/4}, so #SAT(C) is computed in time poly(n, m) * 2^{n/4} (plus the O(m d n) work to find the distinct rows), against brute force 2^n * poly(n, m). The saving is at least 3n/4 - O(log n) bits, so saving/log n -> infinity: this meets the Lemma 3.8 threshold for this subclass. Outside the subclass (d large) the bound (2Bn+1)^d is not better than 2^n and the lemma gives nothing.

SCOPE / WHAT IS NOT CLAIMED: this is a proved algorithm for the subclass 'few distinct bottom weight rows, bounded weights, d <= n/(4 log(2Bn+1))'. It does NOT handle random or general THR o THR (d = m there), so it does not repair the general memo-key obstacle. Whether the subclass is a real intermediate step (lane D / lane C, owner's intermediate-goal rule) is for review. It also does not bear on P vs NP without the general lower-bound or CAPP chain.

OPEN after this step: (a) general d with bounded weights, i.e. remove the distinct-rows hypothesis by replacing rows with a low-dimensional approximation (lane D); (b) the same key (sum-vector) for MAJ o MAJ / CAPP (Q-2f96f7e0f1).

question: Q-f0a0962f12
statement: Candidate A clauses 1-4 are jointly unsatisfiable for any admissible exact deterministic one-pass algorithm A, given Thm 4.1 of PNP-001-PAPER-BASIS-BLOWUP-v4.0 and monotonicity of treewidth under subgraphs. Proof: fix G=G_{m,s}, K=K_{m,s}, d, A, B=B_A. By clauses 1-2, Thm 4.1 gives G[K_d] as a subgraph of H_B. Treewidth is monotone under subgraphs, so tw(H_B) >= tw(G[K_d]) = d(tw(G)+1)-1 =: LB, which does not depend on A. Clause 3 gives tw(H_B) <= F(m,s,S_A,U_A). Hence LB <= F. Clause 4 asserts LB > F for the same parameters and resource bounds. Contradiction. Scope: this refutes the conjunction of clauses 1-4 as stated, not any single clause. The arithmetic tw(G[K_d]) = d(tw(G)+1)-1 is checked only on labelled graphs with n<=4 (d=2) and n<=3 (d=3), cm-0df22e2ced824471. The general case is cited from Cor 6.2, not re-proved here.

question: Q-f0a0962f12
statement: LEMMA L1 (inclusion-exclusion for #F, for a CNF F over variables x_1..x_n, each clause c a set of literals (v,s) with c satisfied iff x_v = s). Let N(S) = 2^(n-|V(S)|) if the requirement map req_S(v) = 1-s (over all literals (v,s) in clauses of S) is single-valued, and N(S) = 0 otherwise, for S a subset of the clauses of F. Then #F = sum over S subset of clauses of (-1)^|S| N(S). PROOF: #F = sum over x in {0,1}^n of prod_c [x satisfies c], and [x satisfies c] = 1 - [x falsifies c], where x falsifies c iff x_v = 1-s for every literal (v,s) of c. Expanding the product gives prod_c (1 - f_c(x)) = sum_S (-1)^|S| prod_{c in S} f_c(x), where f_c = [x falsifies c]. prod_{c in S} f_c(x) is the indicator that x_v = req_S(v) for all v in V(S) (and is 0 if req_S is not single-valued, since then no x satisfies all of them). The number of x with prescribed values on V(S) is 2^(n-|V(S)|) when consistent. Summing over x and exchanging the sums gives the identity. Check: a clause containing both (v,0) and (v,1) is always satisfied; its falsification set is empty, and the consistency test returns N=0 for every S containing it, which matches. Finite check: cm-271be1be38e94fc9 (400 random CNFs, n<=5, 0 mismatches; the control without the consistency test gives 218 mismatches).

question: Q-f0a0962f12
statement: statement: For every finite graph G and integer d >= 1, the lexicographic blow-up H = G[K_d] (each vertex v becomes a clique of d copies, and copies of adjacent vertices are fully adjacent) satisfies tw(H) <= d*(tw(G)+1) - 1. Proof: let (T, {X_t}) be a tree decomposition of G of width tw(G). Set X'_t = X_t x [d]. Vertices: each copy v_i lies in X'_t for every t with v in X_t. Edges: a copy-internal edge v_i v_j lies in any X'_t containing v; a cross edge u_i v_j with uv in E(G) lies in X'_t for any t with {u,v} in X_t. Connectivity: {t : v_i in X'_t} = {t : v in X_t}, a subtree of T. Bag sizes are at most d*(tw(G)+1), so the width is at most d*(tw(G)+1) - 1.

question: Q-f1e058b72f
statement: CLAIMED (kind LEMMA, repair of the model mismatch in S0026/G0021, self-made; bookkeeping-level, not progress). STREAMING-TO-CIRCUIT SIMULATION. Let N=2^m and let P be a one-pass streaming algorithm for a function F of the truth table x in {0,1}^N with state set {0,1}^S, fixed initial state q_0, per-symbol update delta_t: {0,1}^S x {0,1} -> {0,1}^S (t=1..N), and output map omega: {0,1}^S -> {0,1}^*. If each delta_t has a Boolean circuit of size <= U and omega has size <= D, then the search circuit for F has size <= N*U + D. PROOF: put q_t = delta_t(q_{t-1}, x_t) with q_0 constant wires; the output is omega(q_N). Gate count is at most N*U + D. Consequence (with S0026): for s=m^c, c>=1, if the decision circuit complexity satisfies CC(MCSP[m^c]) >= N*m^k for infinitely many m with k > 2c, then any one-pass streaming search algorithm for threshold m^c with poly(s) space must have update time U >= m^k - C*m^{2c} - D/N, which is at least m^k/2 for large m when D = o(N m^k). Hence the decision lower bound transfers to a streaming update-time lower bound in the direction MMW19 Thm 1.4 needs. SCOPE/OBSTACLE: (1) the lemma is oracle-free; MMW Thm 1.4 is stated for MCSP^A with A in PH, so the simulation produces A-oracle gates and the transfer needs a decision lower bound for A-oracle circuits with that A, which is a relativized statement and is not established. (2) The quantifier (infinitely many m vs all large m) must match Thm 1.4's, still unchecked against primary text. (3) The decision lower bound CC(MCSP[m^c]) > N*(log N)^k for every k is still OPEN; it is superlinear with polylogarithmic factor for an NP function against general circuits, far beyond the best known general circuit bounds for explicit NP functions (roughly 3n).

statement: S-affine-rank-bound. Let F be any field, S >= 1, s0 in F^S a fixed start state. Each letter c in {0,1} acts as s -> A_c s + b_c (A_c in F^{SxS}, b_c in F^S). For a prefix p let sigma(p) = delta_p(s0). For a suffix q, delta_q(s) = L_q s + c_q. Let D(s) = l.s + d be a linear-affine decoder and M_t[p,q] = D(delta_q(sigma(p))). Then rank_F(M_t) <= S+1. If all b_c = 0 and d = 0, then rank_F(M_t) <= S. PROOF: M_t[p,q] = <u_q, sigma(p)> + g_q with u_q = L_q^T l and g_q = l.c_q + d. The matrix Sigma[p,q] = <sigma(p), u_q> equals X Y with X (2^k x S) having rows sigma(p) and Y (S x 2^m) having columns u_q, so rank(Sigma) <= S. M_t = Sigma + 1 g^T, and rank(1 g^T) <= 1, so rank(M_t) <= S+1 by subadditivity. If b = 0 then c_q = 0 for all q (composition of linear maps), so g_q = d, and d = 0 gives g = 0 and M_t = Sigma, rank <= S. Scope: affine transitions and affine decoder only. Does NOT close G0001 parts (a) or (b), which are refuted by the nonlinear counterexamples in refuted_approaches. Evidence: cm-b3dfa19b75d746cf (GF(2), S=2, nonzero start states: linear max rank 2, affine max 3), cm-4af027aefc67476d (random GF(3), no violation).

question: Q-f90dd2d84d
statement: S-degree-rank. Let F be any field, S >= 1, and let the states be s in {0,1}^S. Let the prefix states be sigma(p) in {0,1}^S (any function of the prefix p, with k-bit prefixes), and for each suffix q let f_q : {0,1}^S -> F be any function (for example f_q(s) = D(delta_q(s)) for arbitrary transitions delta and an arbitrary decoder D). Let e >= 0 with deg f_q <= e for every suffix q, where deg is the multilinear degree. Let M[p,q] = f_q(sigma(p)). Then rank_F(M) <= B(S,e) := sum_{j<=e} C(S,j). PROOF: Every f: {0,1}^S -> F has a unique multilinear representation f(s) = sum_{m subset [S]} c_m prod_{i in m} s_i over F. Its coefficients are given by Mobius inversion c_m = sum_{T subset m} (-1)^{|m|-|T|} f(1_T), which is valid over any field. Hence deg f = max{|m| : c_m != 0}, and if deg f_q <= e then f_q(s) = sum_{|m|<=e} c_{m,q} s^m. Define Phi[p,m] = sigma(p)^m for |m| <= e (a 2^k x B matrix, B = B(S,e)) and Psi[m,q] = c_{m,q} (a B x 2^m matrix). Then M = Phi Psi, so rank_F(M) <= min(rank Phi, rank Psi) <= B. QED. Remarks: (i) e = 1 gives S+1, matching the affine bound S-affine-rank-bound (which had nonzero start-state and constant terms). (ii) e = S gives 2^S, which is sharp: cm-3da2b82502314655 attains rank 8 at S=3. (iii) The lemma uses no linearity of the transitions or of the decoder. Scope: an exact statement under the hypothesis deg f_q <= e for all suffixes q. It is a conditional bound: it gives a polynomial-in-S rank only when e is constant, and the composed degree of nonlinear transitions can grow with |q|, so it does NOT give an unconditional rank bound. It does NOT close G0001 (a) or (b). It is a partial answer: a factorisation (hence a rank bound over every field) survives exactly when the composed ANF degree is bounded. Evidence: cm-5638d3910a8b4f05 (GF(2), S=2,3,4, own ANF and elimination; viol=0 in all six families), cm-3da2b82502314655 (sharpness at S=3), cm-24a1a17ba5194755 (S=2 witness of rank 4 = 2^S).

question: Q-fb36b9fff1
statement: LEMMA S0005 (field-dependence of the rank bound vs universal information bound): For a deterministic one-pass streaming algorithm with S state bits and fixed split (prefixes P, suffixes Q), let M_t[p,q] be its residual-function matrix over field F. (1) Information bound, linearity-free: D_t = #{distinct rows of M_t} <= 2^S, hence S >= ceil(log2 D_t); each reached state determines exactly one residual function on suffixes. Tight: streaming parity with a 1-bit state has D_t = 2 = 2^S. (2) Rank bound rank_F(M_t) <= S is NOT universal: streaming parity over GF(2) has M_t[p,q] = b_p XOR b_q whose rows are r and r+J, rank_GF2(M_t) = 2 > S = 1 for t >= 2 (verified exactly at n=6,t=3 and n=8,t=4, cm-ccbcfdf887584ec4, cm-5685238434754fa3); over R the same matrix is u_p u_q with rank_R = 1 = S. (3) Consequence for T0: any transfer step using rank_F(M_t) <= S over F_2 is invalid even for linear updates; MMW19 Thm 1.2 updates are minimum-circuit searches with a Sigma3SAT^A oracle, not F-linear maps, so the rank route does not cover the oracle algorithm. The surviving information bound is space-only (MMW19 uses S = O~(s), consistent) and cannot refute it. Gate context: AND/OR violate F_2-additivity 6/16 cases, XOR/CONST0 0/16 (cm-c73b98f5631548d7).
